6.3   Consultations through FGD’s and KII’s As part of the Environmental and Social Screening (ESS) process for the proposed flood shelter construction under the RIVER Project in Bogura District, extensive community consultations were carried out following the participatory approach applied in Bogura District. These consultations were conducted through Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) and Key Informant Interviews (KIIs) across all proposed shelter sites to ensure the active involvement of local stakeholders. The FGDs included representatives from vulnerable groups such as women, landless farmers, school authorities, local elders, and people with disabilities, aiming to understand their perspectives, needs, and concerns regarding the shelter construction and associated interventions. Similarly, KIIs were held with Union Parishad members, school management committee members, teachers, and other relevant local actors to gather insights on land use, community needs, environmental sensitivities, and existing infrastructure conditions. The consultations revealed broad community support for the project, while also highlighting site-specific issues such as demolition activities, access road conditions, and the need for separate sanitation facilities for girls and women. These findings were instrumental in shaping the design and environmental and social management plans for the proposed shelters in Bogura District, ensuring that the interventions are inclusive, locally appropriate, and socially accepted. [SOURCE: Page_66]

6.4   Consultation Outcomes During the stakeholder consultation sessions held for all proposed flood shelter sites in Bogura District under the RIVER Project, several key concerns and suggestions were raised by community members, school authorities, and local representatives. The discussions mainly focused on the risks and vulnerabilities faced by local people due to inadequate shelter options during disaster periods, as well as the potential impacts of construction activities on their livelihoods and daily routines. The issues raised were largely similar across different locations, and a summary of the key concerns and suggestions is presented below:  Participants emphasized the need to construct shelters on elevated plinths to ensure they remain flood-free during peak inundation periods.  Concerns were expressed regarding access roads, particularly their elevation and durability, to ensure all-weather accessibility, especially during floods.  Community members requested separate sanitation facilities for men and women, equipped with adequate water supply and privacy arrangements.  Local residents urged that construction activities be planned in a way that avoids disruption to agricultural practices and minimizes damage to existing rural roads.  Participants suggested incorporating rainwater harvesting systems and solar lighting to enhance the environmental sustainability of the shelters.  There were calls for prioritizing local labor and locally available materials during construction to promote employment and income opportunities for the surrounding communities. [SOURCE: Page_66]

Page | 24 [SOURCE: Page_66]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_67]

   Some participants raised concerns about potential noise, dust, and traffic disturbances during construction, stressing the need for appropriate mitigation measures.    Women participants highlighted the importance of ensuring safe spaces and adequate lighting, particularly around the shelter premises.    Participants recommended involving School Management Committees (SMCs) in shelter planning, operation, and maintenance processes to ensure local ownership and effective management.    The community emphasized the need to establish and publicize a functional grievance redress mechanism (GRM) to enable affected persons to report and resolve concerns during both the construction and operational phases. [SOURCE: Page_67]

The participants were presented with feedback, suggestions, and recommendations listed below:  During the stakeholder consultation sessions, participants expressed strong support for the proposed flood shelter construction, emphasizing the urgent need for safe refuge during recurrent floods.  Community members recommended that the shelters be designed as multi-purpose facilities, serving as schools or community centers during non-flood periods to ensure year-round utility. Several participants stressed that the shelters should be constructed on elevated land or raised plinths to maintain functionality even during severe flooding events.  Female participants highlighted the importance of gender-sensitive design features, including separate sanitation facilities and private spaces for women and girls. Local farmers raised concerns about the potential loss of agricultural land, urging that shelter sites be selected in areas with minimal impact on cultivable land.  Participants also emphasized the need for adequate drainage and waste management systems around shelter sites to prevent waterlogging and associated health risks. They encouraged the engagement of local labor and skilled workers during construction to promote local employment and strengthen community ownership.  Concerns were raised regarding demolition of existing school structures at selected sites. Participants requested that such demolition be carefully managed to avoid disruptions and ensure safety. They also stressed the importance of arranging temporary learning facilities for students to minimize interruption to educational activities during the construction period.  Participants further suggested incorporating ramps, handrails, and other accessibility features to facilitate access for elderly persons and individuals with disabilities. Local Union Parishad representatives requested regular communication and participation in decision-making processes to promote transparency and coordination.  Environmental concerns—including potential noise, dust, and disturbance to local vegetation—were raised, with calls for mitigation through good site management and tree plantation around shelter premises. In addition, participants proposed providing essential emergency and safety equipment such as radios, televisions, raincoats, torches, life jackets, microphones, flags, fire extinguishers, and gumboots within the shelters. [SOURCE: Page_67]

However, there are some specific issues raised by the participants in different places, which are summarized in the following table: Page | 25 [SOURCE: Page_67]

The assessment confirmed that all selected sites are located within existing government primary school premises, where the land is owned by the Government of Bangladesh. Official land records—including khatian, mouza maps, and land use certificates—were verified in coordination with the Upazila Land Office and School Management Committees (SMCs). The findings confirmed that the lands are free from private ownership, encroachment, or third-party claims, and that no involuntary resettlement or economic displacement will occur. A total of 15 schools require demolition of existing old buildings, while 2 schools will need demolition of existing wash blocks to make space for the new shelter construction. Despite these challenges, 5 schools are ready for immediate construction without the need for demolition or major preparatory work, which are as follows:     BOG-001 Uzgram GPS (Gabtali Upazila)     BOG-002 Bhandara Ponipara GPS (Gabtali Upazila)     BOG-008 Dhananjoy GPS (Gabtali Upazila)     BOG-014 Domkandi GPS (Shariakandi Upazila)     BOG-018 Solartair GPS (Shariakandi Upazila) 7.2       Initial Environmental Impacts due to Sub-project The construction of flood shelters under the RIVER project in Bogura District is anticipated to cause a range of initial environmental impacts during the pre-construction and construction phases. Site clearing and earthworks are expected to result in temporary disturbance of the existing land surface, including minor vegetation removal and soil exposure, which may increase the risk of soil erosion and sediment runoff into nearby water bodies. Excavation and foundation works could lead to localized dust generation and noise pollution, potentially affecting nearby communities and sensitive receptors. The operation of construction machinery and transportation of materials will contribute to air emissions, including particulate matter and exhaust gases, which could temporarily degrade local air quality. Additionally, improper management of construction waste and debris might result in contamination of soil and water resources if not adequately controlled. Temporary disruption to drainage patterns and surface water flows may occur, potentially affecting local aquatic ecosystems. There is also a possibility of minor disturbances to local biodiversity due to habitat alteration. Furthermore, increased human activity at the site could lead to safety hazards and traffic congestion in adjacent areas. However, these impacts are expected to be temporary and localized, provided that appropriate mitigation measures and environmental management plans are effectively implemented throughout the project lifecycle to minimize adverse effects on the environment and the local communities. [SOURCE: Page_69]

7.2.2 Key Environmental Related Recommendations Based on the environmental screening and site observations conducted for the flood shelter construction sites under the RIVER project in Bogura District, the following key environmental recommendations are proposed to mitigate adverse impacts and ensure compliance with environmental standards throughout the project lifecycle:    Site Selection and Land Use: Ensure flood shelters are located on government-owned or institutionally recognized land to avoid encroachment on agricultural land, wetlands, or ecologically sensitive zones.    Topsoil Protection: Carefully remove, preserve, and reuse topsoil during site clearance to prevent degradation of fertile soil and ensure restoration of vegetation post- construction.    Dust and Air Pollution Control: Implement dust suppression measures such as regular water sprinkling on access roads and construction sites, especially during dry seasons.    Noise Pollution Minimization: Limit construction activities to daytime hours and maintain equipment and vehicles in good condition to reduce noise levels and community disturbance.    Surface Water and Drainage Management: Establish adequate drainage systems to prevent waterlogging and contamination of nearby ponds or irrigation channels, especially during the monsoon.    Waste Management: Segregate, store, and properly dispose of construction waste, including hazardous materials, to avoid pollution of soil and water bodies.    Sanitation and Workers' Welfare: Provide adequate sanitation facilities, safe drinking water, and proper waste disposal systems for construction workers to ensure hygienic working conditions. [SOURCE: Page_70]

    Biodiversity Protection: Avoid unnecessary tree cutting and disturbance to local flora and fauna. Replant native trees where removal is unavoidable.     Erosion Control: Use soil retention techniques such as grass turfing, slope stabilization, and boundary fencing to prevent soil erosion around shelter foundations.     Community Health and Safety: Establish fencing and signage around the construction area, and ensure regular communication with the local community to address safety concerns.     Monitoring and Supervision: Conduct regular environmental monitoring and engage a dedicated Environmental and Social Manager at the local level for timely supervision and grievance redress. These recommendations are essential for maintaining ecological balance, minimizing construction-related hazards, and ensuring the sustainability of flood shelter infrastructure in the flood-prone areas of Bogura District under the RIVER project. [SOURCE: Page_71]

7.3       Initial Social Impacts on Community due to Subproject The initial social impacts for the RIVER Project initiative in Bogura District are anticipated to be moderate and manageable with proper mitigation measures. During the early phases of construction, temporary disturbances may arise, including restricted access to educational institutions (if shelters are co-located with schools), increased noise and dust levels, and the potential disruption of local livelihoods due to movement of labor and machinery. Additionally, the influx of external laborers may create social sensitivities within the host communities, particularly relating to safety, privacy, and cultural norms. There may also be temporary traffic congestion and limited access to community spaces during material transportation and site development. However, no significant displacement or loss of private assets has been identified at the screening stage. It is critical that community engagement continues throughout the project to ensure transparency and address grievances proactively. With the adoption of an effective Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) and adherence to the World Bank’s Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), the initial social impacts can be mitigated, ensuring the project delivers long-term benefits in disaster resilience and community safety. [SOURCE: Page_71]

7.3.1 Construction Phase Related Impacts During the construction phase of the RIVER project, several social impacts on the surrounding communities are anticipated. Temporary disruption to local daily life may occur due to increased movement of construction vehicles and equipment, leading to traffic congestion, noise, and dust pollution in and around the project sites. These disturbances may affect educational institutions, religious centers, and marketplaces if located nearby. Access restrictions to community facilities or agricultural lands may also be experienced during material transport or excavation work. Labor influx, though limited, might cause concerns related to social cohesion, privacy, and safety, especially for women and children in the locality. Page | 29 [SOURCE: Page_71]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_72]

Furthermore, construction work may lead to potential conflict over land use, particularly if boundaries are not clearly demarcated or if community consultation is inadequate. There is also a risk of temporary loss of livelihood for vendors or informal workers operating near the site. To address these challenges, it is essential to implement a robust communication strategy, engage local stakeholders regularly, enforce a labor code of conduct, and ensure proper grievance redress mechanisms are in place to minimize disruptions and promote social harmony throughout the construction period. Due to construction of the Sub-project, the poor people will get safe shelter at the time of any natural disaster/cyclone. Moreover, their children will get better schooling facility, and some people will get employment. Communication facilities will be improved. There are no adverse impacts on the community as a result of the Sub-project. However, there are some marginal impacts that may occur temporarily, which need to be addressed. These will be mitigated/minimized by adopting necessary mitigation measures, as have been set forth herein. The screening and consultation with stakeholders confirmed that there is no indigenous ethnic community lives in the vicinity of Sub-project sites. Hence, the concerning Small Ethnic Community Development Plan is not triggered. [SOURCE: Page_72]

7.3.2 Engagement of the School Management Committee (SMC) The Active engagement of the School Management Committees (SMCs) has been a key component of the environmental and social screening process for the flood shelter construction under the RIVER Project in Bogura District. SMC members participated in site-specific consultations to identify environmental and social concerns, guide site selection, and promote community ownership. Their inputs on existing school conditions, safety during construction, and continuity of education were instrumental in shaping practical mitigation measures. The SMCs expressed strong support for the shelters, recognizing their dual function as educational facilities and emergency flood refuges. Their continued involvement will be vital for monitoring construction impacts, ensuring effective implementation of the Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), and maintaining transparent communication between the project team and local communities. Upon completion, the infrastructure will be handed over to the Ministry of Primary and Mass Education (MoPME) for operation and maintenance. To ensure long-term sustainability, SMCs will require capacity building in shelter maintenance, meeting management, record-keeping, climate resilience, disaster preparedness, and community engagement. The RIVER Project will support these needs through targeted training and technical assistance to enable SMCs to effectively manage and sustain the shelters post-handover. 7.3.3 Union Disaster Management Committee (UDMC) A Union Parishad is the lowest tier of the local government system in Bangladesh. In each UP, there are about 14 Standing Committees including Union Disaster Management Committee (UDMC) to take care of various activities including services before, during and post calamities at grassroots level. Unfortunately, these Committees have not been made functional and effective. The project should take steps to make the UDMC functional for ensuring better services for the people in the project locations. Page | 30 [SOURCE: Page_72]

SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL FINDINGS AS WELL AS ESMP IN GABTALI UPAZILA, BOGURA DISTRICT The Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project is being implemented by the Government of Bangladesh with financial and technical support from the World Bank to enhance disaster resilience in flood-prone regions. As part of this initiative, 12 multipurpose flood shelters are proposed for construction in Gabtali Upazila of Bogura District, one of the highly vulnerable areas located near the Jamuna River basin. These shelters are designed to serve as safe refuge centers during floods and other natural disasters, while also functioning as schools or multipurpose community facilities during normal periods. [SOURCE: Page_76]

The environmental and social screening has been carried out in compliance with the World Bank’s Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and relevant national laws and regulations of Bangladesh. This report presents the existing environmental and social baseline of Gabtali Upazila, potential impacts of the sub-projects, stakeholder feedback, and proposed management measures through an Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP). [SOURCE: Page_76]

### 1. Existing Geographical and Safeguard Context of Gabtali Upazila

Gabtali Upazila is situated in the southern part of Bogura district, characterized by fertile floodplains, river channels, and low-lying agricultural lands. The region is prone to seasonal flooding, waterlogging, and riverbank erosion, particularly due to its proximity to the Jamuna and Bangali rivers. The local economy largely depends on agriculture, fishing, small-scale trading, and remittances. However, frequent floods disrupt livelihoods, damage crops, and cause displacement of communities. [SOURCE: Page_76]

From a safeguard perspective, Gabtali has a moderate to high disaster vulnerability. Settlements are densely populated, and community infrastructure such as schools and health centers often remain under pressure during flood events. Hence, multipurpose disaster shelters have been prioritized for construction. [SOURCE: Page_76]

2. Drinking water quality status of Gabtali Upazila Groundwater is the primary source of drinking water in Gabtali, extracted mainly through shallow and deep tube wells. While water availability is generally sufficient, seasonal contamination by iron and arsenic has been reported in some unions. The depth of sub- mergeable pump or Tubewell are about 45-250 feet. Salinity is not a major issue in this area, but flooding often contaminates tube wells and surface sources with coliform bacteria, posing risks to public health. Water quality tests from Department of Public Health Engineering (DPHE) surveys indicate that groundwater in the area generally meets Bangladesh Drinking Water Standards (BDWS) for microbiological and chemical parameters. Arsenic levels are within permissible limits in most Page | 34 [SOURCE: Page_76]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_77]

tested wells. Local people usually use shallow tube-well water for drinking and other domestic purposes. Groundwater quality: pH-5.17 to 8.51, DO-2.26 to 8.14mg/l, TDS-23.40 to 320 mg/l, EC -25.7 to 681μs/cm, Fe-0.8 to 7.0 mg/l and As-0.001-0.079mg/l (DPHE Test Result, 2025) [SOURCE: Page_77]

3. Sub-Project Location and Scope A total of 12 flood shelters are proposed across eight (8) unions of Gabtali Upazila. The distribution is as Dakshinpara Union – 1 site, Durghata Union – 1 site, Mahishban Union – 2 sites, Nasipur Union – 2 sites, Nepaltali Union – 3 sites, Ramshanpur Union – 1 site, Sonarai Union – 1 site and Sukhanpukur Union – 1 site. Scope of work includes:  Demolition of old and unsafe structures on the selected sites.  Site preparation, including leveling and filling of low-lying areas.  Construction of a multi-storied reinforced concrete shelter building.  Provision of safe drinking water, sanitation facilities, solar power backup, and emergency access routes.  Landscaping and planting of flood-resistant vegetation after construction. [SOURCE: Page_77]

Stakeholder Consultation and GRC Formation Extensive consultations were held with local communities, school management committees, union parishad representatives, women’s groups, and vulnerable households to ensure inclusiveness in the planning process. The consultations highlighted the urgent need for safe flood shelters, concerns regarding possible land disputes, construction-related nuisances, and demand for employment opportunities for local workers. A Grievance Redress Committee (GRC) has been established at the Upazila level under the leadership of the Upazila Engineer (LGED), with representation from local administration, teachers, women’s representatives, and community leaders. The GRC will provide a transparent mechanism for resolving complaints related to land use, construction impacts, and labor issues. Tree Cutting                      Minimize felling of trees in site and     Implement compensatory plantation (at least 3 saplings for each tree cut). [SOURCE: Page_80]

Filling Depressions               Avoid ecologically sensitive areas;     Alternative sites should be considered to avoid ecological disruption. Construction                      Water sprinkling on dry surfaces; Management                        Covering materials during transport;     Restrict noisy activities to daytime and     Maintain equipment properly. Community                         Maintain ongoing dialogue with stakeholders; Engagement                        ensure transparency in decision-making. GRC Functionality                 Ensure the grievance mechanism remains accessible, especially for women and vulnerable groups;     Regularly monitor GRC effectiveness;     Provide training to committee members. Social Conflict                   Prioritize local workers for construction employment; Prevention                        Enforce a worker Code of Conduct (CoC). [SOURCE: Page_80]

The screening concludes that the construction of 12 flood shelters in Gabtali Upazila will generate substantial long-term social and environmental benefits by enhancing disaster resilience, protecting vulnerable populations, and supporting community development. Although some adverse environmental and social impacts such as tree cutting, land depression filling, dust, noise, and temporary livelihood disruptions are anticipated, these are localized, short-term, and manageable through proper mitigation. [SOURCE: Page_80]

Implementation of the proposed ESMP, community engagement, and grievance redress mechanism will ensure that the project remains environmentally sustainable and socially inclusive, thereby contributing to the overall resilience-building objectives of the RIVER Project in Bogura district. [SOURCE: Page_80]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_82]

LOCATION OF THE SUB-PROJECT The subproject is located in the Northern part of Gabtali Upazila in Bogura District, which is within the Rajshahi Division. The location details of the subproject have been summarized in Table 2. Table 2: Location Details of the Subproject Site District                                          :    Bogura Upazila                                           :    Gabtali Union                                             :    Dakshinpara Mouza                                             :    Uzgram Village                                           :    Uzgram GPS Location                                      :    24.988253 N; 89.428813 E Distance of the site from Upazila HQ              :    16 km Nearby Major Road:                                :    Rangpur-Bagura 6 Lane Road at West side on 07 Km [SOURCE: Page_82]

Nearby River/ Canal:                              :    Gajaria Canal (700m- East-West) [SOURCE: Page_82]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, June 2025) [SOURCE: Page_82]

The catchment area of the subproject mostly comprises of Uzgram Dakhin para, Harir vita, Para baishar, Hizli villages which have been significantly affected by floods. The floods in Bogura District are mainly caused by the overflowing of the Jamuna and its tributaries, especially the Bangali River, which passes through the region. The district’s topography consists of extensive floodplains and low-lying agricultural lands that heighten its flood vulnerability. During the monsoon season, intense rainfall and river overflow inundate large portions of the countryside, leading to waterlogging in settlements and farmland. These flood events have repeatedly disrupted road and transport systems, damaged houses, and caused severe losses to crop production, thereby significantly affecting the livelihoods and resilience of local communities. [SOURCE: Page_82]

The flood shelter will be constructed at 9 No. Uzgram Government Primary School (GPS), which is located at the Uzgram village under Dakshinpara Union of Gabtali Upazila in Bogura District. There are 10 teachers (M-03; F-07) and 513 students (Boys: 246; Girls: 267) in the school, operated by the guidance of School Management Committee (SMC) and government officials of Gabtali Upazila Education Office. The students, teachers and residents of the catchment area come to the proposed site by using the connecting/access road named Kagoil-Uzgram Road. The road is a BC road with 3.06 meters width and just passing beside the 9 No. Uzgram Government Primary School at North side. [SOURCE: Page_82]

The population of the catchment area is about 52000. People in the area are mostly dependent on shallow tubewell water for their daily uses and the average depth of water is 120 ft below the ground. The Dakshinpara Union map indicating sub-project location has been shown respectively Page | 40 [SOURCE: Page_82]

The existing 9 No. Uzgram GPS is situated on 108 decimals of land Comprises of one storied pucca building and two storied pucca school building that currently accommodate all the classrooms and administrative office rooms, located on the northern side. Accordingly, all academic and administrative activities will continue to be conducted within the current school building throughout the construction period. A Shaheed Minar is located on the western side of the school premises. There is a wash block on the north-western corner of the school building. There is a major road on the western side of the school and along with two additional roads located on the northern & eastern sides of the school premises. Some local settlements found beside the school boundary; some are on the northern side and the rest of them are to the western side. The proposed sub-project (construction of new School cum Flood shelter building) is not located within any environmentally sensitive area and will not cause any severe negative effects to the environmental settings of the area, neither to important environmental features. The disaster shelter will be constructed within an existing school boundary, so no agricultural land/ activities or fish farming will be disturbed due to the construction of the sub project. The proposed sub- project location is surrounded by several significant socio-environmental features in all directions. To the north, notable landmarks include Akdhpara Mosque located approximately 150 meters away, Gabtali Dewan Sahir Uddin Ebtadayi Madrasa at 400 meters, Gabtali Mosque at 410 meters, and Awliya Mazar at 415 meters distance. On the southern side, the area hosts Darul Hayder Hafizia Madrasa (100 meters), Begum Hasina Mohila Madrasa (980 meters), Uzgram Community Clinic (150 meters), Amena Memorial Library and Chowdhury Para Mosque (both within 100 meters), along with natural features such as Mograr Beel (500 meters) and a pond situated about 400 meters away. Additionally, Mograpara Mosque is located approximately 520 meters south of the site.To the east of the site, key community landmarks include Uzgram Baytul Siddique Central Jame Mosque (50 meters), the Eidgah ground (55 meters), Uzgram Bazar (100 meters), and the Freedom Fighters Parliament at 120 meters distance. The Uzgram Crematorium is situated around 300 meters away, while Gajaria Canal and Gajarir Beel are located at 700 and 600 meters respectively. On the west side, prominent institutions and landmarks include Uzgram Pintu Girl’s High School and a Mobile Tower, both just 5 meters away, as well as Malipara Durga Mandir and Kali Mandir at around 100 and 110 meters respectively. Further west are the Sarker Para Mosque (300 meters), Mandol Barir Mosque (500 meters), Eidgah Field (510 meters), and the natural water bodies Gajaria Canal Page | 44 [SOURCE: Page_86]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_87]

(750 meters) and Gorar Beel (600 meters). Gucchogram village lies about 1 kilometer west of the sub-project location. This diverse mix of religious, educational, health, cultural, and natural features underscores the socio-environmental importance of the area surrounding the proposed sub-project site. [SOURCE: Page_87]

No significant disturbance to all these establishments/features is anticipated due to construction activities for having sufficient distance from the construction site, and strict construction site management system- including restrictive work schedule during the daytime only, water- sprinkling twice a day in and around the site, proper fencing around the working area, safe storage of materials, etc. Construction related activities and setting up of labor camps along with associated facilities and their management issues will be accounted for impacts more likely to be generated during the pre, post and construction period. Noise pollution from pilling or drilling, air pollution caused by dust or gaseous emissions from vehicle movement, running of motorized equipment and land clearing, odors and soil pollution from leaking of latrines and fecal sludge, will more likely to take place. Soil can further be eroded and polluted from chemical spills or improper disposal of waste materials. Noise and vibration effects generated from pilling and drilling may also trigger landslides and harmful disturbances to local fauna. Impact on surface and ground water bodies might get acute due mainly to the high abstraction rate and disposal/leakage of pollutants to the surface/ground water bodies. Clearing of trees, bushes or any type of vegetation may put impact on floral species and unscrupulous clearance also trigger habitat loss. All these impacts can only be prevented or minimized by adopting measures delineated into the ESMP and good practice engineering and site management. ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SCREENING This section identifies the potential impacts that the various elements of the proposed sub- project may have on the physical, biological and socio-economic environment within half a kilometer of the radial distance around the site. Environmental and Social Assessment (ESA) based on this screening study for the Sub-project as 9 No. Uzgram Government Primary School of Gabtali Upazila under Bogura District has been conducted to identify and determine which potential project impacts may be significant and therefore require the application of reasonable and effective management and/or mitigation measures. In order to realize the exact physical, biological and socio-economic environment of the proposed sub-project site and the influence area in regards to the implementation measures, an extensive field visit was carried out on 29 June 2025 in the Sub-project area. Environmental and Social Screening form, as adopted in Annexure-2 of the Environmental and Social Management Framework of RIVER, was administered for identifying the impacts and their extents. [SOURCE: Page_87]

PUBLIC CONSULTATION AND PARTICIPATION Public participation and community consultation has been taken up as an integral part of environmental assessment process of the project. Field visit has been carried out on 29 June 2025 in and around the Sub-project component site. As part of the impact assessment, Page | 45 [SOURCE: Page_87]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_88]

participatory public consultation was conducted in that area by the field level staffs, and consultants from D&SC. Checklist of the consultation is attached in Annexure-3. The consultation meeting was attended by 28 persons (Male -22 and Female -6) and local individuals, teachers, chairman and/or member of Union Parishad and school management committee were among the attendees in that meeting. The participants were selected from different cohorts of stakeholders, and some of whom will have major active roles before, during and even after the construction works. Therefore, the meeting was organized in an informed, expressive and unbiased manner, wherefrom different views and concerns came across which will be properly taken care of during the design and construction phases. Refer to Figure 8 and Annexure-4 for selected photographs of the participatory public consultation held at site of the 9 No. Uzgram Government Primary School and list of attendees in that public consultation meeting, respectively. A questionnaire was kept ready and responses were elicited. During these consultations, the communities were explained about the project, its benefits, associated social and environmental aspects and possible mitigation measures. The participants were also informed about the project GRM (Grievance Redress Mechanism) system in detail and the disclosure of project documents in websites, and their unrestricted and uninitiated access to those system and resources. As such, public consultation is a living process as the types of problems/ difficulties, involved parties or stakeholders and mode of settlement or resolution processes are more likely to differ with time. Thus, consultation with different parties or stakeholders will be continued throughout the sub-project implementation period and records of resolutions, whatsoever and wherever possible, will be kept in writing at the site and made available on any enquiries or requests by all parties concerned. [SOURCE: Page_88]

Figure 8: Public Consultation Meeting in the Proposed Sub-project Site SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACTS Overall Construction Related Impacts: The proposed construction works are expected to generate localized and temporary environmental and social impacts typical of small- to medium- scale civil works. Key environmental impacts include dust and air emissions, noise and vibration from machinery, construction waste generation, temporary soil disturbance, and minor vegetation loss during site preparation. There may also be risks of water and soil contamination from improper material handling or drainage obstruction. Social impacts are anticipated to be limited, involving temporary disruption of school activities, restricted access to playgrounds, [SOURCE: Page_88]

Page | 46 [SOURCE: Page_88]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_89]

increased traffic movement, and potential occupational health and safety risks for workers. However, no land acquisition, displacement, or impacts on ethnic or vulnerable communities are expected. Overall, the impacts are short-term, reversible, and confined within existing school premises, manageable through standard environmental and social mitigation practices. Tree Cutting: Approximately three trees (3) are likely to be cut down and no water bodies are likely to be filled up due to the construction of the flood shelter. The ecological impact of the subproject is low. There will be temporary negative impacts on physico-chemical environment. Nevertheless, these impacts are manageable if mitigation measures are taken according to ESMP. Grass turfing: Grass turfs on embankment, slope, building compound & any critical place to enhance the ecological condition and protect the top soil. Tentative area of turf has been estimated as 240 square meters (half of total area), after discussion with architects and engineers. It is likely to be changed depending on the requirement during construction as per site design and as per direction of E.I.C. Land Ownership: Availability of adequate public land area is as important as community consent to construct the flood shelter and access roads. The D&S Survey team did not find any conflicts over the school land. The land issue has been discussed in the consultation meeting. Participants unanimously confirmed that the school has its own 108 decimals of land and there is no dispute about this land. Land Acquisition: The proposed Sub-project, 9 No. Uzgram Government Primary School, does not have any involuntary resettlement impacts due to the construction of flood shelter and approach roads as the Sub-projects will be constructed in existing Government Primary Schools’ premises. The Government Primary School has 108 decimals of land. No land acquisition will be required for the activities to be implemented under the project. Access road needs to construct or rehabilitate within its existing alignment. LOCATION OF THE SUB-PROJECT The subproject is located in the Eastern part of Gabtali Upazila in Bogura District, which is within the Rajshahi Division. The location details of the subproject have been summarized in Table 2. Table 2: Location Details of the Subproject Site District                                           :    Bogura Upazila                                            :    Gabtali Union                                              :    Durgahata Mouza                                              :    Bhandara Village                                            :    Bhandara GPS Location                                       :    24.844143 N; 89.511074 E Distance of the site from Upazila HQ               :    8km (North-West) Nearby Major Road:                                 :    Durgahata- Golabari at North side, BC road Wide-12fit [SOURCE: Page_102]

Nearby River/ Canal:                               :    Ichamoti River (1.5km-East) [SOURCE: Page_102]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, July 2025) [SOURCE: Page_102]

The catchment area of the subproject mostly comprises of Bhandara, Ponir para, Lalkha para villages which have been significantly affected by floods. The floods in Bogura District are mainly caused by the overflowing of the Jamuna and its tributaries, especially the Bangali River, which passes through the region. The district’s topography consists of extensive floodplains and low- lying agricultural lands that heighten its flood vulnerability. During the monsoon season, intense rainfall and river overflow inundate large portions of the countryside, leading to waterlogging in settlements and farmland. These flood events have repeatedly disrupted road and transport systems, damaged houses, and caused severe losses to crop production, thereby significantly affecting the livelihoods and resilience of local communities. The flood shelter will be constructed at 61 No. Bhandara Ponir para Government Primary School (GPS), which is located at the Bhandara village under Durgahata Union of Gabtali Upazila in Bogura District. There are 5 teachers (M-01; F-04) and 232 students (Boys: 103; Girls: 129) in the school, operated by the guidance of School Management Committee (SMC) and government officials of Gabtali Upazila Education Office. The students, teachers and residents of the catchment area come to the proposed site by using the connecting/access road named Golabari to Bhandara ponir para madrasha Road. The road is a HBB road with 3.04 meters width and just passing beside the 61 No. Bhandara Ponir para Primary School at East side. The population of the catchment area is about 20,000. People in the area are mostly dependent on shallow tubewell water for their daily uses and the average depth of water is 60 ft below the ground. The Durgahata Union map indicating sub-project location has been shown respectively in Figure 1. The topographical Map with indicative and tentative location of labor camp, [SOURCE: Page_102]

Figure 5: Proposed Waste Disposal Area for the Subproject Site The existing 61 No. Bhandara Ponir para GPS is situated on 100 decimals of land Comprises of two single-storied building that currently accommodate all the classrooms and administrative office rooms located on the Eastern side and a Shaheed Minar adjoining in the existing GPS. The proposed flood shelter is planned to be constructed on the western side of the school premises, with no demolition of the existing building required but it has been identified that electrical pole exist within the school premises, which need to be removed. Accordingly, all academic and administrative activities will continue to be conducted within the current school building throughout the construction period. A labor shed & a material Storage area will be constructed at the eastern side, a waste disposal area will be constructed at the north-eastern side of the compound during the construction period. There is a wash block on the southern corner of the school building. There is a major road on the northern side of the school and along another road located on the eastern sides of the school premises. Some local settlements found near the school boundary on the south-western side. The area experienced severe flooding in the year 1988, with flood waters reaching a height of 5 feet and persisting for approximately 7 days due to this flood existing school condition at that time was very rough for continuing the study. Refer to Figures 6 for photographs of current situation of the existing GPS & Figure 7 for photographs of indicating the necessity for removal of the electrical pole. [SOURCE: Page_105]

The important establishments around the subproject site have been summarized in Table-3 Table 3: Important Establishments Adjacent to the Subproject Site [SOURCE: Page_106]

Direction                      Important Establishments with Approximate Distance North side    Vandara Panirpara Playground (35m), Gorer Bari Tota Stand (585m), Lakhapara Beel (1000m) South side    Mosque (250m), Bhandara Dakhil Madrasa (319m), Bhandara Purba Para (407m), Mohorum Ajhar Mollar Graveyard (680m) East side     Graveyard (5m), Pashchim Panir para Nurani Madrasa (148m), Mosque (250m), Durgahata Baytul Salam Jame Mosque (870m) West side     Graveyard adjacent to school, Bhandara Charmatha (240m), Bhandara Somaj Unnoyon Songothon (276m), Bhandara Maddhyapara Jame Mosque (308m), Mosque (600m) (Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, July 2025) The proposed sub-project (construction of new School cum Flood shelter building) is not located within any environmentally sensitive area and will not cause any severe negative effects to the environmental settings of the area, neither to important environmental features. The disaster shelter will be constructed within an existing school boundary, so no agricultural land/ activities or fish farming will be disturbed due to the construction of the sub project. The project area is surrounded by several important landmarks and facilities in all directions, contributing to its social, educational, and religious significance. To the north, there is the Lakhapara Beel located 1000 meters away, offering a natural water feature, along with Gorer Bari Tota Stand (585m) and the nearby Vandara Panir Para Playground (35m), which serves as a recreational space for the local community. On the south side, key institutions include Bhandara Purba Para (407m), Bhandara Dakhil Madrasa (319m), a mosque (250m), and the Mohorum Ajhar Mollar Graveyard (680m), indicating the presence of both educational and religious infrastructure. The east side features Durgahata Baytul Salam Jame Mosque at 870 meters, Pashchim Panir Para Nurani Madrasa (148m), another mosque (250m), and a graveyard just 5 meters away, highlighting a concentration of religious facilities. On the west, the area is bordered by Bhandara Charmatha (240m), Bhandara Somaj Unnoyon Songothon (276m), Bhandara Maddhya Para Jame Mosque (308m), an additional mosque (600m), and a graveyard adjacent to the school, showcasing a mix of community development initiatives, places of worship, and burial grounds. Overall, the surroundings reflect a well-integrated community with access to religious, educational, and recreational amenities in every direction. No significant disturbance to all these establishments/features is anticipated due to construction activities for having sufficient distance from the construction site, and strict construction site management system- including restrictive work schedule during the daytime only, water- sprinkling twice a day in and around the site, proper fencing around the working area, safe storage of materials, etc. Construction related activities and setting up of labor camps along with associated facilities and Page | 64 [SOURCE: Page_106]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_107]

their management issues will be accounted for impacts more likely to be generated during the pre, post and construction period. Noise pollution from pilling or drilling, air pollution caused by dust or gaseous emissions from vehicle movement, running of motorized equipment and land clearing, odors and soil pollution from leaking of latrines and fecal sludge, will more likely to take place. Soil can further be eroded and polluted from chemical spills or improper disposal of waste materials. Noise and vibration effects generated from pilling and drilling may also trigger landslides and harmful disturbances to local fauna. Impact on surface and ground water bodies might get acute due mainly to the high abstraction rate and disposal/leakage of pollutants to the surface/ground water bodies. Clearing of trees, bushes or any type of vegetation may put impact on floral species and unscrupulous clearance also trigger habitat loss. All these impacts can only be prevented or minimized by adopting measures delineated into the ESMP and good practice engineering and site management. ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SCREENING This section identifies the potential impacts that the various elements of the proposed sub- project may have on the physical, biological and socio-economic environment within half a kilometer of the radial distance around the site. Environmental and Social Assessment (ESA) based on this screening study for the Sub-project as 61 No. Bhandara Ponirpara Government Primary School of Gabtali Upazila under Bogura District has been conducted to identify and determine which potential project impacts may be significant and therefore require the application of reasonable and effective management and/or mitigation measures. In order to realize the exact physical, biological and socio-economic environment of the proposed sub- project site and the influence area in regards to the implementation measures, an extensive field visit was carried out on 01 July 2025 in the Sub-project area. Environmental and Social Screening form, as adopted in Annexure-2 of the Environmental and Social Management Framework of RIVER, was administered for identifying the impacts and their extents. [SOURCE: Page_107]

PUBLIC CONSULTATION AND PARTICIPATION Public participation and community consultation has been taken up as an integral part of environmental assessment process of the project. Field visit has been carried out on 01 July 2025 in and around the Sub-project component site. As part of the impact assessment, participatory public consultation was conducted in that area by the field level staffs, and consultants from D&SC. Checklist of the consultation is attached in Annexure-3. The consultation meeting was attended by 26 persons (Male -12 and Female -14) and local individuals, teachers, chairman and/or member of Union Parishad and school management committee were among the attendees in that meeting. The participants were selected from different cohorts of stakeholders, and some of whom will have major active roles before, during and even after the construction works. Therefore, the meeting was organized in an informed, expressive and unbiased manner, wherefrom different views and concerns came across which will be properly taken care of during the design and construction phases. Refer to Figure 8 and Annexure-4 for selected photographs of the participatory public consultation held at site of the 61 No. Bhandara Ponir para Government Primary School and list of attendees in that public consultation meeting, Page | 65 [SOURCE: Page_107]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_108]

respectively. A questionnaire was kept ready and responses were elicited. During these consultations, the communities were explained about the project, its benefits, associated social and environmental aspects and possible mitigation measures. The participants were also informed about the project GRM (Grievance Redress Mechanism) system in detail and the disclosure of project documents in websites, and their unrestricted and uninitiated access to those system and resources. As such, public consultation is a living process as the types of problems/ difficulties, involved parties or stakeholders and mode of settlement or resolution processes are more likely to differ with time. Thus, consultation with different parties or stakeholders will be continued throughout the sub-project implementation period and records of resolutions, whatsoever and wherever possible, will be kept in writing at the site and made available on any enquiries or requests by all parties concerned. [SOURCE: Page_108]

Figure 8: Public Consultation Meeting in the Proposed Sub-project Site SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACTS Overall Construction Related Impacts: The proposed construction works are expected to generate localized and temporary environmental and social impacts typical of small- to medium- scale civil works. Key environmental impacts include dust and air emissions, noise and vibration from machinery, construction waste generation, temporary soil disturbance, and minor vegetation loss during site preparation. There may also be risks of water and soil contamination from improper material handling or drainage obstruction. Social impacts are anticipated to be limited, involving temporary disruption of school activities, restricted access to playgrounds, increased traffic movement, and potential occupational health and safety risks for workers. However, no land acquisition, displacement, or impacts on ethnic or vulnerable communities are expected. Overall, the impacts are short-term, reversible, and confined within existing school premises, manageable through standard environmental and social mitigation practices. Tree Cutting: No trees are likely to be cut down and no water bodies are likely to be filled up due to the construction of the flood shelter. The ecological impact of the subproject is low. There will be temporary negative impacts on physico-chemical environment. Nevertheless, these impacts are manageable if mitigation measures are taken according to ESMP. Grass turfing: Grass turfs on embankment, slope, building compound & any critical place to enhance the ecological condition and protect the top soil. Tentative area of turf has been [SOURCE: Page_108]

Page | 66 [SOURCE: Page_108]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_109]

estimated as 240 square meters (half of total area), after discussion with architects and engineers. It is likely to be changed depending on the requirement during construction as per site design and as per direction of E.I.C. Land Ownership: Availability of adequate public land area is as important as community consent to construct the flood shelter and access roads. The D&S Survey team did not find any conflicts over the school land. The land issue has been discussed in the meeting. Participants unanimously confirmed that the school has its own 100 decimals of land and there is no dispute about this land. Land Acquisition: The proposed Sub-project 61No. Bhandara Ponir para Government Primary School, does not have any involuntary resettlement impacts due to the construction of flood shelter and approach roads as the Sub-projects will be constructed in existing Government Primary Schools’ premises. The Government Primary School has 100 decimals of land. No land acquisition will be required for the activities to be implemented under the project. Access road needs to construct or rehabilitate within its existing alignment. Considering the impacts identified at this particular school site, the site-specific Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) may be outlined as follows: [SOURCE: Page_109]

The subproject is located in the Eastern part of Gabtali Upazila in Bogura District, which is within the Rajshahi Division. The location details of the subproject have been summarized in Table 2. Table 2: Location Details of the Subproject Site District                                           :    Bogura Upazila                                            :    Gabtali Union                                              :    Mahishaban Mouza                                              :    Mahishaban Village                                            :    Mahishaban GPS Location                                       :    24.827569 N; 89.473602 E Distance of the site from Upazila HQ               :    10 km -North Nearby Major Road:                                 :    12fit wide BC Chelo para- Chandon baisha at North side Nearby River/ Canal:                               :    Icchamoti River (700m-East) [SOURCE: Page_122]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, June 2025) The catchment area of the subproject mostly comprises of Dhora, Moria, Kania para, Mahishaban, Pal para, Ghoria Para, Dhaho para villages which have been significantly affected by floods. The floods in Bogura District are mainly caused by the overflowing of the Jamuna and its tributaries, especially the Bangali River, which passes through the region. The district’s topography consists of extensive floodplains and low-lying agricultural lands that heighten its flood vulnerability. During the monsoon season, intense rainfall and river overflow inundate large portions of the countryside, leading to waterlogging in settlements and farmland. These flood events have repeatedly disrupted road and transport systems, damaged houses, and caused severe losses to crop production, thereby significantly affecting the livelihoods and resilience of local communities. The flood shelter will be constructed at 76 No. Poschim Mahishaban Government Primary School (GPS), which is located at the Mahishaban village under Mahishaban Union of Gabtali Upazila in Bogura District. There are 5 teachers (M-02; F-03) and 124 students (Boys: 66; Girls: 58) in the school, operated by the guidance of School Management Committee (SMC) and government officials of Gabtali Upazila Education Office. The students, teachers and residents of the catchment area come to the proposed site by using the connecting/access road named Chat moria –Kaliapara Road. The road is an Earthen Road with 2.04 meters width and just passing beside the 76 No. Poschim Mahishaban Government Primary School at west side. The population of the catchment area is about 25,000. People in the area are mostly dependent on shallow tubewell water for their daily uses and the average depth of water is 70 ft below the ground The Mahishaban Union map indicating sub-project location has been shown respectively in Figure 1. The topographical Map with indicative and tentative location of labor camp, [SOURCE: Page_122]

The existing 76 No. Poschim Mahishaban GPS has 51 decimals of land comprises of a one-storied school building that currently accommodate all the classrooms and administrative office rooms located on the north-eastern side and Shaheed Minar adjoining in the existing GPS. The proposed flood shelter is planned to be constructed on the eastern side of the school premises. In case of demolition, one classroom and a toilet structure will need to be removed. For the proposed construction, a ditch measuring approximately 25 meters by 15 meters requires filling to make the site suitable. Furthermore, an access road of about 300 meters in length is needed to ensure proper connectivity to the project site. A labor shed & a material storage area will be constructed at the south corner; a waste disposal area will be constructed at the south-west corner of the compound during the construction period. There is a wash block on the south- eastern corner of the school building. There is a major road on the northern side of the school and along another road located on the western side of the school premises. The area experienced severe flooding in the year 1988 & 2017, with flood waters reaching a height of 4.5 feet & 2 feet and persisting for approximately 15 days due to this flood existing school condition at that time was very rough for continuing the study so it was hampered the student’s study life. Refer to Figures 6 photographs of current situation of the existing GPS & Figure 7 photographs for demolished one classroom & toilet. [SOURCE: Page_125]

Figure 6: Existing school Building                    Figure 7: Demolished one Classroom & Toilet [SOURCE: Page_125]

The important establishments around the subproject site have been summarized in Table-3 Table 3: Important Establishments Adjacent to the Subproject Site [SOURCE: Page_126]

Direction                        Important Establishments with Approximate Distance North side        Mahishaban Park (433m), Kabirajbari Mosque (500m), Primary School (700m), High School (700m), South side        Dohopara Mosque (483 m), Palpara Mandir (500m), Trimohoni Mosque (600m), Mahishaban Bazar (964m) East side        Kainapara Jame Mosque (500m), Ichamoti river (700m) West side         Chalkmaria Mosque (500m), Dhora Purba para Baytul Central jame Mosque (790m) (Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, June 2025) The proposed sub-project (construction of new School cum Flood shelter building) is not located within any environmentally sensitive area and will not cause any severe negative effects to the environmental settings of the area, neither to important environmental features. The disaster shelter will be constructed within an existing school boundary, so no agricultural land/ activities or fish farming will be disturbed due to the construction of the sub project. The project area is surrounded by various significant religious, educational, commercial, and natural landmarks, reflecting a well-balanced community structure. On the north side, there is Kabirajbari Mosque (500 meters), a Primary School (700 meters), and a High School (700 meters), indicating the presence of essential educational facilities. Mahishaban Park (433 meters) provides a recreational space for local residents. On the south side, Palpara Mandir (500 meters), Trimohoni Mosque (600 meters), and Dohopara Mosque (483 meters) highlight the area's religious diversity and harmony. Additionally, Mahishaban Bazar (964 meters) serves as a major commercial hub for the community. To the east, Kainapara Jame Mosque (500 meters) and the Ichamoti River (700 meters) showcase both religious significance and natural beauty. On the west side, Chalkmaria Mosque (500 meters) and Dhora Purba Para Baytul Central Jame Mosque (790 meters) further strengthen the area's religious infrastructure. Overall, the surrounding features contribute to a socially, educationally, and spiritually enriched environment. No significant disturbance to all these establishments/features is anticipated due to construction activities for having sufficient distance from the construction site, and strict construction site management system- including restrictive work schedule during the daytime only, water- sprinkling twice a day in and around the site, proper fencing around the working area, safe storage of materials, etc. Construction related activities and setting up of labor camps along with associated facilities and their management issues will be accounted for impacts more likely to be generated during the pre, post and construction period. Noise pollution from pilling or drilling, air pollution caused by dust or gaseous emissions from vehicle movement, running of motorized equipment and land clearing, odors and soil pollution from leaking of latrines and fecal sludge, will more likely to take place. Soil can further be eroded and polluted from chemical spills or improper disposal of waste Page | 84 [SOURCE: Page_126]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_127]

materials. Noise and vibration effects generated from pilling and drilling may also trigger landslides and harmful disturbances to local fauna. Impact on surface and ground water bodies might get acute due mainly to the high abstraction rate and disposal/leakage of pollutants to the surface/ground water bodies. Clearing of trees, bushes or any type of vegetation may put impact on floral species and unscrupulous clearance also trigger habitat loss. All these impacts can only be prevented or minimized by adopting measures delineated into the ESMP and good practice engineering and site management. ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SCREENING This section identifies the potential impacts that the various elements of the proposed sub- project may have on the physical, biological and socio-economic environment within half a kilometer of the radial distance around the site. Environmental and Social Assessment (ESA) based on this screening study for the Sub-project as 76 No. Poschim Mahishaban Government Primary School of Gabtali Upazila under Bogura District has been conducted to identify and determine which potential project impacts may be significant and therefore require the application of reasonable and effective management and/or mitigation measures. In order to realize the exact physical, biological and socio-economic environment of the proposed sub- project site and the influence area in regards to the implementation measures, an extensive field visit was carried out on 30 June 2025 in the Sub-project area. Environmental and Social Screening form, as adopted in Annexure-2 of the Environmental and Social Management Framework of RIVER, was administered for identifying the impacts and their extents. [SOURCE: Page_127]

PUBLIC CONSULTATION AND PARTICIPATION Public participation and community consultation has been taken up as an integral part of environmental assessment process of the project. Field visit has been carried out on 30 June 2025 in and around the Sub-project component site. As part of the impact assessment, participatory public consultation was conducted in that area by the field level staffs, and consultants from D&SC. Checklist of the consultation is attached in Annexure-3. The consultation meeting was attended by 24 persons (Male -20 and Female -4) and local individuals, teachers, chairman and/or member of Union Parishad and school management committee were among the attendees in that meeting. The participants were selected from different cohorts of stakeholders, and some of whom will have major active roles before, during and even after the construction works. Therefore, the meeting was organized in an informed, expressive and unbiased manner, wherefrom different views and concerns came across which will be properly taken care of during the design and construction phases. Refer to Figure 8 and Annexure-4 for selected photographs of the participatory public consultation held at site of the 76 No. Poschim Mahishaban Government Primary School and list of attendees in that public consultation meeting, respectively. A questionnaire was kept ready and responses were elicited. During these consultations, the communities were explained about the project, its benefits, associated social and environmental aspects and possible mitigation measures. [SOURCE: Page_127]

Page | 85 [SOURCE: Page_127]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_128]

The participants were also informed about the project GRM (Grievance Redress Mechanism) system in detail and the disclosure of project documents in websites, and their unrestricted and uninitiated access to those system and resources. As such, public consultation is a living process as the types of problems/ difficulties, involved parties or stakeholders and mode of settlement or resolution processes are more likely to differ with time. Thus, consultation with different parties or stakeholders will be continued throughout the sub-project implementation period and records of resolutions, whatsoever and wherever possible, will be kept in writing at the site and made available on any enquiries or requests by all parties concerned. [SOURCE: Page_128]

Figure 8: Public Consultation Meeting in the Proposed Sub-project Site SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACTS Overall Construction Related Impacts: The proposed construction works are expected to generate localized and temporary environmental and social impacts typical of small- to medium- scale civil works. Key environmental impacts include dust and air emissions, noise and vibration from machinery, construction waste generation, temporary soil disturbance, and minor vegetation loss during site preparation. There may also be risks of water and soil contamination from improper material handling or drainage obstruction. Social impacts are anticipated to be limited, involving temporary disruption of school activities, restricted access to playgrounds, increased traffic movement, and potential occupational health and safety risks for workers. However, no land acquisition, displacement, or impacts on ethnic or vulnerable communities are expected. Overall, the impacts are short-term, reversible, and confined within existing school premises, manageable through standard environmental and social mitigation practices. Tree Cutting: One tree is likely to be cut down and no water bodies are likely to be filled up due to the construction of the flood shelter. The ecological impact of the subproject is low. There will be temporary negative impacts on physico-chemical environment. Nevertheless, these impacts are manageable if mitigation measures are taken according to ESMP. Grass turfing: Grass turfs on embankment, slope, building compound & any critical place to enhance the ecological condition and protect the top soil. Tentative area of turf has been estimated as 240 square meters (half of total area), after discussion with architects and engineers. It is likely to be changed depending on the requirement during construction as per site design and as per direction of E.I.C. [SOURCE: Page_128]

Page | 86 [SOURCE: Page_128]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_129]

Land Ownership: Availability of adequate public land area is as important as community consent to construct the flood shelter and access roads. The D&S Survey team did not find any conflicts over the school land. The land issue has been discussed in the meeting. Participants unanimously confirmed that the school has its own 51 decimals of land and there is no dispute about this land. Land Acquisition: The proposed Sub-project, 76 No. Poschim Mahishaban Government Primary School, does not have any involuntary resettlement impacts due to the construction of flood shelter and approach roads as the Sub-projects will be constructed in existing Government Primary Schools’ premises. The Government Primary School has 51 decimals of land. No land acquisition will be required for the activities to be implemented under the project. Access road needs to construct or rehabilitate within its existing alignment. The subproject is located in the Eastern part of Gabtali Upazila in Bogura District, which is within the Rajshahi Division. The location details of the subproject have been summarized in Table 2. Table 2: Location Details of the Subproject Site District                                           :    Bogura Upazila                                            :    Gabtali Union                                              :    Mahishaban Mouza                                              :    Ranir para Village                                            :    Par Ranir Para GPS Location                                       :    24.848583 N; 89.491332 E Distance of the site from Upazila HQ               :    7 km (North-West) Nearby Major Road:                                 :    10fit wide Golabari-Durgahata at South side, on 1.5 km [SOURCE: Page_142]

Nearby River/ Canal:                               :    Ichamoti River (3km-South) [SOURCE: Page_142]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, June/July 2025) The catchment area of the subproject mostly comprises of Hatibanda, Par Ranir para,Purba par Ranir para, Chalkbera villages which have been significantly affected by floods. The floods in Bogura District are mainly caused by the overflowing of the Jamuna and its tributaries, especially the Bangali River, which passes through the region. The district’s topography consists of extensive floodplains and low-lying agricultural lands that heighten its flood vulnerability. During the monsoon season, intense rainfall and river overflow inundate large portions of the countryside, leading to waterlogging in settlements and farmland. These flood events have repeatedly disrupted road and transport systems, damaged houses, and caused severe losses to crop production, thereby significantly affecting the livelihoods and resilience of local communities. The flood shelter will be constructed at 72 No. Par Ranir Para Government Primary School (GPS), which is located at the Par Ranir Para village under Mahishaban Union of Gabtali Upazila in Bogura District. There are 5 teachers (M-01; F-04) and 170 students (Boys: 80; Girls: 90) in the school, operated by the guidance of School Management Committee (SMC) and government officials of Gabtali Upazila Education Office. The students, teachers and residents of the catchment area come to the proposed site by using the connecting/access road named Zamtola- Methitola Road. The road is a BC road with 2.04 meters width and just passing beside the 72 No. Par Ranir Para Government Primary School at east side. The population of the catchment area is about 5000. People in the area are mostly dependent on shallow tubewell water for their daily uses and the average depth of water is 90 ft below the ground. The Mahishaban Union map indicating sub-project location has been shown respectively in Figure 1. The topographical Map with indicative and tentative location of labor camp, [SOURCE: Page_142]

Figure 5: Proposed Waste Disposal Area for the Subproject Site The existing 72 No. Par Ranir Para GPS is situated on 56 decimals of land Comprises of one storied pucca building and one storied semi-pucca school building that currently accommodate all the classrooms and administrative office rooms, located on the western side. The proposed flood shelter is planned to be constructed on the western side of the school premises. A Shaheed Minar is located on the south-western side of the school premises. AS part of the proposed construction work, several existing structures within the school premises will require demolition. These include the existing school building along with toilet and septic tank measuring (21m×10m), the old tin-shed school building measuring (9.6m×7m) and the Shaheed Minar measuring (6m×4m). In order to ensure smooth continuation of academic activities during the construction period, it has been identified that a temporary school shed will be necessary. For this purpose, the School Management Committee (SMC) has proposed a piece of land located on the southern side of the school premises for the establishment of the temporary shed. A labor shed, a material storage area and a waste disposal area will be constructed at the south corner of the compound during the construction period. There is a road on the southern side of the school and along additional road located on the eastern side of the school premises. Some local settlements found beside the school boundary on the southern side. The area experienced severe flooding in the year 2019, with flood waters reaching a height of 4 feet and persisting for approximately 30 days due to this flood existing school condition at that time was very rough for continuing the study so it was hampered the student’s study life. Refer to Figures 6 & Figure 7 photographs of current situation of the existing GPS & condition of the demolished school building & Shaheed Minar. [SOURCE: Page_145]

Fotkir Beel, a natural water body, is also situated 700 meters to the south, enhancing the area's natural environment. On the east side, Fotkir Beel appears again at a closer distance (300 meters), and Ranir Para Government Primary School is located just 30 meters away, ensuring easy access to foundational education. The west side includes Malek Bazar Mosque (500 meters), Par Ranir Para High School (700 meters), and Cadet Madrasa (520 meters), all of which support higher education and religious instruction.
