Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_147]

graveyard adjacent to the school is present, reflecting the traditional integration of community facilities. Overall, the area is well-planned and rich in essential services and infrastructure. No significant disturbance to all these establishments/features is anticipated due to construction activities for having sufficient distance from the construction site, and strict construction site management system- including restrictive work schedule during the daytime only, water- sprinkling twice a day in and around the site, proper fencing around the working area, safe storage of materials, etc. Construction related activities and setting up of labor camps along with associated facilities and their management issues will be accounted for impacts more likely to be generated during the pre, post and construction period. Noise pollution from pilling or drilling, air pollution caused by dust or gaseous emissions from vehicle movement, running of motorized equipment and land clearing, odors and soil pollution from leaking of latrines and fecal sludge, will more likely to take place. Soil can further be eroded and polluted from chemical spills or improper disposal of waste materials. Noise and vibration effects generated from pilling and drilling may also trigger landslides and harmful disturbances to local fauna. Impact on surface and ground water bodies might get acute due mainly to the high abstraction rate and disposal/leakage of pollutants to the surface/ground water bodies. Clearing of trees, bushes or any type of vegetation may put impact on floral species and unscrupulous clearance also trigger habitat loss. All these impacts can only be prevented or minimized by adopting measures delineated into the ESMP and good practice engineering and site management. ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SCREENING This section identifies the potential impacts that the various elements of the proposed sub- project may have on the physical, biological and socio-economic environment within half a kilometer of the radial distance around the site. Environmental and Social Assessment (ESA) based on this screening study for the Sub-project as 72 No. Par Ranir Para Government Primary School of Gabtali Upazila under Bogura District has been conducted to identify and determine which potential project impacts may be significant and therefore require the application of reasonable and effective management and/or mitigation measures. In order to realize the exact physical, biological and socio-economic environment of the proposed sub-project site and the influence area in regards to the implementation measures, an extensive field visit was carried out on 30 June 2025 in the Sub-project area. Environmental and Social Screening form, as adopted in Annexure-2 of the Environmental and Social Management Framework of RIVER, was administered for identifying the impacts and their extents. PUBLIC CONSULTATION AND PARTICIPATION Public participation and community consultation has been taken up as an integral part of environmental assessment process of the project. Field visit has been carried out on 30 June 2025 in and around the Sub-project component site. As part of the impact assessment, participatory public consultation was conducted in that area by the field level staffs, and consultants from D&SC. Checklist of the consultation is attached in Annexure-3. The [SOURCE: Page_147]

Page | 105 [SOURCE: Page_147]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_148]

consultation meeting was attended by 26 persons (Male -15 and Female -11) and local individuals, teachers, chairman and/or member of Union Parishad and school management committee were among the attendees in that meeting. The participants were selected from different cohorts of stakeholders, and some of whom will have major active roles before, during and even after the construction works. Therefore, the meeting was organized in an informed, expressive and unbiased manner, wherefrom different views and concerns came across which will be properly taken care of during the design and construction phases. Refer to Figure 8 and Annexure-4 for selected photographs of the participatory public consultation held at site of the 72 No. Par Ranir Para Government Primary School and list of attendees in that public consultation meeting, respectively. A questionnaire was kept ready and responses were elicited. During these consultations, the communities were explained about the project, its benefits, associated social and environmental aspects and possible mitigation measures. The participants were also informed about the project GRM (Grievance Redress Mechanism) system in detail and the disclosure of project documents in websites, and their unrestricted and uninitiated access to those system and resources. As such, public consultation is a living process as the types of problems/ difficulties, involved parties or stakeholders and mode of settlement or resolution processes are more likely to differ with time. Thus, consultation with different parties or stakeholders will be continued throughout the sub-project implementation period and records of resolutions, whatsoever and wherever possible, will be kept in writing at the site and made available on any enquiries or requests by all parties concerned. [SOURCE: Page_148]

Figure 8: Public Consultation Meeting in the Proposed Sub-project Site SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACTS Overall Construction Related Impacts: The proposed construction works are expected to generate localized and temporary environmental and social impacts typical of small- to medium- scale civil works. Key environmental impacts include dust and air emissions, noise and vibration from machinery, construction waste generation, temporary soil disturbance, and minor vegetation loss during site preparation. There may also be risks of water and soil contamination from improper material handling or drainage obstruction. Social impacts are anticipated to be limited, involving temporary disruption of school activities, restricted access to playgrounds, increased traffic movement, and potential occupational health and safety risks for workers. However, no land acquisition, displacement, or impacts on ethnic or vulnerable communities are [SOURCE: Page_148]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_149]

expected. Overall, the impacts are short-term, reversible, and confined within existing school premises, manageable through standard environmental and social mitigation practices. Tree Cutting: Approximately Ten (10) trees (large and small size) are likely to be cut down and at a distance 0f 300 meters to the east of the GPS premises, there is a beel (wetland) which is primarily used for fish farming purposes but no water bodies are likely to be filled up due to the construction of the flood shelter. The ecological impact of the subproject is low. There will be temporary negative impacts on physico-chemical environment. Nevertheless, these impacts are manageable if mitigation measures are taken according to ESMP. Grass turfing: Grass turfs on embankment, slope, building compound & any critical place to enhance the ecological condition and protect the top soil. Tentative area of turf has been estimated as 240 square meters (half of total area), after discussion with architects and engineers. It is likely to be changed depending on the requirement during construction as per site design and as per direction of E.I.C. Land Ownership: Availability of adequate public land area is as important as community consent to construct the flood shelter and access roads. The D&S Survey team did not find any conflicts over the school land. The land issue has been discussed in the meeting. Participants unanimously confirmed that the school has its own 56 decimals of land and there is no dispute about this land. Land Acquisition: The proposed Sub-project, 72 No. Par Ranir Para Government Primary School, does not have any involuntary resettlement impacts due to the construction of flood shelter and approach roads as the Sub-projects will be constructed in existing Government Primary Schools’ premises. The Government Primary School has 56 decimals of land. No land acquisition will be required for the activities to be implemented under the project. Access road needs to construct or rehabilitate within its existing alignment. Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_163]

The subproject is located in the Southern part of Gabtali Upazila in Bogura District, which is within the Rajshahi Division. The location details of the subproject have been summarized in Table 2. Table 2: Location Details of the Subproject Site District                                           :    Bogura Upazila                                            :    Gabtali Union                                              :    Nasipur Mouza                                              :    Itali Village                                            :    Bara Itali GPS Location                                       :    24.765097 N; 89.473866 E Distance of the site from Upazila HQ               :    16 km Nearby Major Road:                                 :    16ft. wide BC Baghbari-Dhonot Road at South side on 15km [SOURCE: Page_163]

Nearby River/ Canal:                               :    Bangali River (5km-East) [SOURCE: Page_163]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, July 2025) The catchment area of the subproject mostly comprises of Majbari, Berer bari, Beltoli, Bara Itali villages which have been significantly affected by floods. The floods in Bogura District are mainly caused by the overflowing of the Jamuna and its tributaries, especially the Bangali River, which passes through the region. The district’s topography consists of extensive floodplains and low- lying agricultural lands that heighten its flood vulnerability. During the monsoon season, intense rainfall and river overflow inundate large portions of the countryside, leading to waterlogging in settlements and farmland. These flood events have repeatedly disrupted road and transport systems, damaged houses, and caused severe losses to crop production, thereby significantly affecting the livelihoods and resilience of local communities. The flood shelter will be constructed at 50 No. Bara Itali Government Primary School (GPS), which is located at the Bara Itali village under Nasipur Union of Gabtali Upazila in Bogura District. There are 5 teachers (M-02; F-03) and 90 students (Boys: 47; Girls: 43) in the school, operated by the guidance of School Management Committee (SMC) and government officials of Gabtali Upazila Education Office. The students, teachers and residents of the catchment area come to the proposed site by using the connecting/access road named Baghbari to Dublagari Road. The road is a BC road with 2.04 meters width and just passing beside the 50 No. Bara Itali Government Primary School at North side. The population of the catchment area is about 20000. People in the area are mostly dependent on shallow tubewell water for their daily uses and the average depth of water is 60 ft below the ground. The Nasipur Union map indicating sub-project location has been shown respectively in Figure 1. The topographical Map with indicative and tentative location of labor camp, [SOURCE: Page_163]

The existing 50 No. Bara Itali GPS is situated on 35 decimals of land Comprises of one storied tin- shed & one storied pucca school building that currently accommodate all the classrooms and administrative office rooms, located on the northern and eastern side. The proposed flood shelter is planned to be constructed on the opposite side of the school building, that is towards the southern side of the school premises. A Shaheed Minar is located on the north-eastern side of the school premises. AS part of the proposed construction work, several existing structures within the school premises will require demolition. These include the existing school building measuring (19m×9m), which also contains a toilet and septic tank of approximately (5.5m×3.5m). Additionally, there is an old tin shed school building measuring (6.7m×4m), and a Shaheed Minar measuring (3.3m×3m). For the proposed construction, a ditch measuring 14 meters by 5 meters will need to be filled to make the site suitable. Key findings indicate that a temporary school shed is required during the construction period. To accommodate this, the School Management Committee (SMC) has proposed a nearby plot of land, outside the existing school premises, within the adjacent madrasa premises. A labor shed & a material storage area will be constructed to the north-east corner, outside the proposed area, a waste disposal area will be constructed at the east corner of the compound during the construction period. [SOURCE: Page_166]

There is a major road on the southern side of the school and along additional road located on the northern side of the school premises. Some local settlements found beside the school boundary on the western side. The area experienced severe flooding in the year 1988, with flood waters reaching a height of 3 feet and persisting for approximately 15 days due to this flood existing school condition at that time was very rough for continuing the study so it was hampered the student’s study life. Refer to Figure 6 & Figure 7 for photographs of current situation of the existing GPS & demolished school building & Shaheed Minar [SOURCE: Page_166]

The important establishments around the subproject site have been summarized in Table-3 Table 3: Important Establishments Adjacent to the Subproject Site [SOURCE: Page_167]

Direction                      Important Establishments with Approximate Distance North side    Dakhil Madrasa (100m), Bara Itali Jame Mosque (200m), Community Space (500m), Graveyard (400m) South side    Hafezia Madrasa (900m) East side     Bara Itali central Eidgah (72.84m), Eidgah (200m), Mosque (300m), West side     Dhoniar beel (1000m) [SOURCE: Page_167]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, July 2025) [SOURCE: Page_167]

The proposed sub-project (construction of new School cum Flood shelter building) is not located within any environmentally sensitive area and will not cause any severe negative effects to the environmental settings of the area, neither to important environmental features. The disaster shelter will be constructed within an existing school boundary, so no agricultural land/ activities or fish farming will be disturbed due to the construction of the sub project. The project area is surrounded by a variety of religious, educational, and community landmarks in all four directions. On the north side, there is the Bara Itali Jame Mosque located 200 meters away, along with a Dakhil Madrasa just 100 meters from the center, providing accessible religious and educational services. A community space is situated 500 meters to the north, supporting social activities, while a graveyard at 400 meters reflects traditional community planning. To the south, A Hafezia Madrasa is present 900 meters away, offering specialized religious education. On the east side, the area features an Eidgah at 200 meters, another mosque at 300 meters, and the Bara Itali Central Eidgah at 72.84 meters, which collectively highlight the area's strong religious presence, especially during major Islamic festivals. The west side is bordered by Dhoniar Beel, a significant natural water body located 1000 meters away, contributing to the area's environmental and ecological balance. Overall, the surrounding infrastructure provides a well- rounded mix of religious, educational, social, and environmental resources that support the local community's daily life. [SOURCE: Page_167]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_168]

No significant disturbance to all these establishments/features is anticipated due to construction activities for having sufficient distance from the construction site, and strict construction site management system- including restrictive work schedule during the daytime only, water- sprinkling twice a day in and around the site, proper fencing around the working area, safe storage of materials, etc. Construction related activities and setting up of labor camps along with associated facilities and their management issues will be accounted for impacts more likely to be generated during the pre, post and construction period. Noise pollution from pilling or drilling, air pollution caused by dust or gaseous emissions from vehicle movement, running of motorized equipment and land clearing, odors and soil pollution from leaking of latrines and fecal sludge, will more likely to take place. Soil can further be eroded and polluted from chemical spills or improper disposal of waste materials. Noise and vibration effects generated from pilling and drilling may also trigger landslides and harmful disturbances to local fauna. Impact on surface and ground water bodies might get acute due mainly to the high abstraction rate and disposal/leakage of pollutants to the surface/ground water bodies. Clearing of trees, bushes or any type of vegetation may put impact on floral species and unscrupulous clearance also trigger habitat loss. All these impacts can only be prevented or minimized by adopting measures delineated into the ESMP and good practice engineering and site management. ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SCREENING This section identifies the potential impacts that the various elements of the proposed sub- project may have on the physical, biological and socio-economic environment within half a kilometer of the radial distance around the site. Environmental and Social Assessment (ESA) based on this screening study for the Sub-project as 50 No. Bara Itali Government Primary School of Gabtali Upazila under Bogura District has been conducted to identify and determine which potential project impacts may be significant and therefore require the application of reasonable and effective management and/or mitigation measures. In order to realize the exact physical, biological and socio-economic environment of the proposed sub-project site and the influence area in regards to the implementation measures, an extensive field visit was carried out on 01July 2025 in the Sub-project area. Environmental and Social Screening form, as adopted in Annexure-2 of the Environmental and Social Management Framework of RIVER, was administered for identifying the impacts and their extents. [SOURCE: Page_168]

PUBLIC CONSULTATION AND PARTICIPATION Public participation and community consultation has been taken up as an integral part of environmental assessment process of the project. Field visit has been carried out on 01 July 2025 in and around the Sub-project component site. As part of the impact assessment, participatory public consultation was conducted in that area by the field level staffs, and consultants from D&SC. Checklist of the consultation is attached in Annexure-3. The consultation meeting was attended by 17 persons (Male -12 and Female -5) and local individuals, teachers, chairman and/or member of Union Parishad and school management committee were among the [SOURCE: Page_168]

Page | 126 [SOURCE: Page_168]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_169]

attendees in that meeting. The participants were selected from different cohorts of stakeholders, and some of whom will have major active roles before, during and even after the construction works. Therefore, the meeting was organized in an informed, expressive and unbiased manner, wherefrom different views and concerns came across which will be properly taken care of during the design and construction phases. Refer to Figure 8 and Annexure-4 for selected photographs of the participatory public consultation held at site of the 50 No. Bara Itali Government Primary School and list of attendees in that public consultation meeting, respectively. A questionnaire was kept ready and responses were elicited. During these consultations, the communities were explained about the project, its benefits, associated social and environmental aspects and possible mitigation measures. The participants were also informed about the project GRM (Grievance Redress Mechanism) system in detail and the disclosure of project documents in websites, and their unrestricted and uninitiated access to those system and resources. As such, public consultation is a living process as the types of problems/ difficulties, involved parties or stakeholders and mode of settlement or resolution processes are more likely to differ with time. Thus, consultation with different parties or stakeholders will be continued throughout the sub-project implementation period and records of resolutions, whatsoever and wherever possible, will be kept in writing at the site and made available on any enquiries or requests by all parties concerned. [SOURCE: Page_169]

Figure 8: Public Consultation Meeting in the Proposed Sub-project Site SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACTS Overall Construction Related Impacts: The proposed construction works are expected to generate localized and temporary environmental and social impacts typical of small- to medium- scale civil works. Key environmental impacts include dust and air emissions, noise and vibration from machinery, construction waste generation, temporary soil disturbance, and minor vegetation loss during site preparation. There may also be risks of water and soil contamination from improper material handling or drainage obstruction. Social impacts are anticipated to be limited, involving temporary disruption of school activities, restricted access to playgrounds, increased traffic movement, and potential occupational health and safety risks for workers. However, no land acquisition, displacement, or impacts on ethnic or vulnerable communities are expected. Overall, the impacts are short-term, reversible, and confined within existing school premises, manageable through standard environmental and social mitigation practices. [SOURCE: Page_169]

Page | 127 [SOURCE: Page_169]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_170]

Tree Cutting: Approximately Six (6) trees are likely to be cut down and at a distance of 1 kilometer to the west of the GPS premises, there is a beel (wetland) named ‘Dhoniar Beel’ with an average depth of about 4 feet; however, there is no possibility of the water body being filled up due to the construction of the flood shelter. The ecological impact of the subproject is low. There will be temporary negative impacts on physico-chemical environment. Nevertheless, these impacts are manageable if mitigation measures are taken according to ESMP. Grass turfing: Grass turfs on embankment, slope, building compound & any critical place to enhance the ecological condition and protect the top soil. Tentative area of turf has been estimated as 240 square meters (half of total area), after discussion with architects and engineers. It is likely to be changed depending on the requirement during construction as per site design and as per direction of E.I.C. Land Ownership: Availability of adequate public land area is as important as community consent to construct the flood shelter and access roads. The D&S Survey team did not find any conflicts over the school land. The land issue has been discussed in the meeting. Participants unanimously confirmed that the school has its own 35 decimals of land and there is no dispute about this land. Land Acquisition: The proposed Sub-project, 50 No. Bara Itali Government Primary School, does not have any involuntary resettlement impacts due to the construction of flood shelter and approach roads as the Sub-projects will be constructed in existing Government Primary Schools’ premises. The Government Primary School has 35 decimals of land. No land acquisition will be required for the activities to be implemented under the project. Access road needs to construct or rehabilitate within its existing alignment. Considering the impacts identified at this particular school site, the site-specific Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) may be outlined as follows: [SOURCE: Page_170]

LOCATION OF THE SUB-PROJECT The subproject is located in the Southern part of Gabtali Upazila in Bogura District, which is within the Rajshahi Division. The location details of the subproject have been summarized in Table 2. Table 2: Location Details of the Subproject Site District                                          :    Bogura Upazila                                           :    Gabtali Union                                             :    Nasipur Mouza                                             :    Nasipur Village                                           :    Horrerdighi GPS Location                                      :    24.796999 N; 89.478942 E Distance of the site from Upazila HQ              :    15km -North Nearby Major Road:                                :    16ft. wide BC Bhagbari-Bonani Road at South side on 1.5 km [SOURCE: Page_184]

Nearby River/ Canal:                              :    Ichamoti Sakha River (500m-West) [SOURCE: Page_184]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, July 2025) The catchment area of the subproject mostly comprises of Mahishaban, Horrerdighi, Bhagbari, Poler bari, Kolapopa, Nizgram, Dayarampur villages which have been significantly affected by floods. The floods in Bogura District are mainly caused by the overflowing of the Jamuna and its tributaries, especially the Bangali River, which passes through the region. The district’s topography consists of extensive floodplains and low-lying agricultural lands that heighten its flood vulnerability. During the monsoon season, intense rainfall and river overflow inundate large portions of the countryside, leading to waterlogging in settlements and farmland. These flood events have repeatedly disrupted road and transport systems, damaged houses, and caused severe losses to crop production, thereby significantly affecting the livelihoods and resilience of local communities. The flood shelter will be constructed at 77 No. Horrerdighi Government Primary School (GPS), which is located at the Horrerdighi village under Nasipur Union of Gabtali Upazila in Bogura District. There are 5 teachers (M-04; F-01) and 141 students (Boys: 63; Girls: 78) in the school, operated by the guidance of School Management Committee (SMC) and government officials of Gabtali Upazila Education Office. The students, teachers and residents of the catchment area come to the proposed site by using the connecting/access road named Horrerdighi Mondol bari Road. The road is a HBB road with 3.04 meters width and just passing adjacent the 77 No. Horrerdighi Government Primary School. The population of the catchment area is about 22000. People in the area are mostly dependent on shallow tubewell water for their daily uses and the average depth of water is 80 ft below the Page | 142 [SOURCE: Page_184]

The existing 77 No. Horrerdighi GPS is situated on 51 decimals of land Comprises of two single- storied buildings that currently accommodate all the classrooms and administrative office rooms, located on the eastern and western side and a wash block adjacent in the school building. A Shaheed Minar is located on the eastern side of the school premises. The proposed flood shelter is planned to be constructed on the east side of the school premises. In case of demolition, the identified old structures include an existing school building measuring approximately 19 meters by 11 meters, a wash block measuring 14 meters by 4.5 meters, and a Shaheed Minar with dimensions of 5 meters by 3 meters. Additionally, a ditch of around 23 meters by 5 meters exists within the premises, which will require proper filling for future construction activities. As part of the key findings, it has also been identified that two electrical poles need to be removed to ensure safety and to make the site suitable for the proposed development. A labor shed & a waste disposal will be constructed at the north corner; a material storage area will be constructed at the west corner of the compound during the construction period. There is a major road on the southern side of the school and along additional road adjacent the school premises. Some local settlements found beside the school boundary on the southern side. The area experienced severe flooding in the year 1988, with flood waters reaching a height of 6 feet and persisting for approximately 20 days due to this flood existing school condition at that time was very rough for continuing the study so it was hampered the student’s study life. Refer to Figure 6 & Figure 7 photographs of current situation of the existing GPS & condition of the demolished school building, wash block & Shaheed Minar. [SOURCE: Page_187]

The proposed sub-project (construction of new School cum Flood shelter building) is not located within any environmentally sensitive area and will not cause any severe negative effects to the environmental settings of the area, neither to important environmental features. The disaster shelter will be constructed within an existing school boundary, so no agricultural land/ activities or fish farming will be disturbed due to the construction of the sub project. The project area is surrounded by various significant landmarks and institutions that contribute to its cultural, religious, and natural landscape. On the north side, notable establishments include the Horrerdighi Uttar Para Mosque, located approximately 400 meters away, and the Dayarampur Sirajul Haque Dakhil Madrasa, situated about 500 meters from the central point. To the south, there is the Horrerdighi Purbo Para Mosque at a distance of 200 meters, along with a Hafezia Madrasa 500 meters away, and the Poshchim Para Mosque, located around 700 meters from the center. The east side is bordered by natural water bodies such as Lotagari Beel, 500 meters away, and Elengir Beel, just 200 meters from the site. On the west side, the Ichamoti Sakha River flows approximately 500 meters from the area, adding to the natural environment of the region. This diverse mix of religious institutions and natural features highlights the cultural richness and ecological value of the surrounding area. [SOURCE: Page_188]

No significant disturbance to all these establishments/features is anticipated due to construction activities for having sufficient distance from the construction site, and strict construction site management system- including restrictive work schedule during the daytime only, water- sprinkling twice a day in and around the site, proper fencing around the working area, safe storage of materials, etc. Construction related activities and setting up of labor camps along with associated facilities and their management issues will be accounted for impacts more likely to be generated during the pre, post and construction period. Noise pollution from pilling or drilling, air pollution caused by dust or gaseous emissions from vehicle movement, running of motorized equipment and land clearing, odors and soil pollution from leaking of latrines and fecal sludge, will more likely to take place. Soil can further be eroded and polluted from chemical spills or improper disposal of waste Page | 146 [SOURCE: Page_188]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_189]

materials. Noise and vibration effects generated from pilling and drilling may also trigger landslides and harmful disturbances to local fauna. Impact on surface and ground water bodies might get acute due mainly to the high abstraction rate and disposal/leakage of pollutants to the surface/ground water bodies. Clearing of trees, bushes or any type of vegetation may put impact on floral species and unscrupulous clearance also trigger habitat loss. All these impacts can only be prevented or minimized by adopting measures delineated into the ESMP and good practice engineering and site management. ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SCREENING This section identifies the potential impacts that the various elements of the proposed sub- project may have on the physical, biological and socio-economic environment within half a kilometer of the radial distance around the site. Environmental and Social Assessment (ESA) based on this screening study for the Sub-project as 77 No. Horrerdighi Government Primary School of Gabtali Upazila under Bogura District has been conducted to identify and determine which potential project impacts may be significant and therefore require the application of reasonable and effective management and/or mitigation measures. In order to realize the exact physical, biological and socio-economic environment of the proposed sub-project site and the influence area in regards to the implementation measures, an extensive field visit was carried out on 01 July 2025 in the Sub-project area. Environmental and Social Screening form, as adopted in Annexure-2 of the Environmental and Social Management Framework of RIVER, was administered for identifying the impacts and their extents. [SOURCE: Page_189]

PUBLIC CONSULTATION AND PARTICIPATION Public participation and community consultation has been taken up as an integral part of environmental assessment process of the project. Field visit has been carried out on 01 July 2025 in and around the Sub-project component site. As part of the impact assessment, participatory public consultation was conducted in that area by the field level staffs, and consultants from D&SC. Checklist of the consultation is attached in Annexure-3. The consultation meeting was attended by 22 persons (Male -16 and Female -6) and local individuals, teachers, chairman and/or member of Union Parishad and school management committee were among the attendees in that meeting. The participants were selected from different cohorts of stakeholders, and some of whom will have major active roles before, during and even after the construction works. Therefore, the meeting was organized in an informed, expressive and unbiased manner, wherefrom different views and concerns came across which will be properly taken care of during the design and construction phases. Refer to Figure 8 and Annexure-4 for selected photographs of the participatory public consultation held at site of the 77 No. Horrerdighi Government Primary School and list of attendees in that public consultation meeting, respectively. A questionnaire was kept ready and responses were elicited. During these consultations, the communities were explained about the project, its benefits, associated social and environmental aspects and possible mitigation measures. [SOURCE: Page_189]

Page | 147 [SOURCE: Page_189]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_190]

The participants were also informed about the project GRM (Grievance Redress Mechanism) system in detail and the disclosure of project documents in websites, and their unrestricted and uninitiated access to those system and resources. As such, public consultation is a living process as the types of problems/ difficulties, involved parties or stakeholders and mode of settlement or resolution processes are more likely to differ with time. Thus, consultation with different parties or stakeholders will be continued throughout the sub-project implementation period and records of resolutions, whatsoever and wherever possible, will be kept in writing at the site and made available on any enquiries or requests by all parties concerned. [SOURCE: Page_190]

Figure 8: Public Consultation Meeting in the Proposed Sub-project Site SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACTS Overall Construction Related Impacts: The proposed construction works are expected to generate localized and temporary environmental and social impacts typical of small- to medium- scale civil works. Key environmental impacts include dust and air emissions, noise and vibration from machinery, construction waste generation, temporary soil disturbance, and minor vegetation loss during site preparation. There may also be risks of water and soil contamination from improper material handling or drainage obstruction. Social impacts are anticipated to be limited, involving temporary disruption of school activities, restricted access to playgrounds, increased traffic movement, and potential occupational health and safety risks for workers. However, no land acquisition, displacement, or impacts on ethnic or vulnerable communities are expected. Overall, the impacts are short-term, reversible, and confined within existing school premises, manageable through standard environmental and social mitigation practices. Tree Cutting: Approximately two (2) trees are likely to be cut down and no water bodies are likely to be filled up due to the construction of the flood shelter. The ecological impact of the subproject is low. There will be temporary negative impacts on physico-chemical environment. Nevertheless, these impacts are manageable if mitigation measures are taken according to ESMP. Grass turfing: Grass turfs on embankment, slope, building compound & any critical place to enhance the ecological condition and protect the top soil. Tentative area of turf has been estimated as 240 square meters (half of total area), after discussion with architects and engineers. It is likely to be changed depending on the requirement during construction as per site design and as per direction of E.I.C. Page | 148 [SOURCE: Page_190]

Land Ownership: Availability of adequate public land area is as important as community consent to construct the flood shelter and access roads. The D&S Survey team did not find any conflicts over the school land. The land issue has been discussed in the meeting. Participants unanimously confirmed that the school has its own 51 decimals of land and there is no dispute about this land. Land Acquisition: The proposed Sub-project, 77 No. Horrerdighi Government Primary School, does not have any involuntary resettlement impacts due to the construction of flood shelter and approach roads as the Sub-projects will be constructed in existing Government Primary Schools’ premises. The Government Primary School has 51 decimals of land. No land acquisition will be required for the activities to be implemented under the project. Access road needs to construct or rehabilitate within its existing alignment. Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_204]

LOCATION OF THE SUB-PROJECT The subproject is located in the Eastern part of Gabtali Upazila in Bogura District, which is within the Rajshahi Division. The location details of the subproject have been summarized in Table 2. Table 2: Location Details of the Subproject Site District                                           :    Bogura Upazila                                            :    Gabtali Union                                              :    Nepaltali Mouza                                              :    Dhananjoy Village                                            :    Bil Sorolia GPS Location                                       :    24.897317 N; 89.491028 E Distance of the site from Upazila HQ               :    8km Nearby Major Road:                                 :    12ft. Wide BC Bil Sorolia-Naruamala at North side on 5km. Nearby River/ Canal:                               :    Nolgoria Canal (400m-West), Soiller khal (250m- East) [SOURCE: Page_204]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, June 2025) The catchment area of the subproject mostly comprises of Bil Sorolia, Dhananjoy, Kadomtoli, Akondapara villages which have been significantly affected by floods. The floods in Bogura District are mainly caused by the overflowing of the Jamuna and its tributaries, especially the Bangali River, which passes through the region. The district’s topography consists of extensive floodplains and low-lying agricultural lands that heighten its flood vulnerability. During the monsoon season, intense rainfall and river overflow inundate large portions of the countryside, leading to waterlogging in settlements and farmland. These flood events have repeatedly disrupted road and transport systems, damaged houses, and caused severe losses to crop production, thereby significantly affecting the livelihoods and resilience of local communities. [SOURCE: Page_204]

The flood shelter will be constructed at Bil Sorolia Government Primary School (GPS), which is located at the Bil Sorolia village under Nepaltali Union of Gabtali Upazila in Bogura District. There are 6 teachers and 109 students (Boys: 48; Girls: 61) in the school, operated by the guidance of School Management Committee (SMC) and government officials of Gabtali Upazila Education Office. The students, teachers and residents of the catchment area come to the proposed site by using the connecting/access road Bil Sorolia Road. The road is an Earthen Road with 3.04 meters width and just passing adjacent the Bil Sorolia Government Primary School. [SOURCE: Page_204]

The population of the catchment area is about 52000. People in the area are mostly dependent on shallow tubewell water for their daily uses and the average depth of water is 30 ft below the ground.The Nepaltali Union map indicating sub-project location has been shown respectively in Page | 162 [SOURCE: Page_204]

The existing Bil Sorolia GPS is situated on 49 decimals of land Comprises of one storied pucca building located on the southern side & two single-storied buildings that currently accommodate all the classrooms and administrative office rooms, located on the south and western side. A Shaheed Minar is located on the southern side of the school premises. The proposed flood shelter is planned to be constructed across the south-western part of the school premises. A labor shed & a material storage area will be constructed at the east corner; a waste disposal area will be constructed at the north-east corner of the compound during the construction period. In case of demolition, the existing structures within the school premises include two old school buildings measuring 21.5 meters by 9.4 meters and 17.8 meters by 9.6 meters, respectively. In addition, there is a tin-shed structure with a dimension of 7.8 meters by 5.7 meters. [SOURCE: Page_207]

The key findings of the assessment indicate that the development of an access road will be required to facilitate the proposed construction works. Furthermore, to ensure uninterrupted academic activities during the construction period, the establishment of a temporary school shed has been identified as essential. There is a major road on the northern side of the school and along additional road adjacent the school premises. Some local settlements found beside the school boundary on the western side. The area experienced severe flooding in the year 2020, with flood waters reaching a height of 6 feet and persisting for approximately 20-25 days due to this flood existing school condition at that time was very rough for continuing the study so it was hampered the student’s study life. Refer to Figures 6 for photographs of current situation of the existing GPS & Figure 7 photographs for demolished old school building. [SOURCE: Page_207]

The important establishments around the subproject site have been summarized in Table-3 Table 3: Important Establishments Adjacent to the Subproject Site [SOURCE: Page_208]

Direction                      Important Establishments with Approximate Distance North side    Kadamtali Bakshipara Mosque (300m), Kadamtali Bakshipara Eidgah Field (800m), Chalkchakiar Beel (1km) South side    Bil Sorolia Mosque (50m), Nolgoriar Beel (500m) East side     Bil Sorolia Eidgah Field (100m), Soiller Beel (200m), Kadamtali Tairpara Eidgah Field (400m) West side     Kadamtali Khapara Eidgah Field (264m), Kadamtali Khapara Nur Jame Mosque (270m), Nolgoria Beel (400m) (Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, June 2025) [SOURCE: Page_208]

The proposed sub-project (construction of new School cum Flood shelter building) is not located within any environmentally sensitive area and will not cause any severe negative effects to the environmental settings of the area, neither to important environmental features. The disaster shelter will be constructed within an existing school boundary, so no agricultural land/ activities or fish farming will be disturbed due to the construction of the sub project. The project area is surrounded by a variety of religious, educational, and community landmarks in all four directions. To the north, key landmarks include the Kadamtali Bakshipara Mosque, located approximately 300 meters away, the Kadamtali Bakshipara Eidgah Field at a distance of 800 meters, and the natural water body Chalkchakiar Beel, situated about 1 kilometer from the center. On the south side, the Bil Sorolia Mosque is very close, just 50 meters away, and the Nolgoriar Beel, located 500 meters away. The east side features significant sites such as the Kadamtali Tairpara Eidgah Field (400 meters), the Bil Sorolia Eidgah Field (100 meters), and the Soiller Beel (200 meters), all contributing to the area's religious and natural landscape. On the west side, the Kadamtali Khapara Nur Jame Mosque is situated 270 meters away, with the nearby Kadamtali Khapara Eidgah Field at 264 meters, and the Nolgoria Beel located about 400 meters from the center. Overall, this area reflects a harmonious coexistence of community, faith, education, and nature. [SOURCE: Page_208]

Page | 166 [SOURCE: Page_208]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_209]

No significant disturbance to all these establishments/features is anticipated due to construction activities for having sufficient distance from the construction site, and strict construction site management system- including restrictive work schedule during the daytime only, water- sprinkling twice a day in and around the site, proper fencing around the working area, safe storage of materials, etc. Construction related activities and setting up of labor camps along with associated facilities and their management issues will be accounted for impacts more likely to be generated during the pre, post and construction period. Noise pollution from pilling or drilling, air pollution caused by dust or gaseous emissions from vehicle movement, running of motorized equipment and land clearing, odors and soil pollution from leaking of latrines and fecal sludge, will more likely to take place. Soil can further be eroded and polluted from chemical spills or improper disposal of waste materials. Noise and vibration effects generated from pilling and drilling may also trigger landslides and harmful disturbances to local fauna. Impact on surface and ground water bodies might get acute due mainly to the high abstraction rate and disposal/leakage of pollutants to the surface/ground water bodies. Clearing of trees, bushes or any type of vegetation may put impact on floral species and unscrupulous clearance also trigger habitat loss. All these impacts can only be prevented or minimized by adopting measures delineated into the ESMP and good practice engineering and site management. ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SCREENING This section identifies the potential impacts that the various elements of the proposed sub- project may have on the physical, biological and socio-economic environment within half a kilometer of the radial distance around the site. Environmental and Social Assessment (ESA) based on this screening study for the Sub-project as Bil Sorolia Government Primary School of Gabtali Upazila under Bogura District has been conducted to identify and determine which potential project impacts may be significant and therefore require the application of reasonable and effective management and/or mitigation measures. In order to realize the exact physical, biological and socio-economic environment of the proposed sub-project site and the influence area in regards to the implementation measures, an extensive field visit was carried out on 30 June 2025 in the Sub-project area. Environmental and Social Screening form, as adopted in Annexure-2 of the Environmental and Social Management Framework of RIVER, was administered for identifying the impacts and their extents. [SOURCE: Page_209]

PUBLIC CONSULTATION AND PARTICIPATION Public participation and community consultation has been taken up as an integral part of environmental assessment process of the project. Field visit has been carried out on 30 June 2025 in and around the Sub-project component site. As part of the impact assessment, participatory public consultation was conducted in that area by the field level staffs, and consultants from D&SC. Checklist of the consultation is attached in Annexure-3. The consultation meeting was attended by 34 persons (Male -17 and Female -17) and local individuals, teachers, chairman and/or member of Union Parishad and school management [SOURCE: Page_209]

Page | 167 [SOURCE: Page_209]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_210]

committee were among the attendees in that meeting. The participants were selected from different cohorts of stakeholders, and some of whom will have major active roles before, during and even after the construction works. Therefore, the meeting was organized in an informed, expressive and unbiased manner, wherefrom different views and concerns came across which will be properly taken care of during the design and construction phases. Refer to Figure 8 and Annexure-4 for selected photographs of the participatory public consultation held at site of the Bil Sorolia Government Primary School and list of attendees in that public consultation meeting, respectively. A questionnaire was kept ready and responses were elicited. During these consultations, the communities were explained about the project, its benefits, associated social and environmental aspects and possible mitigation measures. The participants were also informed about the project GRM (Grievance Redress Mechanism) system in detail and the disclosure of project documents in websites, and their unrestricted and uninitiated access to those system and resources. As such, public consultation is a living process as the types of problems/ difficulties, involved parties or stakeholders and mode of settlement or resolution processes are more likely to differ with time. Thus, consultation with different parties or stakeholders will be continued throughout the sub-project implementation period and records of resolutions, whatsoever and wherever possible, will be kept in writing at the site and made available on any enquiries or requests by all parties concerned. [SOURCE: Page_210]

Figure 8: Public Consultation Meeting in the Proposed Sub-project Site SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACTS Overall Construction Related Impacts: The proposed construction works are expected to generate localized and temporary environmental and social impacts typical of small- to medium- scale civil works. Key environmental impacts include dust and air emissions, noise and vibration from machinery, construction waste generation, temporary soil disturbance, and minor vegetation loss during site preparation. There may also be risks of water and soil contamination from improper material handling or drainage obstruction. Social impacts are anticipated to be limited, involving temporary disruption of school activities, restricted access to playgrounds, increased traffic movement, and potential occupational health and safety risks for workers. However, no land acquisition, displacement, or impacts on ethnic or vulnerable communities are expected. Overall, the impacts are short-term, reversible, and confined within existing school premises, manageable through standard environmental and social mitigation practices. Tree Cutting: Approximately Ten (10) trees are likely to be cut down and no water bodies are Page | 168 [SOURCE: Page_210]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_211]

likely to be filled up due to the construction of the flood shelter. The ecological impact of the subproject is low. There will be temporary negative impacts on physico-chemical environment. Nevertheless, these impacts are manageable if mitigation measures are taken according to ESMP. Grass turfing: Grass turfs on embankment, slope, building compound & any critical place to enhance the ecological condition and protect the top soil. Tentative area of turf has been estimated as 240 square meters (half of total area), after discussion with architects and engineers. It is likely to be changed depending on the requirement during construction as per site design and as per direction of E.I.C. Land Ownership: Availability of adequate public land area is as important as community consent to construct the flood shelter and access roads. The D&S Survey team did not find any conflicts over the school land. The land issue has been discussed in the meeting. Participants unanimously confirmed that the school has its own 49 decimals of land and there is no dispute about this land. Land Acquisition: The proposed Sub-project, Bil Sorolia Government Primary School, does not have any involuntary resettlement impacts due to the construction of flood shelter and approach roads as the Sub-projects will be constructed in existing Government Primary Schools’ premises. The Government Primary School has 49 decimals of land. No land acquisition will be required for the activities to be implemented under the project. Access road needs to construct or rehabilitate within its existing alignment. Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_225]

LOCATION OF THE SUB-PROJECT The subproject is located in the Eastern part of Gabtali Upazila in Bogura District, which is within the Rajshahi Division. The location details of the subproject have been summarized in Table 2. Table 2: Location Details of the Subproject Site District                                           :    Bogura Upazila                                            :    Gabtali Union                                              :    Nepaltali Mouza                                              :    Dhananjoy Village                                            :    Dhananjoy GPS Location                                       :    24.892182 N; 89.496754 E Distance of the site from Upazila HQ               :    8 km South Nearby Major Road:                                 :    Chelopara-Shariakandi road: South side, Distance: 2km, wide: 10fit, BC road Nearby River/ Canal:                               :    Sharkidah Khal (North-500m) [SOURCE: Page_225]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, June 2025) The catchment area of the subproject mostly comprises of Terotakhi, Akonda para, Tair para, Kaludanga, Kadomtoli,Shahbajpur, Dhananjoy villages which have been significantly affected by floods. Gabtali Upazila, located within the low-lying eastern alluvial tract of Bogura District, is notably prone to flooding. Its fertile lands are nourished by silt deposited during floods, but this geographical advantage also comes with heightened flood risk. The presence of multiple rivers— including the Jamuna, Karatoya, and Bangali—coupled with numerous canals and natural wetlands (khals and beels) creates conditions where heavy monsoon rainfall and river overflow routinely inundate the area. These floods can severely disrupt agriculture, infrastructure, and local livelihoods. The flood shelter will be constructed at Dhananjoy Government Primary School (GPS), which is located at the Dhananjoy village under Nepaltali Union of Gabtali Upazila in Bogura District. There are 7 teachers, and 210 students (Boys: 108; Girls: 102) in the school, operated by the guidance of School Management Committee (SMC) and government officials of Gabtali Upazila Education Office. The students, teachers and residents of the catchment area come to the proposed site by using the connecting/access road named 10fit wide Dhananjoy GPS connecting earthern road. The road is a BC road with 10fit width and just passing beside the Dhananjoy Government Primary School at South side. The population of the catchment area is about 30000-35000. People in the area are mostly dependent on shallow tubewell water for their daily uses and the average depth of water is 35- 40ft below the ground. The Nepaltali Union map indicating sub-project location has been shown respectively in Figure 1. The topographical Map with indicative and tentative location of labor Page | 183 [SOURCE: Page_225]

The existing Dhananjoy Government Primary School occupies 96 decimals of land, with a one- storied pucca building situated on the northern side and a semi-pucca school building on the western side that currently accommodate all classrooms and administrative offices. A Shaheed Minar and flag stand are located in front of the pucca building on the north. The proposed flood shelter is planned for construction on the eastern side of the school premises, with no demolition of existing structures required, ensuring that all academic and administrative activities will continue uninterrupted in the current facilities throughout the construction period. During this time, a temporary labour shed, materials storage area, and waste disposal site will be established on the northern side of the premises. There are local settlelment around the school area. The site is bounded to the south by the Chelopara–Shariakandi Road and to the north by the Sharkidah Khal canal while an additional access road, known as Dhananjoy Road, provides entry to the school. Derer Beel is located within 100 meters of the school area. A considerable number of trees exist within the school boundaries, of which only two will need to be removed. Figure 6 present photographs of the existing GPS facilities. [SOURCE: Page_228]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, June 2025) The proposed sub-project (construction of new School cum Flood shelter building) is not located within any environmentally sensitive area and will not cause any severe negative effects to the environmental settings of the area, neither to important environmental features. The disaster shelter will be constructed within an existing school boundary, so no agricultural land/ activities or fish farming will be disturbed due to the construction of the sub project. There are found some socio-environmental features such as Dhananjay Uttar Para Mosque/ Dhananjay Baytul Madrasha (300m), Kadamtali GPS (1km), Kadamtali High School (1km), Kadamtali Mosque (500m) on the North side of the proposed sub-project location. To the South, Dhananjay Madan Mohan Kali Temple (500m), Dhananjay Dakshin Para Mosque (300m), Teropakhi Mosque (400m), Nepaltali GPS/High School (1km) Nepaltali Bazar (1km) are found on from the sub- project component. Dhananjay Central Mosque (100m), Dhananjay Mandalpara Mosque (200m), Tekani Beel (300m) found on the East side from the sub-project component & Derer Beel (100m) is located on West side from the sub-project location. No significant disturbance to all these establishments/features is anticipated due to construction activities for having sufficient distance from the construction site, and strict construction site management system- including restrictive work schedule during the daytime only, water- sprinkling twice a day in and around the site, proper fencing around the working area, safe storage of materials, etc. Construction related activities and setting up of labor camps along with associated facilities and their management issues will be accounted for impacts more likely to be generated during the pre, post and construction period. Noise pollution from pilling or drilling, air pollution caused by dust or gaseous emissions from vehicle movement, running of motorized equipment and land clearing, odors and soil pollution from leaking of latrines and fecal sludge, will more likely to take place. Soil can further be eroded and polluted from chemical spills or improper disposal of waste materials. Noise and vibration effects generated from pilling and drilling may also trigger landslides and harmful disturbances to local fauna. Impact on surface and ground water bodies might get acute due mainly to the high abstraction rate and disposal/leakage of pollutants to the surface/ground water bodies. Clearing of trees, bushes or any type of vegetation may put impact on floral species and unscrupulous clearance also trigger habitat loss. All these impacts can only be prevented or minimized by adopting measures delineated into the ESMP and good practice [SOURCE: Page_229]

ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SCREENING This section identifies the potential impacts that the various elements of the proposed sub- project may have on the physical, biological and socio-economic environment within half a kilometer of the radial distance around the site. Environmental and Social Assessment (ESA) based on this screening study for the Sub-project as Dhananjay Government Primary School of Gabtali Upazila under Bogura District has been conducted to identify and determine which potential project impacts may be significant and therefore require the application of reasonable and effective management and/or mitigation measures. In order to realize the exact physical, biological and socio-economic environment of the proposed sub-project site and the influence area in regards to the implementation measures, an extensive field visit was carried out on 30 June 2025 in the Sub-project area. Environmental and Social Screening form, as adopted in Annexure-2 of the Environmental and Social Management Framework of RIVER, was administered for identifying the impacts and their extents. [SOURCE: Page_230]

PUBLIC CONSULTATION AND PARTICIPATION Public participation and community consultation has been taken up as an integral part of environmental assessment process of the project. Field visit has been carried out on 30 June 2025 in and around the Sub-project component site. As part of the impact assessment, participatory public consultation was conducted in that area by the field level staffs, and consultants from D&SC. Checklist of the consultation is attached in Annexure-3. The consultation meeting was attended by 76 persons (Male -10 and Female -66) and local individuals, teachers, chairman and/or member of Union Parishad and school management committee were among the attendees in that meeting. The participants were selected from different cohorts of stakeholders, and some of whom will have major active roles before, during and even after the construction works. Therefore, the meeting was organized in an informed, expressive and unbiased manner, wherefrom different views and concerns came across which will be properly taken care of during the design and construction phases. Refer to Figure 8 and Annexure-4 for selected photographs of the participatory public consultation held at site of the Dhananjay Government Primary School and list of attendees in that public consultation meeting, respectively. A questionnaire was kept ready and responses were elicited. During these consultations, the communities were explained about the project, its benefits, associated social and environmental aspects and possible mitigation measures. The participants were also informed about the project GRM (Grievance Redress Mechanism) system in detail and the disclosure of project documents in websites, and their unrestricted and uninitiated access to those system and resources. As such, public consultation is a living process as the types of problems/ difficulties, involved parties or stakeholders and mode of settlement or resolution processes are more likely to differ with time. Thus, consultation with different parties or stakeholders will be continued throughout the sub-project implementation period and [SOURCE: Page_230]

records of resolutions, whatsoever and wherever possible, will be kept in writing at the site and made available on any enquiries or requests by all parties concerned. [SOURCE: Page_231]

Figure 8: Public Consultation Meeting in the Proposed Sub-project Site SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACTS Overall Construction Related Impacts: The proposed construction works are expected to generate localized and temporary environmental and social impacts typical of small- to medium- scale civil works. Key environmental impacts include dust and air emissions, noise and vibration from machinery, construction waste generation, temporary soil disturbance, and minor vegetation loss during site preparation. There may also be risks of water and soil contamination from improper material handling or drainage obstruction. Social impacts are anticipated to be limited, involving temporary disruption of school activities, restricted access to playgrounds, increased traffic movement, and potential occupational health and safety risks for workers. However, no land acquisition, displacement, or impacts on ethnic or vulnerable communities are expected. Overall, the impacts are short-term, reversible, and confined within existing school premises, manageable through standard environmental and social mitigation practices. Tree Cutting: Approximately 2 trees (large size) are likely to be cut down and no water bodies are likely to be filled up due to the construction of the flood shelter. The ecological impact of the subproject is low. There will be temporary negative impacts on physico-chemical environment. Nevertheless, these impacts are manageable if mitigation measures are taken according to ESMP. Grass turfing: Grass turfs on embankment, slope, building compound & any critical place to enhance the ecological condition and protect the top soil. Tentative area of turf has been estimated as 240 square meters (half of total area), after discussion with architects and engineers. It is likely to be changed depending on the requirement during construction as per site design and as per direction of E.I.C. Land Ownership: Availability of adequate public land area is as important as community consent to construct the flood shelter and access roads. The D&S Survey team did not find any conflicts over the school land. The land issue has been discussed in the meeting. Participants unanimously confirmed that the school has its own 96 decimals of land and there is no dispute about this land. Land Acquisition: The proposed Sub-project, Dhananjay Government Primary School, does not Page | 189 [SOURCE: Page_231]

have any involuntary resettlement impacts due to the construction of flood shelter and approach roads as the Sub-projects will be constructed in existing Government Primary Schools’ premises. The Government Primary School has 96 decimals of land. No land acquisition will be required for the activities to be implemented under the project. LOCATION OF THE SUB-PROJECT The subproject is located in the Eastern part of Gabtali Upazila in Bogura District, which is within the Rajshahi Division. The location details of the subproject have been summarized in Table 2. Table 2: Location Details of the Subproject Site District                                           :    Bogura Upazila                                            :    Gabtali Union                                              :    Nepaltali Mouza                                              :    Dhananjoy Village                                            :    Uttar Kaludanga GPS Location                                       :    24.888802 N; 89.513545 E Distance of the site from Upazila HQ               :    8 km West Nearby Major Road:                                 :    Shariakandi-Bogura road: South side, Distance-1.5 km, Wide-30ft., BC road Nearby River/ Canal:                               :    Shukdaha River (East-500m) [SOURCE: Page_245]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, July 2025) The catchment area of the subproject mostly comprises of Kallyanpur, Kaludanga, Kushahata, Shalukgari villages which have been significantly affected by floods. Uttar Kaludanga, under Nepaltali Union of Gabtali Upazila, sits on the low-lying floodplain shaped by the Bangali– Karatoya–Jamuna River system. During the monsoon, heavy rainfall and upstream inflows raise water levels in these rivers; the Bangali River (now substantially fed by the Jamuna) spreads over adjacent floodplains and drainage channels, leading to seasonal inundation of low areas and damage to homes, roads, cropland, and local livelihoods. The upazila’s landscape includes several natural wetlands (beels) notably Charar Beel and others listed for Gabtali, and Burungi Beel within Nepaltali Union—which hold and slowly release floodwater, increasing local flood susceptibility while also supporting fisheries and agriculture. In short, Uttar Kaludanga’s flood hazard is driven by monsoon rainfall + Jamuna-fed River overflow across a beel-dotted, low- relief floodplain. These floods can severely disrupt agriculture, infrastructure, and local livelihoods. The flood shelter will be constructed at 59 No. Uttar Kaludanga Government Primary School (GPS), which is located at the Uttar Kaludanga village under Nepaltali Union of Gabtali Upazila in Bogura District. There are 6 teachers (Male: 3 & Female:3), and 131 students (Boys: 72; Girls: 59) in the school, operated by the guidance of School Management Committee (SMC) and government officials of Gabtali Upazila Education Office. The students, teachers and residents of the catchment area come to the proposed site by using the connecting/access road, Shabajpur to Kaludanga chowrasta road. The road is BC road with wide-10fit and just passing beside the 59 No. Uttar Kaludanga Government Primary School at West side. Page | 203 [SOURCE: Page_245]

Figure 5: Proposed Waste Disposal Area for the Subproject Site The existing 59 No. Uttar Kaludanga Government Primary School occupies 43 decimals of land, with a one-storied pucca building located on the northern side and a semi-pucca building on the western side that currently accommodate all classrooms and administrative offices. A Shaheed Minar is situated to the north, in front of the pucca building. The proposed flood shelter is planned for construction at the center of the school premises, requiring the demolition of existing structures, namely the old one-storied pucca building (19m × 9m) with toilet (6m × 0.6m) and the semi-pucca school building (24.3m × 10m). To ensure continuity of academic and administrative activities during the construction period, a temporary school shed will be provided. Additionally, a temporary labour shed will be set up on the south-western side, a materials storage area on the south-eastern side, and a waste disposal site on the eastern side of the premises. The school is bordered by a graveyard adjacent to the compound, a semi-pucca road on the south, and the Shukdoho River on the east, while access to the school is facilitated through Shahbazpur–Kaludanga Chowrasta Road. Kaludanga Beel is located within 500 meters of the school area. A significant number of trees exist within the school boundaries, though only one will need to be removed. Historical flood records indicate that the area was inundated during the 1998 flood, with water reaching a depth of 6 feet and persisting for 30 days, and again in 2019 when 3 feet of water remained for 14 days. Figure 6 and Figure 7 present photographs of the existing GPS facilities and condition of the demolished school building. [SOURCE: Page_248]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, July 2025) The proposed sub-project (construction of new School cum Flood shelter building) is not located within any environmentally sensitive area and will not cause any severe negative effects to the environmental settings of the area, neither to important environmental features. The disaster shelter will be constructed within an existing school boundary, so no agricultural land/ activities or fish farming will be disturbed due to the construction of the sub project. There are found some socio-environmental features such as; To the north lies Kallayanpur Emdadul Ulum Kaomi Madrasha (approx. 500 m). To the south, key receptors include a graveyard (approx. 90 m), a community clinic (approx. 100 m), and Kaludanga Beel (approx. 500 m). On the east side are Dhananjay Central Mosque (approx. 100 m), a graveyard adjacent to the school, Uttar Kaludanga Mosque (approx. 100 m), and the Shukdaha River (approx. 500 m). To the west, a Mahila Madrasha (approx. 80 m) and an Eidgah (approx. 100 m) are situated nearby from the sub- project location. No significant disturbance to all these establishments/features is anticipated due to construction activities for having sufficient distance from the construction site, and strict construction site management system- including restrictive work schedule during the daytime only, water- sprinkling twice a day in and around the site, proper fencing around the working area, safe storage of materials, etc. Construction related activities and setting up of labor camps along with associated facilities and their management issues will be accounted for impacts more likely to be generated during the pre, post and construction period. Noise pollution from pilling or drilling, air pollution caused by dust or gaseous emissions from vehicle movement, running of motorized equipment and land clearing, odors and soil pollution from leaking of latrines and fecal sludge, will more likely to take place. Soil can further be eroded and polluted from chemical spills or improper disposal of waste materials. Noise and vibration effects generated from pilling and drilling may also trigger landslides and harmful disturbances to local fauna. Impact on surface and ground water bodies might get acute due mainly to the high abstraction rate and disposal/leakage of pollutants to the surface/ground water bodies. Clearing of trees, bushes or any type of vegetation may put impact on floral species and unscrupulous clearance also trigger habitat loss. All these impacts can only be prevented or minimized by adopting measures delineated into the ESMP and good practice Page | 207 [SOURCE: Page_249]

ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SCREENING This section identifies the potential impacts that the various elements of the proposed sub- project may have on the physical, biological and socio-economic environment within half a kilometer of the radial distance around the site. Environmental and Social Assessment (ESA) based on this screening study for the Sub-project as 59 No. Uttar Kaludanga Government Primary School of Gabtali Upazila under Bogura District has been conducted to identify and determine which potential project impacts may be significant and therefore require the application of reasonable and effective management and/or mitigation measures. In order to realize the exact physical, biological and socio-economic environment of the proposed sub- project site and the influence area in regards to the implementation measures, an extensive field visit was carried out on 05 July 2025 in the Sub-project area. Environmental and Social Screening form, as adopted in Annexure-2 of the Environmental and Social Management Framework of RIVER, was administered for identifying the impacts and their extents. [SOURCE: Page_250]

PUBLIC CONSULTATION AND PARTICIPATION Public participation and community consultation has been taken up as an integral part of environmental assessment process of the project. Field visit has been carried out on 05 July 2025 in and around the Sub-project component site. As part of the impact assessment, participatory public consultation was conducted in that area by the field level staffs, and consultants from D&SC. Checklist of the consultation is attached in Annexure-3. The consultation meeting was attended by 33 persons (Male -30 and Female -3) and local individuals, teachers, chairman and/or member of Union Parishad and school management committee were among the attendees in that meeting. The participants were selected from different cohorts of stakeholders, and some of whom will have major active roles before, during and even after the construction works. Therefore, the meeting was organized in an informed, expressive and unbiased manner, wherefrom different views and concerns came across which will be properly taken care of during the design and construction phases. Refer to Figure 8 and Annexure-4 for selected photographs of the participatory public consultation held at site of the 59 No. Uttar Kaludanga Government Primary School and list of attendees in that public consultation meeting, respectively. A questionnaire was kept ready and responses were elicited. During these consultations, the communities were explained about the project, its benefits, associated social and environmental aspects and possible mitigation measures. The participants were also informed about the project GRM (Grievance Redress Mechanism) system in detail and the disclosure of project documents in websites, and their unrestricted and uninitiated access to those system and resources. As such, public consultation is a living process as the types of problems/ difficulties, involved parties or stakeholders and mode of settlement or resolution processes are more likely to differ with time. Thus, consultation with different parties or stakeholders will be continued throughout the sub-project implementation period and [SOURCE: Page_250]
