records of resolutions, whatsoever and wherever possible, will be kept in writing at the site and made available on any enquiries or requests by all parties concerned. [SOURCE: Page_251]

Figure 8: Public Consultation Meeting in the Proposed Sub-project Site SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACTS Overall Construction Related Impacts: The proposed construction works are expected to generate localized and temporary environmental and social impacts typical of small- to medium- scale civil works. Key environmental impacts include dust and air emissions, noise and vibration from machinery, construction waste generation, temporary soil disturbance, and minor vegetation loss during site preparation. There may also be risks of water and soil contamination from improper material handling or drainage obstruction. Social impacts are anticipated to be limited, involving temporary disruption of school activities, restricted access to playgrounds, increased traffic movement, and potential occupational health and safety risks for workers. However, no land acquisition, displacement, or impacts on ethnic or vulnerable communities are expected. Overall, the impacts are short-term, reversible, and confined within existing school premises, manageable through standard environmental and social mitigation practices. Tree Cutting: Approximately 1 tree is likely to be cut down and no water bodies are likely to be filled up due to the construction of the flood shelter. The ecological impact of the subproject is low. There will be temporary negative impacts on physico-chemical environment. Nevertheless, these impacts are manageable if mitigation measures are taken according to ESMP. Grass turfing: Grass turfs on embankment, slope, building compound & any critical place to enhance the ecological condition and protect the top soil. Tentative area of turf has been estimated as 240 square meters (half of total area), after discussion with architects and engineers. It is likely to be changed depending on the requirement during construction as per site design and as per direction of E.I.C. Land Ownership: Availability of adequate public land area is as important as community consent to construct the flood shelter and access roads. The D&S Survey team did not find any conflicts over the school land. The land issue has been discussed in the meeting. Participants unanimously confirmed that the school has its own 43 decimals of land and there is no dispute about this land. The subproject is located in the Northern part of Gabtali Upazila in Bogura District, which is within the Rajshahi Division. The location details of the subproject have been summarized in Table 2. Table 2: Location Details of the Subproject Site District                                          :    Bogura Upazila                                           :    Gabtali Union                                             :    Ramshanpur Mouza                                             :    Hosenpur Village                                           :    Hosenpur GPS Location                                      :    24.928539 N; 89.445757 E Distance of the site from Upazila HQ              :    6 km Nearby Major Road:                                :    Sonaray-Gabtoli road: South side, Distance-3.5 km, wide-4m, BC road [SOURCE: Page_265]

Nearby River/ Canal:                              :    Ichamati River (East-200m) [SOURCE: Page_265]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, June 2025) The catchment area of the subproject mostly comprises of Noshkuri para, Taiyer para, Jaguli, Tatura, Moddyamer chew, Rameshwarpur villages which have been significantly affected by floods. Hosenpur—a village under Rameshwarpur Union in Gabtali Upazila—lies on Bogura’s low-lying eastern alluvial tract, where rivers and wetlands make the area naturally flood-prone. Seasonal flooding here is driven largely by the Jamuna’s monsoon dynamics and by its hydraulically connected floodplain rivers—especially the Bangali, which links to the Jamuna within Bogura—so overbank flows during heavy rains spread across adjacent floodplains and drainage channels. The upazila also contains numerous beels (natural wetlands)—including Charar Beel and others—that store and slowly release water, increasing flood susceptibility of surrounding settlements and cropland. As a result, intense monsoon rainfall plus river overflow routinely inundates low-lying areas, disrupting roads, homes, agriculture, and local livelihoods. The flood shelter will be constructed at 26 No. Hosenpur Government Primary School (GPS), which is located at the Hosenpur village under Rameshwarpur Union of Gabtali Upazila in Bogura District. There are 7 teachers (Male:2 & Female:5), and 189 students (Boys: 100; Girls: 89) in the school, operated by the guidance of School Management Committee (SMC) and government officials of Gabtali Upazila Education Office. The students, teachers and residents of the catchment area come to the proposed site by using the connecting/access road, Hosenpur stand to WBM road. The road is BC road with wide-3meter and just passing beside the 26 No. Hosenpur Government Primary School at East side. The population of the catchment area is about 30,000-32,000. The local population is largely dependent on shallow tubewell water for daily use, with the average groundwater depth ranging [SOURCE: Page_265]

The existing 26 No. Hosenpur Government Primary School occupies 49 decimals of land, with two one-storied pucca buildings located on the southern side that currently accommodate all classrooms and administrative offices. A Shaheed Minar is situated to the east of the premises. The proposed flood shelter is planned for construction on the south-western side, requiring the demolition of existing structures, namely one old one-storied pucca building measuring 16.3m × 8.0m and another measuring 18.8m × 8.0m with an attached toilet (2.3m × 1.7m). To ensure that academic and administrative activities continue uninterrupted throughout the construction period, a temporary school shed will be established. In addition, a temporary labour shed and materials storage area will be located on the eastern side, with a waste disposal site positioned on the north-western side of the premises. The school is bordered by a graveyard to the south- west and a mosque to the east, with pucca roads from both the north and east. The Ichamoti River lies approximately 200 meters east of the site, while Korchar Beel and Chorar Beel are each located about 1 kilometer away, and Gozar Beel is situated within 500 meters of the school area. A local settlement with a pucca building is located adjacent to the school premises. A considerable number of trees are present within the school boundaries, though only three will need to be removed. Historical flood records indicate that the area was inundated during the 1988 flood, when water reached a depth of 3 feet and remained for 10 to 12 days. Figure 6 and Figure 7 present photographs of the existing GPS facilities and condition of the demolished school building. [SOURCE: Page_268]

Figure 6: Existing school Building                         Figure 7: Demolished school Building [SOURCE: Page_268]

Direction                      Important Establishments with Approximate Distance North side    Family Graveyard (500m), Noshkuripara Mosque (750m), Noshkuripara Nurani Hafezia Madrasha (800m), Noshkuripara GPS (450m), Noshkuripara Central Mosque (750m), Ichamati River (1km), Noshkuripara Vanga (1km) South side    Hosenpur Kaomi Madrasa (500m), Hosenpur Mosque (550m), Ichamati River (1km), Korchar Beel (1km), Taher Para GPS (700m) East side     Ichamati River (200m), Gozar Beel (500m), Hosenpur Central Mosque (500m) West side     Mathpara Mosque (500m), Eidgah (550), Hosenpur Graveyard (1km), Jaguli Bazar (800m), Jaguli Mosque (1km), Khanbari Hafizia Madrasa (1km), Jaguli Community Clinic / Jaguli GPS/ Jaguli Dimukhi High School (1km) (Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, June 2025) The proposed sub-project (construction of new School cum Flood shelter building) is not located within any environmentally sensitive area and will not cause any severe negative effects to the environmental settings of the area, neither to important environmental features. The disaster shelter will be constructed within an existing school boundary, so no agricultural land/ activities or fish farming will be disturbed due to the construction of the sub project. The project area is surrounded by a variety of religious, educational, and community landmarks in all four directions. To the north, the Family Graveyard is located about 500 meters away, while the Noshkuripara Mosque and Noshkuripara Central Mosque are both situated within 750 meters. The Noshkuripara Nurani Hafezia Madrasha lies 800 meters away, and the Noshkuripara GPS is closer at 450 meters. The Ichamati River flows at a distance of 1 kilometer, alongside Noshkuripara Vanga at the same distance. On the southern side, Hosenpur Kaomi Madrasa is 500 meters away, with Hosenpur Mosque at 550 meters. The Ichamati River and Korchar Beel are both situated approximately 1 kilometer to the south, while Taher Para GPS is positioned 700 meters away. Towards the east, Hosenpur Central Mosque is located 500 meters from the site, the Ichamati River flows just 200 meters away, and Gozar Beel lies 500 meters to the east. On the western side, Mathpara Mosque is 500 meters away, with an Eidgah located 550 meters from the area. Further west, Hosenpur Graveyard is at a distance of 1 kilometer, while Jaguli Bazar lies 800 meters away. Other key institutions in the west include Jaguli Mosque, Khanbari Hafizia Madrasa, Jaguli Community Clinic, Jaguli GPS, and Jaguli Dimukhi High School, all located within approximately 1 kilometer. Collectively, these landmarks highlight the presence of strong religious, educational, and communal infrastructure around the site, supported by natural features such as rivers and wetlands. No significant disturbance to all these establishments/features is anticipated due to construction activities for having sufficient distance from the construction site, and strict construction site management system- including restrictive work schedule during the daytime only, water- [SOURCE: Page_269]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_270]

sprinkling twice a day in and around the site, proper fencing around the working area, safe storage of materials, etc. Construction related activities and setting up of labor camps along with associated facilities and their management issues will be accounted for impacts more likely to be generated during the pre, post and construction period. Noise pollution from pilling or drilling, air pollution caused by dust or gaseous emissions from vehicle movement, running of motorized equipment and land clearing, odors and soil pollution from leaking of latrines and fecal sludge, will more likely to take place. Soil can further be eroded and polluted from chemical spills or improper disposal of waste materials. Noise and vibration effects generated from pilling and drilling may also trigger landslides and harmful disturbances to local fauna. Impact on surface and ground water bodies might get acute due mainly to the high abstraction rate and disposal/leakage of pollutants to the surface/ground water bodies. Clearing of trees, bushes or any type of vegetation may put impact on floral species and unscrupulous clearance also trigger habitat loss. All these impacts can only be prevented or minimized by adopting measures delineated into the ESMP and good practice engineering and site management. ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SCREENING This section identifies the potential impacts that the various elements of the proposed sub- project may have on the physical, biological and socio-economic environment within half a kilometer of the radial distance around the site. Environmental and Social Assessment (ESA) based on this screening study for the Sub-project as 26 No. Hosenpur Government Primary School of Gabtali Upazila under Bogura District has been conducted to identify and determine which potential project impacts may be significant and therefore require the application of reasonable and effective management and/or mitigation measures. In order to realize the exact physical, biological and socio-economic environment of the proposed sub-project site and the influence area in regards to the implementation measures, an extensive field visit was carried out on 29 June 2025 in the Sub-project area. Environmental and Social Screening form, as adopted in Annexure-2 of the Environmental and Social Management Framework of RIVER, was administered for identifying the impacts and their extents. [SOURCE: Page_270]

PUBLIC CONSULTATION AND PARTICIPATION Public participation and community consultation has been taken up as an integral part of environmental assessment process of the project. Field visit has been carried out on 29 June 2025 in and around the Sub-project component site. As part of the impact assessment, participatory public consultation was conducted in that area by the field level staffs, and consultants from D&SC. Checklist of the consultation is attached in Annexure-3. The consultation meeting was attended by 33 persons (Male -20 and Female -13) and local individuals, teachers, chairman and/or member of Union Parishad and school management committee were among the attendees in that meeting. The participants were selected from different cohorts of stakeholders, and some of whom will have major active roles before, during and even after the construction works. Therefore, the meeting was organized in an informed, [SOURCE: Page_270]

Page | 228 [SOURCE: Page_270]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_271]

expressive and unbiased manner, wherefrom different views and concerns came across which will be properly taken care of during the design and construction phases. Refer to Figure 8 and Annexure-4 for selected photographs of the participatory public consultation held at site of the 26 No. Hosenpur Government Primary School and list of attendees in that public consultation meeting, respectively. A questionnaire was kept ready and responses were elicited. During these consultations, the communities were explained about the project, its benefits, associated social and environmental aspects and possible mitigation measures. The participants were also informed about the project GRM (Grievance Redress Mechanism) system in detail and the disclosure of project documents in websites, and their unrestricted and uninitiated access to those system and resources. As such, public consultation is a living process as the types of problems/ difficulties, involved parties or stakeholders and mode of settlement or resolution processes are more likely to differ with time. Thus, consultation with different parties or stakeholders will be continued throughout the sub-project implementation period and records of resolutions, whatsoever and wherever possible, will be kept in writing at the site and made available on any enquiries or requests by all parties concerned. [SOURCE: Page_271]

Figure 8: Public Consultation Meeting in the Proposed Sub-project Site SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACTS Overall Construction Related Impacts: The proposed construction works are expected to generate localized and temporary environmental and social impacts typical of small- to medium- scale civil works. Key environmental impacts include dust and air emissions, noise and vibration from machinery, construction waste generation, temporary soil disturbance, and minor vegetation loss during site preparation. There may also be risks of water and soil contamination from improper material handling or drainage obstruction. Social impacts are anticipated to be limited, involving temporary disruption of school activities, restricted access to playgrounds, increased traffic movement, and potential occupational health and safety risks for workers. However, no land acquisition, displacement, or impacts on ethnic or vulnerable communities are expected. Overall, the impacts are short-term, reversible, and confined within existing school premises, manageable through standard environmental and social mitigation practices. Tree Cutting: Approximately 3 trees (medium/large size) are likely to be cut down and no water bodies are likely to be filled up due to the construction of the flood shelter. The ecological impact of the subproject is low. There will be temporary negative impacts on physico-chemical environment. Nevertheless, these impacts are manageable if mitigation measures are taken Page | 229 [SOURCE: Page_271]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_272]

according to ESMP. Grass turfing: Grass turfs on embankment, slope, building compound & any critical place to enhance the ecological condition and protect the top soil. Tentative area of turf has been estimated as 240 square meters (half of total area), after discussion with architects and engineers. It is likely to be changed depending on the requirement during construction as per site design and as per direction of E.I.C. Land Ownership: Availability of adequate public land area is as important as community consent to construct the flood shelter and access roads. The D&S Survey team did not find any conflicts over the school land. The land issue has been discussed in the meeting. Participants unanimously confirmed that the school has its own 49 decimals of land and there is no dispute about this land. Land Acquisition: The proposed Sub-project, 26 No. Hosenpur Government Primary School, does not have any involuntary resettlement impacts due to the construction of flood shelter and approach roads as the Sub-projects will be constructed in existing Government Primary Schools’ premises. The Government Primary School has 49 decimals of land. No land acquisition will be required for the activities to be implemented under the project. Access road needs to construct or rehabilitate within its existing alignment. LOCATION OF THE SUB-PROJECT The subproject is located in the Northern part of Gabtali Upazila in Bogura District, which is within the Rajshahi Division. The location details of the subproject have been summarized in Table 2. Table 2: Location Details of the Subproject Site District                                         :     Bogura Upazila                                          :     Gabtali Union                                            :     Sonarai Mouza                                            :     Jamirbaria Village                                          :     Jamirbaria GPS Location                                     :     24.971019 N; 89.445748 E Distance of the site from Upazila HQ             :     12 km Nearby Major Road:                               :     12ft. wide BC Jamirbaria-Gabtoli Road at South side Nearby River/ Canal:                             :     Gazaria River (East-350m) [SOURCE: Page_286]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, June 2025) The catchment area of the subproject mostly comprises of Jamirbaria Buritola, Hatkhola para, Dikdai, Parabaisha, Fupidori para, Fupi moddya para, Fupi Mondal para, Fupi Dakshin para, Karim para, Jamirbaria Dharmatola, Ager para- villages which have been significantly affected by floods. Jamirbaria —a village under Sonarai Union in Gabtali Upazila— lies on the low-lying floodplain of the Jamuna–Bangali river system. Seasonal flooding is driven by the Jamuna’s monsoon behavior and its hydraulic linkage to the Bangali River, so heavy rainfall and upstream inflows trigger overbank spread across shallow floodplains and drainage channels. The upazila also contains numerous beels (natural wetlands)—notably Charar Beel—that store and slowly release monsoon water, increasing flood susceptibility of adjacent settlements and cropland. As a result, intense monsoon rainfall plus river overflow routinely inundates low-lying areas, disrupting roads, homes, agriculture, and local livelihoods. The flood shelter will be constructed at 32 No.Jamirbaria Burital Government Primary School (GPS), which is located at the Jamirbaria village under Sonarai Union of Gabtali Upazila in Bogura District. There are 4 teachers (Male:3 & Female:1), and 126 students (Boys: 60; Girls: 66) in the school, operated by the guidance of School Management Committee (SMC) and government officials of Gabtali Upazila Education Office. The students, teachers and residents of the catchment area come to the proposed site by using the connecting/access road, 32 No.Jamirbaria Burital GPS. The population of the catchment area is about 20,000-22,000. Most residents in the area rely on shallow tubewells to meet their daily water needs, with groundwater generally found at an Page | 244 [SOURCE: Page_286]

The existing 32 No. Jamirbaria Burital Government Primary School occupies 33 decimals of land, comprising two one-storied GPS buildings—one located on the northern side and the other on the western side—which currently accommodate all classrooms and administrative offices. The proposed flood shelter is planned for construction on the western side of the premises, requiring the demolition of the existing western building measuring 16.2m × 8.5m. During the construction period, all academic and administrative activities will continue in the northern building. Temporary facilities, including a labour shed, materials storage area, and waste disposal site, will be established on the eastern side of the premises. [SOURCE: Page_289]

The school is bordered to the south by the Jamirbaria–Gabtoli BC Road (12 feet wide), which runs adjacent to the school, while the Sharkidah Khal canal lies to the north. Six trees are located within the school boundaries; however, none will need to be removed. A water body and a semi- pucca building are situated directly to the north of the school, though they will not obstruct the construction process. Within a 1 km radius of the school are several local settlements, along with a mosque, eidgah, mandir, beels, a community clinic, and a bazar. Historical flood records show that the area was inundated in 1988, when floodwaters reached a depth of 5 feet and remained for 10 days. Figure 6 and Figure 7 present photographs of the existing GPS facilities and condition of the demolished school building. [SOURCE: Page_289]

meters away, with Khupidori Para Mosque at 320 meters, Khupi Mondol Para Mosque/Madrasa at 500 meters, and Khupi Community Clinic at about 650 meters. Altogether, the site is surrounded by a rich mix of religious, cultural, educational, and natural landmarks, reflecting a well-developed community infrastructure in the Jamirbaria area. No significant disturbance to all these establishments/features is anticipated due to construction activities for having sufficient distance from the construction site, and strict construction site management system- including restrictive work schedule during the daytime only, water- sprinkling twice a day in and around the site, proper fencing around the working area, safe storage of materials, etc. Construction related activities and setting up of labor camps along with associated facilities and their management issues will be accounted for impacts more likely to be generated during the pre, post and construction period. Noise pollution from pilling or drilling, air pollution caused by dust or gaseous emissions from vehicle movement, running of motorized equipment and land clearing, odors and soil pollution from leaking of latrines and fecal sludge, will more likely to take place. Soil can further be eroded and polluted from chemical spills or improper disposal of waste materials. Noise and vibration effects generated from pilling and drilling may also trigger landslides and harmful disturbances to local fauna. Impact on surface and ground water bodies might get acute due mainly to the high abstraction rate and disposal/leakage of pollutants to the surface/ground water bodies. Clearing of trees, bushes or any type of vegetation may put impact on floral species and unscrupulous clearance also trigger habitat loss. All these impacts can only be prevented or minimized by adopting measures delineated into the ESMP and good practice engineering and site management. ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SCREENING This section identifies the potential impacts that the various elements of the proposed sub- project may have on the physical, biological and socio-economic environment within half a kilometer of the radial distance around the site. Environmental and Social Assessment (ESA) based on this screening study for the Sub-project as 32 No. Jamirbaria Burital Government Primary School of Gabtali Upazila under Bogura District has been conducted to identify and determine which potential project impacts may be significant and therefore require the application of reasonable and effective management and/or mitigation measures. In order to realize the exact physical, biological and socio-economic environment of the proposed sub- project site and the influence area in regards to the implementation measures, an extensive field visit was carried out on 29 June 2025 in the Sub-project area. Environmental and Social Screening form, as adopted in Annexure-2 of the Environmental and Social Management Framework of RIVER, was administered for identifying the impacts and their extents. [SOURCE: Page_291]

PUBLIC CONSULTATION AND PARTICIPATION Public participation and community consultation has been taken up as an integral part of environmental assessment process of the project. Field visit has been carried out on 29 June 2025 in and around the Sub-project component site. As part of the impact assessment, [SOURCE: Page_291]

Page | 249 [SOURCE: Page_291]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_292]

participatory public consultation was conducted in that area by the field level staffs, and consultants from D&SC. Checklist of the consultation is attached in Annexure-3. The consultation meeting was attended by 24 persons (Male -15 and Female -09) and local individuals, teachers, chairman and/or member of Union Parishad and school management committee were among the attendees in that meeting. The participants were selected from different cohorts of stakeholders, and some of whom will have major active roles before, during and even after the construction works. Therefore, the meeting was organized in an informed, expressive and unbiased manner, wherefrom different views and concerns came across which will be properly taken care of during the design and construction phases. Refer to Figure 8 and Annexure-4 for selected photographs of the participatory public consultation held at site of the 32 No. Jamirbaria Burital Government Primary School and list of attendees in that public consultation meeting, respectively. A questionnaire was kept ready and responses were elicited. During these consultations, the communities were explained about the project, its benefits, associated social and environmental aspects and possible mitigation measures. The participants were also informed about the project GRM (Grievance Redress Mechanism) system in detail and the disclosure of project documents in websites, and their unrestricted and uninitiated access to those system and resources. As such, public consultation is a living process as the types of problems/ difficulties, involved parties or stakeholders and mode of settlement or resolution processes are more likely to differ with time. Thus, consultation with different parties or stakeholders will be continued throughout the sub-project implementation period and records of resolutions, whatsoever and wherever possible, will be kept in writing at the site and made available on any enquiries or requests by all parties concerned. Key environmental impacts include dust and air emissions, noise and vibration from machinery, construction waste generation, temporary soil disturbance, and minor vegetation loss during site preparation. There may also be risks of water and soil contamination from improper material handling or drainage obstruction. Social impacts are anticipated to be limited, involving temporary disruption of school activities, restricted access to playgrounds, increased traffic movement, and potential occupational health and safety risks for workers. However, no land acquisition, displacement, or impacts on ethnic or vulnerable communities are [SOURCE: Page_292]

There will be temporary negative impacts on physico-chemical environment. Nevertheless, these impacts are manageable if mitigation measures are taken according to ESMP. Grass turfing: Grass turfs on embankment, slope, building compound & any critical place to enhance the ecological condition and protect the top soil. Tentative area of turf has been estimated as 240 square meters (half of total area), after discussion with architects and engineers. Land Acquisition: The proposed Sub-project, 32 No. Jamirbaria Burital Government Primary School, does not have any involuntary resettlement impacts due to the construction of flood shelter and approach roads as the Sub-projects will be constructed in existing Government Primary Schools’ premises. The Government Primary School has 33 decimals of land. No land acquisition will be required for the activities to be implemented under the project. Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_306]

The subproject is located in the Eastern part of Gabtali Upazila in Bogura District, which is within the Rajshahi Division. The location details of the subproject have been summarized in Table 2. Table 2: Location Details of the Subproject Site District                                           :    Bogura Upazila                                            :    Gabtali Union                                              :    Sukhan Pukur Mouza                                              :    Nij Kakra Village                                            :    Kajlapara GPS Location                                       :    24.91365 N; 89.499211 E Distance of the site from Upazila HQ               :    14 km Nearby Major Road:                                 :    12ft. wide BC Sukhanpukur rail station-Shabajpur road at East-West Side Nearby River/ Canal:                               :    Kakra Khal (West-300m), Kajli Khal (East-500m) [SOURCE: Page_306]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, July 2025) The catchment area of the subproject mostly comprises of Kajlapara, Niz kakra, Momin hata, Par kakra, Kadomtoli, Soratoli, Dholir char, Kismotkakra villages which have been significantly affected by floods. Kajlapara (Sukhanpukur Union, Gabtali Upazila, Bogura) lies in the low-lying floodplain east of the Karatoya, where canals (khals) and natural wetlands (beels) make the area inherently flood-prone. Seasonal flooding here is driven by heavy monsoon rainfall and the behavior of the Jamuna–Bangali–Karatoya river system: Bogura’s “eastern alluvial tract” is generally low-lying and intersected by numerous khals, with annual overflows depositing silt yet raising flood risk; in recent decades the Jamuna has become a primary source of flow for the Bangali, enhancing overbank spread across adjacent floodplains and drainage channels in Gabtali. Within Gabtali, multiple rivers and notable beels (e.g., Charar Beel) store and slowly release monsoon water, which helps fisheries but also prolongs local inundation—so roads, homesteads, cropland and livelihoods in and around Kajlapara are routinely disrupted during peak monsoon. The flood shelter will be constructed at 53 No. Kajlapara Government Primary School (GPS), which is located at the Kajlapara village under Sukhan Pukur Union of Gabtali Upazila in Bogura District. There are 4 teachers, and 81 students (Boys: 43; Girls: 38) in the school, operated by the guidance of School Management Committee (SMC) and government officials of Gabtali Upazila Education Office. The students, teachers and residents of the catchment area come to the proposed site by using the connecting/access road named 53 No. Kajlapara GPS road. [SOURCE: Page_306]

The population of the catchment area is about 28,000-30,000. The local population primarily depends on shallow tubewells for their everyday water usage, with groundwater typically available at a depth ranging between 130 and 150 feet below ground level. The Sukhan Pukur Page | 264 [SOURCE: Page_306]

The existing 53 No. Kajlapara Government Primary School spans 61 decimals of land and consists of a one-storied pucca building on the northern side and a semi-pucca tin-shed structure on the western side, both currently serving as classrooms and administrative offices. A Shaheed Minar is located on the southern boundary. The proposed flood shelter is to be built on the northern side, which will require the demolition of both existing buildings—the pucca structure (19m × 9.4m) and the tin-shed structure (16.4m × 8.4m)—as well as the toilet block on the east (1.9m × 1.6m). During the construction phase, academic and administrative activities will continue in a temporary shed to be erected for this purpose. Additional temporary facilities, including a labour shed, materials storage area, and a waste disposal site, will be set up on the eastern side of the school compound. Although the premises contain a large number of trees of different sizes, only five will need to be removed. The school is directly connected to a pucca road on the south, and a new access road of approximately 70 meters will also be required. Within a 1 km radius, there are several local settlements along with a mosque, eidgah, graveyard, beels, and a pond. Historical flood records indicate that in 1988 the area was submerged, with water levels rising to 4 feet and remaining for 30 days. Figure 6 and Figure 7 present photographs of the existing GPS facilities and condition of the demolished school building. [SOURCE: Page_309]

Direction                      Important Establishments with Approximate Distance North side     Kajlapara-Madhya Para Mosque (300m), Kajlapara-Akandabari Mosque (500m), Nayapara Mosque (900m) South side     Kajlapara Central Mosque (300m), Al-Madina Mosque (500m), Dakshin Kajlapara Mosque (550m), Eidgah Math (560m) Kajlapara Family Graveyard (200m), Pond (700m), Boyarmari Beel (1km) East side      Kajlapara Eidgah Math (350m), Kajla Beel (350m), West side      Kakra Beel (100m) [SOURCE: Page_310]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, July 2025) The proposed sub-project (construction of new School cum Flood shelter building) is not located within any environmentally sensitive area and will not cause any severe negative effects to the environmental settings of the area, neither to important environmental features. The disaster shelter will be constructed within an existing school boundary, so no agricultural land/ activities or fish farming will be disturbed due to the construction of the sub project. The project site is surrounded by a number of notable landmarks in all directions. To the north, Kajlapara-Madhya Para Mosque is located 300 meters away, followed by Kajlapara-Akandabari Mosque at 500 meters and Nayapara Mosque at about 900 meters. On the southern side, important landmarks include Kajlapara Central Mosque (300 meters), Al-Madina Mosque (500 meters), and Dakshin Kajlapara Mosque (550 meters). An Eidgah Math lies at 560 meters, while the Kajlapara Family Graveyard is only 200 meters away. Additionally, a pond is situated 700 meters south, and Boyarmari Beel is located about 1 kilometer away. Towards the east, Kajlapara Eidgah Math and Kajla Beel are both found at a distance of 350 meters. On the western side, Kakra Beel is located closest, only 100 meters from the site. Together, these landmarks highlight the presence of strong religious, cultural, and natural features surrounding the area. No significant disturbance to all these establishments/features is anticipated due to construction activities for having sufficient distance from the construction site, and strict construction site management system- including restrictive work schedule during the daytime only, water- sprinkling twice a day in and around the site, proper fencing around the working area, safe storage of materials, etc. Construction related activities and setting up of labor camps along with associated facilities and their management issues will be accounted for impacts more likely to be generated during the pre, post and construction period. Noise pollution from pilling or drilling, air pollution caused by dust or gaseous emissions from vehicle movement, running of motorized equipment and land clearing, odors and soil pollution from leaking of latrines and fecal sludge, will more likely to take place. Soil can further be eroded and polluted from chemical spills or improper disposal of waste materials. Noise and vibration effects generated from pilling and drilling may also trigger [SOURCE: Page_310]

Page | 268 [SOURCE: Page_310]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_311]

landslides and harmful disturbances to local fauna. Impact on surface and ground water bodies might get acute due mainly to the high abstraction rate and disposal/leakage of pollutants to the surface/ground water bodies. Clearing of trees, bushes or any type of vegetation may put impact on floral species and unscrupulous clearance also trigger habitat loss. All these impacts can only be prevented or minimized by adopting measures delineated into the ESMP and good practice engineering and site management. ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SCREENING This section identifies the potential impacts that the various elements of the proposed sub- project may have on the physical, biological and socio-economic environment within half a kilometer of the radial distance around the site. Environmental and Social Assessment (ESA) based on this screening study for the Sub-project as 53 No. Kajlapara Government Primary School of Gabtali Upazila under Bogura District has been conducted to identify and determine which potential project impacts may be significant and therefore require the application of reasonable and effective management and/or mitigation measures. In order to realize the exact physical, biological and socio-economic environment of the proposed sub-project site and the influence area in regards to the implementation measures, an extensive field visit was carried out on 05 July 2025 in the Sub-project area. Environmental and Social Screening form, as adopted in Annexure-2 of the Environmental and Social Management Framework of RIVER, was administered for identifying the impacts and their extents. [SOURCE: Page_311]

PUBLIC CONSULTATION AND PARTICIPATION Public participation and community consultation has been taken up as an integral part of environmental assessment process of the project. Field visit has been carried out on 05 July 2025 in and around the Sub-project component site. As part of the impact assessment, participatory public consultation was conducted in that area by the field level staffs, and consultants from D&SC. Checklist of the consultation is attached in Annexure-3. The consultation meeting was attended by 49 persons (Male -37 and Female -12) and local individuals, teachers, chairman and/or member of Union Parishad and school management committee were among the attendees in that meeting. The participants were selected from different cohorts of stakeholders, and some of whom will have major active roles before, during and even after the construction works. Therefore, the meeting was organized in an informed, expressive and unbiased manner, wherefrom different views and concerns came across which will be properly taken care of during the design and construction phases. Refer to Figure 8 and Annexure-4 for selected photographs of the participatory public consultation held at site of the 53 No. Kajlapara Government Primary School and list of attendees in that public consultation meeting, respectively. A questionnaire was kept ready and responses were elicited. During these consultations, the communities were explained about the project, its benefits, associated social and environmental aspects and possible mitigation measures. The participants were also informed about the project GRM (Grievance Redress Mechanism) system in detail and the disclosure of project documents in websites, and their unrestricted and [SOURCE: Page_311]

Page | 269 [SOURCE: Page_311]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_312]

uninitiated access to those system and resources. As such, public consultation is a living process as the types of problems/ difficulties, involved parties or stakeholders and mode of settlement or resolution processes are more likely to differ with time. Thus, consultation with different parties or stakeholders will be continued throughout the sub-project implementation period and records of resolutions, whatsoever and wherever possible, will be kept in writing at the site and made available on any enquiries or requests by all parties concerned. [SOURCE: Page_312]

Figure 8: Public Consultation Meeting in the Proposed Sub-project Site SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACTS Overall Construction Related Impacts: The proposed construction works are expected to generate localized and temporary environmental and social impacts typical of small- to medium- scale civil works. Key environmental impacts include dust and air emissions, noise and vibration from machinery, construction waste generation, temporary soil disturbance, and minor vegetation loss during site preparation. There may also be risks of water and soil contamination from improper material handling or drainage obstruction. Social impacts are anticipated to be limited, involving temporary disruption of school activities, restricted access to playgrounds, increased traffic movement, and potential occupational health and safety risks for workers. However, no land acquisition, displacement, or impacts on ethnic or vulnerable communities are expected. Overall, the impacts are short-term, reversible, and confined within existing school premises, manageable through standard environmental and social mitigation practices. Tree Cutting: Approximately 5 trees (large size) are likely to be cut down and no water bodies are likely to be filled up due to the construction of the flood shelter. The ecological impact of the subproject is low. There will be temporary negative impacts on physico-chemical environment. Nevertheless, these impacts are manageable if mitigation measures are taken according to ESMP. Grass turfing: Grass turfs on embankment, slope, building compound & any critical place to enhance the ecological condition and protect the top soil. Tentative area of turf has been estimated as 240 square meters (half of total area), after discussion with architects and engineers. It is likely to be changed depending on the requirement during construction as per site design and as per direction of E.I.C. Land Ownership: Availability of adequate public land area is as important as community consent to construct the flood shelter and access roads. The D&S Survey team did not find any conflicts [SOURCE: Page_312]

Page | 270 [SOURCE: Page_312]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_313]

over the school land. The land issue has been discussed in the meeting. Participants unanimously confirmed that the school has its own 61 decimals of land and there is no dispute about this land. Land Acquisition: The proposed Sub-project, 53 No. Kajlapara Government Primary School, does not have any involuntary resettlement impacts due to the construction of flood shelter and approach roads as the Sub-projects will be constructed in existing Government Primary Schools’ premises. The Government Primary School has 61 decimals of land. No land acquisition will be required for the activities to be implemented under the project. Access road needs to construct or rehabilitate within its existing alignment. Considering the impacts identified at this particular school site, the site-specific Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) may be outlined as follows: [SOURCE: Page_313]

## SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL FINDINGS AS WELL AS ESMP IN SHARIAKANDI UPAZILA, BOGURA DISTRICT

1. Existing Geographical and Environmental Conditions of Shariakandi Upazila Shariakandi Upazila, situated on the eastern edge of Bogura District, lies along the Jamuna River floodplain and is highly vulnerable to recurrent seasonal flooding, riverbank erosion, and water logging. The upazila consists of fertile alluvial soils deposited by the Brahmaputra-Jamuna River system, which makes it agriculturally productive but also susceptible to erosion and flooding hazards. Topographically, the area is flat, with low-lying lands and depressions that act as temporary water retention basins during the monsoon. From a safeguard perspective, Shariakandi is considered environmentally sensitive due to the fragile riverbank ecosystems, floodplain biodiversity, and dependence of local communities on agriculture and fishing. Safeguard concerns in the area include: (i) risks of displacement due to bank erosion, (ii) contamination of drinking water during floods, (iii) seasonal loss of livelihood, and (iv) vulnerability of schools and rural infrastructure to natural hazards. [SOURCE: Page_325]

2. Drinking water quality status of Shariakandi Upazila The drinking water quality status in Shariakandi varies across unions. Groundwater extracted through shallow and deep tube wells is the main source of drinking water. While most tube wells provide water within acceptable standards, some areas show elevated levels of iron, manganese, and turbidity, while arsenic presence is generally low compared to southern districts (DPHE, 2022). During floods, many shallow tube wells are submerged, leading to contamination and reliance on surface water or temporary supplies, raising significant health risks. Groundwater quality: pH-5.17 to 8.51, DO-2.26 to 8.14mg/l, TDS-23.40 to 320 mg/l, EC -25.7 to 681μs/cm, Fe-0.6 to 3.3 mg/l and As-0.015-0.121mg/l (DPHE Test Result, 2025). 3. Sub-Project Location and Scope Under the RIVER Project, a total of 9 flood shelters are proposed to be constructed in Shariakandi Upazila across 4 unions. These shelters will serve as multipurpose facilities, functioning as schools in normal times and as disaster shelters during floods and other emergencies. The distribution of sites is as follows:    Fulbari Union – 4 sites    Kutubpur Union – 2 sites    Narchi Union – 2 sites    Shariakandi Union – 1 site [SOURCE: Page_325]

Stakeholder Consultation and GRC Formation Stakeholder consultations were conducted with local communities, Union Parishad representatives, teachers, school management committees, women’s groups, and vulnerable households etc. The consultations revealed strong community support for the project due to its role in reducing flood vulnerability, ensuring safety, and providing educational infrastructure. Key community concerns included:    Preservation of local water bodies during site filling.    Assurance of safe drinking water and sanitation facilities in shelters.    Minimizing dust, noise, and traffic disturbances during construction.    Local employment opportunities during construction phase. 5. Important Cultural, Archaeological, and Environmentally Sensitive Sites Screening of the sub-project sites did not identify any archaeological heritage sites or nationally protected cultural structures within the immediate project influence area. However, several mosques, temples, and graveyards are located near villages and require careful attention to avoid disturbances during construction. From an environmental standpoint, the sites are located in floodplain ecosystems where small wetlands, homestead vegetation, and agricultural biodiversity (paddy fields, seasonal crops) are present. These sensitive resources could be impacted by indiscriminate clearing, filling, or material storage. The Jamuna riverbank near some sites is highly erosion-prone and needs specific attention during earthworks. [SOURCE: Page_327]

LOCATION OF THE SUB-PROJECT The subproject is located in the South-West part of Shariakandi Upazila in Bogura District, which is within the Rajshahi Division. The location details of the subproject have been summarized in Table 2. Table 2: Location Details of the Subproject Site District                                          :    Bogura Upazila                                           :    Shariakandi Union                                             :    Fulbari Mouza                                             :    Domkandi Village                                           :    Char Domkandi GPS Location                                      :    24.828611 N; 89.563056 E Distance of the site from Upazila HQ              :    13 km North Nearby Major Road:                                :    Fulbari- Kutubpur : East side, wide-14fit, BC road. Nearby River/ Canal:                              :    Bangla River (West-300m) [SOURCE: Page_330]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, July 2025) The catchment area of the subproject mostly comprises of Machir para, Char Domkandi Dakshin para, Kajla, Baroikandi, Domkandi villages which have been significantly affected by floods. Char Domkandi (Fulbari Union, Shariakandi Upazila, Bogura) sits on the active floodplain of the Jamuna, within an upazila where roughly two-fifths of the area is water and the Jamuna flows south through a mosaic of low-lying chars. Seasonal flooding is driven by intense monsoon rainfall and Jamuna overbanking, with additional exchange of flood pulses through the Jamuna– Bangali linkage at Shariakandi (fish-pass connection), which helps spread water across adjacent floodplains and drainage channels. The locality is officially recorded under Fulbari Union, and project data identify a Char Domkandi school site in Fulbari close to a Bangali branch river, underscoring its riverine setting. Recurrent erosion and inundation are documented for Shariakandi, with recent events marooning thousands in low-lying unions. Overall, Char Domkandi’s flood hazard reflects a char-dominated, low-relief floodplain where monsoon flows and river dynamics routinely disrupt roads, homesteads, cropland and livelihoods. The flood shelter will be constructed at Char Domkandi Government Primary School (GPS), which is located at the Char Domkandi village under Fulbari Union of Shariakandi Upazila in Bogura District. There are 5 teachers (M: 3; F: 2) and 150 students (Boys: 71; Girls: 79) in the school, operated by the guidance of School Management Committee (SMC) and government officials of Shariakandi Upazila Education Office. The students, teachers and residents of the catchment area come to the proposed site by using the connecting/access road named Char Domkandi GPS road. The road is a BC road with wide-4fit and just passing beside the Char Domkandi Government Primary School on the North side. Page | 288 [SOURCE: Page_330]

Figure 5: Proposed Waste Disposal Area for the Subproject Site The existing Char Domkandi Government Primary School covers 61 decimals of land and currently comprises a one-storied pucca building in the central portion and a semi-pucca tin- shed building on the northern side, both serving as classrooms and administrative offices. Located on the southern side are a Shaheed Minar and a wash block. The proposed flood shelter is planned for the northern side of the compound, which will necessitate the demolition of the existing pucca building (19m × 9m), the tin-shed building (6.5m × 5.7m), the central toilet block (2.5m × 2m), and an existing tubewell structure (3m × 2.5m). During the construction period, all educational and administrative functions will be relocated to a temporary shed. Supporting facilities, including a labour shed, a materials storage area on the eastern side, and a waste disposal site on the southern side, will also be established. While the premises contain numerous trees of varying sizes, only ten will need to be removed. The site is served by a 14-foot-wide kutcha road to the east, with an additional access road approximately 10 feet wide. Within a 1 km radius of the school, there are several local settlements as well as a mosque, agricultural land, a graveyard, a shamshan ghat, and a madrasa, with the Char Domrakandi Mosque located adjacent to the school. The Bangla River lies about 300 meters west of the premises, with an approximate width of 90 feet and a depth of 20 feet. Historical records show that the area experienced flooding in both 1988 and 2007, when water levels rose to 2 feet and remained for 15 to 20 days. (Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, July 2025) The proposed sub-project (construction of new School cum Flood shelter building) is not located within any environmentally sensitive area and will not cause any severe negative effects to the environmental settings of the area, neither to important environmental features. The disaster shelter will be constructed within an existing school boundary, so no agricultural land/ activities or fish farming will be disturbed due to the construction of the sub project. The project site is surrounded by a number of notable landmarks in all directions. To the north, the area is bordered by agricultural land just 50 meters away, along with a graveyard located about 500 meters from the site. On the south side, more agricultural land stretches around 600 meters away. Toward the east, several key religious and educational landmarks can be found, including the Char Domkandi Mosque situated adjacent to a school, the Char New Domkandi Mosque at a distance of 400 meters, the Baitun Nur Mosque about 800 meters away, and an Eidgah with a Nurania Madrasa located approximately 1 kilometer from the area. To the west, a Hindu crematorium lies at a distance of about 1 kilometer, highlighting the cultural and religious diversity of the surroundings. No significant disturbance to all these establishments/features is anticipated due to construction activities for having sufficient distance from the construction site, and strict construction site management system- including restrictive work schedule during the daytime only, water- sprinkling twice a day in and around the site, proper fencing around the working area, safe storage of materials, etc. Construction related activities and setting up of labor camps along with associated facilities and their management issues will be accounted for impacts more likely to be generated during the pre, post and construction period. Noise pollution from pilling or drilling, air pollution caused by dust or gaseous emissions from vehicle movement, running of motorized equipment and land clearing, odors and soil pollution from leaking of latrines and fecal sludge, will more likely to take place. Soil can further be eroded and polluted from chemical spills or improper disposal of waste materials. Noise and vibration effects generated from pilling and drilling may also trigger landslides and harmful disturbances to local fauna. Impact on surface and ground water bodies might get acute due mainly to the high abstraction rate and disposal/leakage of pollutants to the surface/ground water bodies. ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SCREENING This section identifies the potential impacts that the various elements of the proposed sub- project may have on the physical, biological and socio-economic environment within half a kilometer of the radial distance around the site. Environmental and Social Assessment (ESA) based on this screening study for the Sub-project as Char Domkandi Government Primary School of Shariakandi Upazila under Bogura District has been conducted to identify and determine which potential project impacts may be significant and therefore require the application of reasonable and effective management and/or mitigation measures. In order to realize the exact physical, biological and socio-economic environment of the proposed sub-project site and the influence area in regards to the implementation measures, an extensive field visit was carried out on 02 July 2025 in the Sub-project area. Environmental and Social Screening form, as adopted in Annexure-2 of the Environmental and Social Management Framework of RIVER, was administered for identifying the impacts and their extents. [SOURCE: Page_335]

PUBLIC CONSULTATION AND PARTICIPATION Public participation and community consultation has been taken up as an integral part of environmental assessment process of the project. Field visit has been carried out on 02 July 2025 in and around the Sub-project component site. As part of the impact assessment, participatory public consultation was conducted in that area by the field level staffs, and consultants from D&SC. Checklist of the consultation is attached in Annexure-3. The consultation meeting was attended by 20 persons (Male -18 and Female -02) and local individuals, teachers, chairman and/or member of Union Parishad and school management committee were among the attendees in that meeting. The participants were selected from different cohorts of stakeholders, and some of whom will have major active roles before, during and even after the construction works. Therefore, the meeting was organized in an informed, expressive and unbiased manner, wherefrom different views and concerns came across which will be properly taken care of during the design and construction phases. Refer to Figure 8 and Annexure-4 for selected photographs of the participatory public consultation held at site of the Char Domkandi Government Primary School and list of attendees in that public consultation meeting, respectively. A questionnaire was kept ready and responses were elicited. During these consultations, the communities were explained about the project, its benefits, associated social and environmental aspects and possible mitigation measures. The participants were also informed about the project GRM (Grievance Redress Mechanism) system in detail and the disclosure of project documents in websites, and their unrestricted and uninitiated access to those system and resources. As such, public consultation is a living process as the types of problems/ difficulties, involved parties or stakeholders and mode of settlement or resolution processes are more likely to differ with time. Thus, consultation with different [SOURCE: Page_335]

Page | 293 [SOURCE: Page_335]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_336]

parties or stakeholders will be continued throughout the sub-project implementation period and records of resolutions, whatsoever and wherever possible, will be kept in writing at the site and made available on any enquiries or requests by all parties concerned. [SOURCE: Page_336]

Figure 8: Public Consultation Meeting in the Proposed Sub-project Site [SOURCE: Page_336]

SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACTS Overall Construction Related Impacts: The proposed construction works are expected to generate localized and temporary environmental and social impacts typical of small- to medium- scale civil works. Key environmental impacts include dust and air emissions, noise and vibration from machinery, construction waste generation, temporary soil disturbance, and minor vegetation loss during site preparation. There may also be risks of water and soil contamination from improper material handling or drainage obstruction. Social impacts are anticipated to be limited, involving temporary disruption of school activities, restricted access to playgrounds, increased traffic movement, and potential occupational health and safety risks for workers. However, no land acquisition, displacement, or impacts on ethnic or vulnerable communities are expected. Overall, the impacts are short-term, reversible, and confined within existing school premises, manageable through standard environmental and social mitigation practices. Tree Cutting: Approximately 21 trees (medium/large size) are likely to be cut down and no water bodies are likely to be filled up due to the construction of the flood shelter. [There are water bodies (Bangla River) on the west side of the shelter (size: 90ft & depth 20ft)] The ecological impact of the subproject is low. There will be temporary negative impacts on physico-chemical environment. Nevertheless, these impacts are manageable if mitigation measures are taken according to ESMP. Grass turfing: Grass turfs on embankment, slope, building compound & any critical place to enhance the ecological condition and protect the top soil. Tentative area of turf has been estimated as 240 square meters (half of total area), after discussion with architects and engineers. It is likely to be changed depending on the requirement during construction as per site design and as per direction of E.I.C. Land Ownership: Availability of adequate public land area is as important as community consent to construct the flood shelter and access roads. The D&S Survey team did not find any conflicts over the school land. The land issue has been discussed in the meeting. Participants unanimously confirmed that the school has its own 66 decimals of land and there is no dispute about this Page | 294 [SOURCE: Page_336]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_337]

land. Land Acquisition: The proposed Sub-project, Char Domkandi Government Primary School, does not have any involuntary resettlement impacts due to the construction of flood shelter and approach roads as the Sub-projects will be constructed in existing Government Primary Schools’ premises. The Government Primary School has 66 decimals of land. No land acquisition will be required for the activities to be implemented under the project. Access road needs to construct or rehabilitate within its existing alignment. Considering the impacts identified at this particular school site, the site-specific Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) may be outlined as follows: [SOURCE: Page_337]

As per project ESMF, PIU, project engineer’s suggestion and experience from other LGED projects such as MDSP, EMCRP etc. adequate budget has been proposed for the environmental management for the mitigation and enhancement measures. It may vary depending on the real time situation and requirement of the construction. The subproject activities have temporary and localized negative impact on noise level during construction phase due to movement of the subproject vehicles and equipment. Hence, budget includes analytical monitoring for noise level. For solid waste management adequate waste bins will be installed. The budget for labor shed, and site office construction is included in the civil works items. Therefore, it is not included in the environmental budget. It should be noted that the contractor will be paid as per actual work done. [SOURCE: Page_349]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_351]

The subproject is located in the South-West part of Shariakandi Upazila in Bogura District, which is within the Rajshahi Division. The location details of the subproject have been summarized in Table 2. Table 2: Location Details of the Subproject Site District                                           :    Bogura Upazila                                            :    Shariakandi Union                                              :    Fulbari Mouza                                              :    Domkandi Village                                            :    Domkandi GPS Location                                       :    24.836864 N; 89.565098 E Distance of the site from Upazila HQ               :    10 km North Nearby Major Road:                                 :    16ft. wide BC Sonamiya-Shariakandi Road at West side on 10km Nearby River/ Canal:                               :    Bangla River (East-800m) [SOURCE: Page_351]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, July 2025) The catchment area of the subproject mostly comprises of Dhaho para, New Sonatola, Char Domkandi, Betoyerkandi villages which have been significantly affected by floods. Domkandi under Fulbari Union of Shariakandi Upazila, Bogura, sits on the active floodplain of the Jamuna, in an upazila where about two-fifths of the area is open water—chiefly the Jamuna—and low- lying chars dominate the landscape. Seasonal flooding is driven by intense monsoon rainfall and Jamuna over-banking, with additional propagation of flood pulses through the Shariakandi fish- pass linkage between the Jamuna and the Bangali, which spreads water across adjoining floodplains and drainage channels. Domkandi/Char Domkandi is formally listed under Fulbari Union’s village roster, and project siting records show Domkandi GPS and Char Domkandi GPS schools within Fulbari near a Bangali branch, underscoring the settlement’s riverine exposure. As a result, monsoon floods routinely inundate homesteads, cropland and access roads, with conditions closely tracked at the Jamuna–Shariakandi gauge (SW15J), and erosion/isolation recurring across the char belt. The flood shelter will be constructed at Domkandi Government Primary School (GPS), which is located at the Domkandi village under Fulbari Union of Shariakandi Upazila in Bogura District. There are 6 teachers (M: 4; F: 2) and 103 students (Boys: 49; Girls: 54) in the school, operated by the guidance of School Management Committee (SMC) and government officials of Shariakandi Upazila Education Office. The students, teachers and residents of the catchment area come to the proposed site by using the connecting/access road named Char Domkandi to Badth road. The road is a connecting earthen road with wide-10ft. and just passing beside the Domkandi Government Primary School at South side. [SOURCE: Page_351]

Daily water needs in the area are mainly met through shallow tubewells, with groundwater typically accessed at a depth of around 70 feet below ground level. Figure 5: Proposed Waste Disposal Area for the Subproject Site The existing Domkandi Government Primary School covers 82 decimals of land and includes a one-storied pucca building on the western side along with two semi-pucca buildings, one located on the west and the other on the northern side, all of which are currently used for classrooms and administrative purposes. A wash block is also situated on the western side. The proposed flood shelter will be constructed on the southern side of the premises, and no demolition of existing structures will be required. Throughout the construction period, academic and administrative activities will continue without interruption in the existing facilities. Temporary arrangements, including a labour shed, a materials storage area on the northern side, and a waste disposal site on the eastern side, will be established within the compound. The site is accessible via a pucca road located 70 meters to the west and a 10-foot-wide kutcha road to the north, while transportation access is provided by the Sonamia–Shariakandi Road. Within a 1 km radius of the school are several local settlements, and an Eidgah is located adjacent to the premises. The Domkandi Mora Khal lies directly east of the school boundary. Historical flood records show that the area was submerged in 1988, when water rose to a depth of 4 feet and remained for 30 days, and again in 2019, when 1.5 feet of water persisted for 15–20 days. (Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, July 2025) The proposed sub-project (construction of new School cum Flood shelter building) is not located within any environmentally sensitive area and will not cause any severe negative effects to the environmental settings of the area, neither to important environmental features. The disaster shelter will be constructed within an existing school boundary, so no agricultural land/ activities or fish farming will be disturbed due to the construction of the sub project. On the north side, the area features an Eidgah adjacent to a school, along with nearby agricultural land just 50 meters away. Further north, the Domkandi Mandir stands at around 500 meters, and a community clinic is located approximately 700 meters from the site. To the south, there is a family graveyard next to a school, with agricultural land only 20 meters away. Toward the east, stretches of agricultural land begin at about 100 meters, while the Char Domkandi Mosque and the Bengali River both lie around 700 meters from the area. On the west side, the Domkandi Central Mosque is located within a short distance of just 100 meters highlighting the cultural and religious diversity of the surroundings. No significant disturbance to all these establishments/features is anticipated due to construction activities for having sufficient distance from the construction site, and strict construction site management system- including restrictive work schedule during the daytime only, water- sprinkling twice a day in and around the site, proper fencing around the working area, safe storage of materials, etc. Construction related activities and setting up of labor camps along with associated facilities and their management issues will be accounted for impacts more likely to be generated during the pre, post and construction period. Noise pollution from pilling or drilling, air pollution caused by dust or gaseous emissions from vehicle movement, running of motorized equipment and land clearing, odors and soil pollution from leaking of latrines and fecal sludge, will more likely to take place. Soil can further be eroded and polluted from chemical spills or improper disposal of waste materials. Noise and vibration effects generated from pilling and drilling may also trigger landslides and harmful disturbances to local fauna. Impact on surface and ground water bodies might get acute due mainly to the high abstraction rate and disposal/leakage of pollutants to the surface/ground water bodies. Clearing of trees, bushes or any type of vegetation may put impact on floral species and unscrupulous clearance also trigger habitat loss. All these impacts can only Page | 313 [SOURCE: Page_355]

ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SCREENING This section identifies the potential impacts that the various elements of the proposed sub- project may have on the physical, biological and socio-economic environment within half a kilometer of the radial distance around the site. Environmental and Social Assessment (ESA) based on this screening study for the Sub-project as Domkandi Government Primary School of Shariakandi Upazila under Bogura District has been conducted to identify and determine which potential project impacts may be significant and therefore require the application of reasonable and effective management and/or mitigation measures. In order to realize the exact physical, biological and socio-economic environment of the proposed sub-project site and the influence area in regards to the implementation measures, an extensive field visit was carried out on 02 July 2025 in the Sub-project area. Environmental and Social Screening form, as adopted in Annexure-2 of the Environmental and Social Management Framework of RIVER, was administered for identifying the impacts and their extents. [SOURCE: Page_356]

PUBLIC CONSULTATION AND PARTICIPATION Public participation and community consultation has been taken up as an integral part of environmental assessment process of the project. Field visit has been carried out on 02 July 2025 in and around the Sub-project component site. As part of the impact assessment, participatory public consultation was conducted in that area by the field level staffs, and consultants from D&SC. Checklist of the consultation is attached in Annexure-3. The consultation meeting was attended by 19 persons (Male -17 and Female -02) and local individuals, teachers, chairman and/or member of Union Parishad and school management committee were among the attendees in that meeting. The participants were selected from different cohorts of stakeholders, and some of whom will have major active roles before, during and even after the construction works. Therefore, the meeting was organized in an informed, expressive and unbiased manner, wherefrom different views and concerns came across which will be properly taken care of during the design and construction phases. Refer to Figure 8 and Annexure-4 for selected photographs of the participatory public consultation held at site of the Domkandi Government Primary School and list of attendees in that public consultation meeting, respectively. A questionnaire was kept ready and responses were elicited. During these consultations, the communities were explained about the project, its benefits, associated social and environmental aspects and possible mitigation measures. The participants were also informed about the project GRM (Grievance Redress Mechanism) system in detail and the disclosure of project documents in websites, and their unrestricted and uninitiated access to those system and resources. As such, public consultation is a living process as the types of problems/ difficulties, involved parties or stakeholders and mode of settlement or resolution processes are more likely to differ with time. Thus, consultation with different parties or stakeholders will be continued throughout the sub-project implementation period and [SOURCE: Page_356]

SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACTS Overall Construction Related Impacts: The proposed construction works are expected to generate localized and temporary environmental and social impacts typical of small- to medium- scale civil works. Key environmental impacts include dust and air emissions, noise and vibration from machinery, construction waste generation, temporary soil disturbance, and minor vegetation loss during site preparation. There may also be risks of water and soil contamination from improper material handling or drainage obstruction. Social impacts are anticipated to be limited, involving temporary disruption of school activities, restricted access to playgrounds, increased traffic movement, and potential occupational health and safety risks for workers. However, no land acquisition, displacement, or impacts on ethnic or vulnerable communities are expected. Overall, the impacts are short-term, reversible, and confined within existing school premises, manageable through standard environmental and social mitigation practices. Environmental Impacts: No trees are likely to be cut down and no water bodies are likely to be filled up due to the construction of the flood shelter. [There are water bodies (Domkandi Mora Khal) on the east side adjacent to the shelter]. The ecological impact of the subproject is low. There will be temporary negative impacts on physico-chemical environment. Nevertheless, these impacts are manageable if mitigation measures are taken according to ESMP. Grass turfing: Grass turfs on embankment, slope, building compound & any critical place to enhance the ecological condition and protect the top soil. Tentative area of turf has been estimated as 240 square meters (half of total area), after discussion with architects and engineers. It is likely to be changed depending on the requirement during construction as per site design and as per direction of E.I.C. Land Ownership: Availability of adequate public land area is as important as community consent to construct the flood shelter and access roads. The D&S Survey team did not find any conflicts over the school land. The land issue has been discussed in the meeting. Participants unanimously confirmed that the school has its own 82 decimals of land and there is no dispute about this land. Land Acquisition: The proposed Sub-project, Domkandi Government Primary School, does not Page | 315 [SOURCE: Page_357]
