LOCATION OF THE SUB-PROJECT The subproject is located in the Northern part of Shariakandi Upazila in Bogura District, which is within the Rajshahi Division. The location details of the subproject have been summarized in Table 2. Table 2: Location Details of the Subproject Site District                                          :    Bogura Upazila                                           :    Shariakandi Union                                             :    Fulbari Mouza                                             :    Fulbari Village                                           :    Ramnagar GPS Location                                      :    24.887552 N; 89.554582 E Distance of the site from Upazila HQ              :    2.5 km Nearby Major Road:                                :    Shariakandi-Bogura Road at South side Nearby River/ Canal:                              :    Baromasha Canal (East -6 m) [SOURCE: Page_370]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, July 2025) The catchment area of the subproject mostly comprises of Kuptola, Kuptola Shahapara, Amtoli, Char Ramnagar villages which have been significantly affected by floods. The floods in Shariakandi Upazila are mainly caused by the natural behavior of the Jamuna. Presence of Cholon Beel and smaller wetland are seen also seen within these upazilas contributing to regions flood susceptibility. During monsoon season, heavy rainfall and overflow of rivers inundates the surrounding low-lying areas creating flood hazard and have had profound impacts on the village's infrastructure and livelihoods. The flood shelter will be constructed at Ramnagar Government Primary School (GPS), which is located at the Ramnagar village under Fulbari Union of Shariakandi Upazila in Bogura District. There are 07 teachers, and 262 students (Boys: 101; Girls: 161) in the school, operated by the guidance of School Management Committee (SMC) and government officials of Tarash Upazila Education Office. The students, teachers and residents of the catchment area come to the proposed site by using the connecting/access road named Ramnagar to Garumara Road. The road is a BC road with 3.04 meters width and just passing beside the Ramnagar Government Primary School at East side. The population of the catchment area is about 10,000. The Fulbari Union map indicating sub- project location has been shown respectively in Figure 1. The topographical Map with indicative and tentative location of labor camp, construction materials storage area, and waste disposal area have been shown in Figure 2 which shall be placed as per direction and satisfaction of LGED and E.I.C. [SOURCE: Page_370]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_374]

The proposed sub-project (construction of new School cum Flood shelter building) is not located within any environmentally sensitive area and will not cause any severe negative effects to the environmental settings of the area, neither to important environmental features. The disaster shelter will be constructed within an existing school boundary, so no agricultural land/ activities or fish farming will be disturbed due to the construction of the sub project. There are found some socio-environmental features such as Chak Chakia bil (200m), Ningra bil (350m) on the North side of the proposed sub-project location. To the south, Mandal bari graveyard (500m), Kali Mandir (600m), Mandal Bari Jame Mosque (500m) are found on from the sub-project component. Kuptala Shahapara Mandir (150m), Kuptala High School (500m), Baromasha Khal (6m), Bangali River (500m) found on the East side from the sub-project component. Some important socio-environmental features such as Ramnagar Uttarpara Mosque (Adjacent), Ramnagar Hafezia Madrasa (200m) located on West side from the sub-project location. No significant disturbance to all these establishments/features is anticipated due to construction activities for having sufficient distance from the construction site, and strict construction site management system- including restrictive work schedule during the daytime only, water- sprinkling twice a day in and around the site, proper fencing around the working area, safe storage of materials, etc. Construction related activities and setting up of labor camps along with associated facilities and their management issues will be accounted for impacts more likely to be generated during the pre, post and construction period. Noise pollution from pilling or drilling, air pollution caused by dust or gaseous emissions from vehicle movement, running of motorized equipment and land clearing, odors and soil pollution from leaking of latrines and fecal sludge, will more likely to take place. Soil can further be eroded and polluted from chemical spills or improper disposal of waste materials. Noise and vibration effects generated from pilling and drilling may also trigger landslides and harmful disturbances to local fauna. Impact on surface and ground water bodies might get acute due mainly to the high abstraction rate and disposal/leakage of pollutants to the surface/ground water bodies. Clearing of trees, bushes or any type of vegetation may put impact on floral species and unscrupulous clearance also trigger habitat loss. All these impacts can only be prevented or minimized by adopting measures delineated into the ESMP and good practice engineering and site management. ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SCREENING This section identifies the potential impacts that the various elements of the proposed sub- project may have on the physical, biological and socio-economic environment within half a kilometer of the radial distance around the site. Environmental and Social Assessment (ESA) based on this screening study for the Sub-project as Ramnagar Government Primary School of Shariakandi Upazila under Bogura District has been conducted to identify and determine which potential project impacts may be significant and therefore require the application of reasonable and effective management and/or mitigation measures. In order to realize the exact physical, biological and socio-economic environment of the proposed sub-project site and the influence area in regards to the implementation measures, an extensive field visit was carried out on 02 [SOURCE: Page_374]

Page | 332 [SOURCE: Page_374]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_375]

July 2025 in the Sub-project area. Environmental and Social Screening form, as adopted in Annexure-2 of the Environmental and Social Management Framework of RIVER, was administered for identifying the impacts and their extents. [SOURCE: Page_375]

PUBLIC CONSULTATION AND PARTICIPATION Public participation and community consultation has been taken up as an integral part of environmental assessment process of the project. Field visit has been carried out on 02 July 2025 in and around the Sub-project component site. As part of the impact assessment, participatory public consultation was conducted in that area by the field level staffs, and consultants from D&SC. Checklist of the consultation is attached in Annexure-3. The consultation meeting was attended by 29 persons (Male -06 and Female -23) and local individuals, teachers, chairman and/or member of Union Parishad and school management committee were among the attendees in that meeting. The participants were selected from different cohorts of stakeholders, and some of whom will have major active roles before, during and even after the construction works. Therefore, the meeting was organized in an informed, expressive and unbiased manner, wherefrom different views and concerns came across which will be properly taken care of during the design and construction phases. Refer to Figure 8 and Annexure-4 for selected photographs of the participatory public consultation held at site of the Ramnagar Government Primary School and list of attendees in that public consultation meeting, respectively. A questionnaire was kept ready and responses were elicited. During these consultations, the communities were explained about the project, its benefits, associated social and environmental aspects and possible mitigation measures. The participants were also informed about the project GRM (Grievance Redress Mechanism) system in detail and the disclosure of project documents in websites, and their unrestricted and uninitiated access to those system and resources. As such, public consultation is a living process as the types of problems/ difficulties, involved parties or stakeholders and mode of settlement or resolution processes are more likely to differ with time. Thus, consultation with different parties or stakeholders will be continued throughout the sub-project implementation period and records of resolutions, whatsoever and wherever possible, will be kept in writing at the site and made available on any enquiries or requests by all parties concerned. [SOURCE: Page_375]

SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACTS Overall Construction Related Impacts: The proposed construction works are expected to generate localized and temporary environmental and social impacts typical of small- to medium- scale civil works. Key environmental impacts include dust and air emissions, noise and vibration from machinery, construction waste generation, temporary soil disturbance, and minor vegetation loss during site preparation. There may also be risks of water and soil contamination from improper material handling or drainage obstruction. Social impacts are anticipated to be limited, involving temporary disruption of school activities, restricted access to playgrounds, increased traffic movement, and potential occupational health and safety risks for workers. However, no land acquisition, displacement, or impacts on ethnic or vulnerable communities are expected. Overall, the impacts are short-term, reversible, and confined within existing school premises, manageable through standard environmental and social mitigation practices. Tree cutting: Approximately 17 Nos. (Medium to large) trees are likely to be cut down and no water bodies are likely to be filled up due to the construction of the flood shelter. The ecological impact of the subproject is low. There will be temporary negative impacts on physic-chemical environment. Nevertheless, these impacts are manageable if mitigation measures are taken according to ESMP. Grass turfing: Grass turfs on embankment, slope, building compound & any critical place to enhance the ecological condition and protect the top soil. Tentative area of turf has been estimated as 240 square meters (half of total area), after discussion with architects and engineers. It is likely to be changed depending on the requirement during construction as per site design and as per direction of E.I.C. Land Ownership: Availability of adequate public land area is as important as community consent to construct the flood shelter and access roads. The D&S Survey team did not find any conflicts over the school land. The land issue has been discussed in the meeting. Participants unanimously confirmed that the school has its own 50 decimals of land and there is no dispute about this land. Land Acquisition: The proposed Sub-project, Ramnagar Government Primary School, does not [SOURCE: Page_376]

Page | 334 [SOURCE: Page_376]

have any involuntary resettlement impacts due to the construction of flood shelter and approach roads as the Sub-projects will be constructed in existing Government Primary Schools’ premises. Access road needs to construct or rehabilitate within its existing alignment. As per project ESMF, PIU, project engineer’s suggestion and experience from other LGED projects such as MDSP, EMCRP etc., adequate budget has been proposed for the environmental management for the mitigation and enhancement measures. It may vary depending on the real time situation and requirement of the construction. The subproject activities have temporary and localized negative impact on noise level during construction phase due to movement of the subproject vehicles and equipment. Hence, budget includes analytical monitoring for noise level. For solid waste management adequate waste bins will be installed. The budget for labor shed, and site office construction is included in the civil works items. Therefore, it is not included in the environmental budget. It should be noted that the contractor will be paid as per actual work done. [SOURCE: Page_388]

The subproject is located in the Northern part of Shariakandi Upazila in Bogura District, which is within the Rajshahi Division. The location details of the subproject have been summarized in Table 2. Table 2: Location Details of the Subproject Site District                                          :    Bogura Upazila                                           :    Shariakandi Union                                             :    Fulbari Mouza                                             :    Ramchandapur Village                                           :    Harina GPS Location                                      :    24.871133 N; 89.529077 E Distance of the site from Upazila HQ              :    7 km Nearby Major Road:                                :    Bogura-Shariakandi Road at North Side [SOURCE: Page_390]

Nearby River/ Canal:                              :    Sukhdoho (North-500m) [SOURCE: Page_390]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, July 2025) The catchment area of the subproject mostly comprises of Fulbari, Baluyer tair, Majbari, Fulbari Dakshin para villages which have been significantly affected by floods. The floods in Shariakandi Upazila are mainly caused by the natural behavior of the Jamuna. Presence of Cholon Beel and smaller wetland are seen also seen within these upazilas contributing to regions flood susceptibility. During monsoon season, heavy rainfall and overflow of rivers inundates the surrounding low-lying areas creating flood hazard and have had profound impacts on the village's infrastructure and livelihoods. The flood shelter will be constructed at Harina Government Primary School (GPS), which is located at the Harina village under Fulbari Union of Shariakandi Upazila in Bogura District. There are 08 teachers, and 217 students (Boys: 111; Girls: 106) in the school, operated by the guidance of School Management Committee (SMC) and government officials of Tarash Upazila Education Office. The students, teachers and residents of the catchment area come to the proposed site by using the connecting/access road named Shahid Momataj Road. The road is a BC road with 3.04 meters width and just passing beside the Harina Government Primary School at north side. The population of the catchment area is about 30,000. The Fulbari Union map indicating sub- project location has been shown respectively in Figure 1. The topographical Map with indicative and tentative location of labor camp, construction materials storage area, and waste disposal area have been shown in Figure 2 which shall be placed as per direction and satisfaction of LGED and E.I.C. [SOURCE: Page_390]

Figure 5: Proposed Waste Disposal Area for the Subproject Site The existing Harina Government Primary School has 53 decimals of land comprises of one- storied pucca building and a new one storied pucca school building that currently accommodates all classrooms and administrative offices. The proposed flood shelter is planned to be constructed in the school premises by demolishing the old one-storied pucca building. All academic and administrative activities will move to the temporary school shed during the construction period. Community members residing adjacent to the school have emphasized the importance of ensuring uninterrupted class operations to maintain continuity in students’ education. Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_394]

The proposed sub-project (construction of new School cum Flood shelter building) is not located within any environmentally sensitive area and will not cause any severe negative effects to the environmental settings of the area, neither to important environmental features. The disaster shelter will be constructed within an existing school boundary, so no agricultural land/ activities or fish farming will be disturbed due to the construction of the sub project. There are found some socio-environmental features such as Dobila Purba Para Mosque (10m), Bedekata Diyar (100m) on the North side of the proposed sub-project location. To the south, Dobila Dakkhin Para Mosque (200m), Islampur Chakrohali Mosque (1km), Kata Khal (1Km) are found on from the sub-project component. Dobila High School (50m), Dobila Islampur Madrasa (1km), Dobila Islampur Graveyard (1km), Dobila Islampur Mosque (1km), Dobila Islampur Eidgah (1km) found on the East side from the sub-project component. Some important socio-environmental features such as Dobila Mondir (500m), Saint Gan Catholic Church (550m), Dobila Central Mosque (600m), Dobila Magura Union Council (1000m) located on West side from the sub-project location. No significant disturbance to all these establishments/features is anticipated due to construction activities for having sufficient distance from the construction site, and strict construction site management system- including restrictive work schedule during the daytime only, water- sprinkling twice a day in and around the site, proper fencing around the working area, safe storage of materials, etc. Construction related activities and setting up of labor camps along with associated facilities and their management issues will be accounted for impacts more likely to be generated during the pre, post and construction period. Noise pollution from pilling or drilling, air pollution caused by dust or gaseous emissions from vehicle movement, running of motorized equipment and land clearing, odors and soil pollution from leaking of latrines and fecal sludge, will more likely to take place. Soil can further be eroded and polluted from chemical spills or improper disposal of waste materials. Noise and vibration effects generated from pilling and drilling may also trigger landslides and harmful disturbances to local fauna. Impact on surface and ground water bodies might get acute due mainly to the high abstraction rate and disposal/leakage of pollutants to the surface/ground water bodies. Clearing of trees, bushes or any type of vegetation may put impact on floral species and unscrupulous clearance also trigger habitat loss. All these impacts can only be prevented or minimized by adopting measures delineated into the ESMP and good practice engineering and site management. ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SCREENING This section identifies the potential impacts that the various elements of the proposed sub- project may have on the physical, biological and socio-economic environment within half a kilometer of the radial distance around the site. Environmental and Social Assessment (ESA) based on this screening study for the Sub-project as Harina Government Primary School of Shariakandi Upazila under Bogura District has been conducted to identify and determine which potential project impacts may be significant and therefore require the application of reasonable and effective management and/or mitigation measures. In order to realize the exact physical, [SOURCE: Page_394]

Page | 352 [SOURCE: Page_394]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_395]

biological and socio-economic environment of the proposed sub-project site and the influence area in regards to the implementation measures, an extensive field visit was carried out on 03 July 2025 in the Sub-project area. Environmental and Social Screening form, as adopted in Annexure-2 of the Environmental and Social Management Framework of RIVER, was administered for identifying the impacts and their extents. [SOURCE: Page_395]

PUBLIC CONSULTATION AND PARTICIPATION Public participation and community consultation has been taken up as an integral part of environmental assessment process of the project. Field visit has been carried out on 03 July 2025 in and around the Sub-project component site. As part of the impact assessment, participatory public consultation was conducted in that area by the field level staffs, and consultants from D&SC. Checklist of the consultation is attached in Annexure-3. The consultation meeting was attended by 20 persons (Male -07 and Female -13) and local individuals, teachers, chairman and/or member of Union Parishad and school management committee were among the attendees in that meeting. The participants were selected from different cohorts of stakeholders, and some of whom will have major active roles before, during and even after the construction works. Therefore, the meeting was organized in an informed, expressive and unbiased manner, wherefrom different views and concerns came across which will be properly taken care of during the design and construction phases. Refer to Figure 8 and Annexure-4 for selected photographs of the participatory public consultation held at site of the Harina Government Primary School and list of attendees in that public consultation meeting, respectively. A questionnaire was kept ready and responses were elicited. During these consultations, the communities were explained about the project, its benefits, associated social and environmental aspects and possible mitigation measures. The participants were also informed about the project GRM (Grievance Redress Mechanism) system in detail and the disclosure of project documents in websites, and their unrestricted and uninitiated access to those system and resources. As such, public consultation is a living process as the types of problems/ difficulties, involved parties or stakeholders and mode of settlement or resolution processes are more likely to differ with time. Thus, consultation with different parties or stakeholders will be continued throughout the sub-project implementation period and records of resolutions, whatsoever and wherever possible, will be kept in writing at the site and made available on any enquiries or requests by all parties concerned. [SOURCE: Page_395]

SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACTS Overall Construction Related Impacts: The proposed construction works are expected to generate localized and temporary environmental and social impacts typical of small- to medium- scale civil works. Key environmental impacts include dust and air emissions, noise and vibration from machinery, construction waste generation, temporary soil disturbance, and minor vegetation loss during site preparation. There may also be risks of water and soil contamination from improper material handling or drainage obstruction. Social impacts are anticipated to be limited, involving temporary disruption of school activities, restricted access to playgrounds, increased traffic movement, and potential occupational health and safety risks for workers. However, no land acquisition, displacement, or impacts on ethnic or vulnerable communities are expected. Overall, the impacts are short-term, reversible, and confined within existing school premises, manageable through standard environmental and social mitigation practices. Tree cutting: Approximately 20 Nos. trees are likely to be cut down and no water bodies are likely to be filled up due to the construction of the flood shelter. The ecological impact of the subproject is low. There will be temporary negative impacts on physic-chemical environment. Nevertheless, these impacts are manageable if mitigation measures are taken according to ESMP. Grass turfing: Grass turfs on embankment, slope, building compound & any critical place to enhance the ecological condition and protect the top soil. Tentative area of turf has been estimated as 240 square meters (half of total area), after discussion with architects and engineers. It is likely to be changed depending on the requirement during construction as per site design and as per direction of E.I.C. Land Ownership: Availability of adequate public land area is as important as community consent to construct the flood shelter and access roads. The D&S Survey team did not find any conflicts over the school land. The land issue has been discussed in the meeting. Participants unanimously confirmed that the school has its own 53 decimals of land and there is no dispute about this land. Land Acquisition: The proposed Sub-project, Harina Government Primary School, does not have any involuntary resettlement impacts due to the construction of flood shelter and approach roads as the Sub-projects will be constructed in existing Government Primary Schools’ premises. Page | 354 [SOURCE: Page_396]

Access road needs to construct or rehabilitate within its existing alignment. Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_410]

The subproject is located in the Northern part of Shariakandi Upazila in Bogura District, which is within the Rajshahi Division. The location details of the subproject have been summarized in Table 2. Table 2: Location Details of the Subproject Site District                                           :    Bogura Upazila                                            :    Shariakandi Union                                              :    Kutubpur Mouza                                              :    Kutubpur Village                                            :    Kajla GPS Location                                       :    24.820726 N; 89.570354 E Distance of the site from Upazila HQ               :    14 km Nearby Major Road:                                 :    Kutubpur-Shariakandi Road at East side [SOURCE: Page_410]

Nearby River/ Canal:                               :    Bangali River (West side-2 km) [SOURCE: Page_410]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, July 2025) The catchment area of the subproject mostly comprises of New Kajla, Baroikandi, Kutubpur, Solartair, Domkandi, Bansata villages which have been significantly affected by floods. The floods in Shariakandi Upazila are mainly caused by the natural behavior of the Jamuna. Presence of Cholon Beel and smaller wetland are seen also seen within these upazilas contributing to regions flood susceptibility. During monsoon season, heavy rainfall and overflow of rivers inundates the surrounding low-lying areas creating flood hazard and have had profound impacts on the village's infrastructure and livelihoods. The flood shelter will be constructed at Kajla New Government Primary School (GPS), which is located at the Kajla village under Kutubpur Union of Shariakandi Upazila in Bogura District. There are 04 teachers, and 145 students (Boys: 70; Girls: 75) in the school, operated by the guidance of School Management Committee (SMC) and government officials of Tarash Upazila Education Office. The students, teachers and residents of the catchment area come to the proposed site by using the connecting/access road named Kutubpur-Shariakandi Road. The road is a BC road with 4.57 meters width and just passing beside the Kajla New Government Primary School at East side. The population of the catchment area is about 25,000 – 30,000. The Kutubpur Union map indicating sub-project location has been shown respectively in Figure 1. The topographical Map with indicative and tentative location of labor camp, construction materials storage area, and waste disposal area have been shown in Figure 2 which shall be placed as per direction and satisfaction of LGED and E.I.C. [SOURCE: Page_410]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_414]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, July 2025) The proposed sub-project (construction of new School cum Flood shelter building) is not located within any environmentally sensitive area and will not cause any severe negative effects to the environmental settings of the area, neither to important environmental features. The disaster shelter will be constructed within an existing school boundary, so no agricultural land/ activities or fish farming will be disturbed due to the construction of the sub project. There are found some socio-environmental features such as Kutubpur nayapara mosque (500m), Kajla Kutubpur Eidgah Math (1km) on the North side of the proposed sub-project location. To the south, New Kajla Jame Mosque (3m), Kajla Central Graveyard (50m), Kajlar Bil (400m) are found on from the sub-project component. Kutubpur Mosque (900m), Pakuria Para GPS (1km) found on the East side from the sub-project component. Some important socio-environmental features such as Merur Char Jame Mosque (1km) located on West side from the sub-project location. No significant disturbance to all these establishments/features is anticipated due to construction activities for having sufficient distance from the construction site, and strict construction site management system- including restrictive work schedule during the daytime only, water- sprinkling twice a day in and around the site, proper fencing around the working area, safe storage of materials, etc. Construction related activities and setting up of labor camps along with associated facilities and their management issues will be accounted for impacts more likely to be generated during the pre, post and construction period. Noise pollution from pilling or drilling, air pollution caused by dust or gaseous emissions from vehicle movement, running of motorized equipment and land clearing, odors and soil pollution from leaking of latrines and fecal sludge, will more likely to take place. Soil can further be eroded and polluted from chemical spills or improper disposal of waste materials. Noise and vibration effects generated from pilling and drilling may also trigger landslides and harmful disturbances to local fauna. Impact on surface and ground water bodies might get acute due mainly to the high abstraction rate and disposal/leakage of pollutants to the surface/ground water bodies. Clearing of trees, bushes or any type of vegetation may put impact on floral species and unscrupulous clearance also trigger habitat loss. All these impacts can only be prevented or minimized by adopting measures delineated into the ESMP and good practice engineering and site management. ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SCREENING This section identifies the potential impacts that the various elements of the proposed sub- project may have on the physical, biological and socio-economic environment within half a kilometer of the radial distance around the site. Environmental and Social Assessment (ESA) based on this screening study for the Sub-project as Kajla New Government Primary School of Shariakandi Upazila under Bogura District has been conducted to identify and determine which potential project impacts may be significant and therefore require the application of reasonable and effective management and/or mitigation measures. In order to realize the exact physical, biological and socio-economic environment of the proposed sub-project site and the influence area in regards to the implementation measures, an extensive field visit was carried out on 02 Page | 372 [SOURCE: Page_414]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_415]

July 2025 in the Sub-project area. Environmental and Social Screening form, as adopted in Annexure-2 of the Environmental and Social Management Framework of RIVER, was administered for identifying the impacts and their extents. [SOURCE: Page_415]

PUBLIC CONSULTATION AND PARTICIPATION Public participation and community consultation has been taken up as an integral part of environmental assessment process of the project. Field visit has been carried out on 02 July 2025 in and around the Sub-project component site. As part of the impact assessment, participatory public consultation was conducted in that area by the field level staffs, and consultants from D&SC. Checklist of the consultation is attached in Annexure-3. The consultation meeting was attended by 23 persons (Male -20 and Female -3) and local individuals, teachers, chairman and/or member of Union Parishad and school management committee were among the attendees in that meeting. The participants were selected from different cohorts of stakeholders, and some of whom will have major active roles before, during and even after the construction works. Therefore, the meeting was organized in an informed, expressive and unbiased manner, wherefrom different views and concerns came across which will be properly taken care of during the design and construction phases. Refer to Figure 8 and Annexure-4 for selected photographs of the participatory public consultation held at site of the Kajla New Government Primary School and list of attendees in that public consultation meeting, respectively. A questionnaire was kept ready and responses were elicited. During these consultations, the communities were explained about the project, its benefits, associated social and environmental aspects and possible mitigation measures. The participants were also informed about the project GRM (Grievance Redress Mechanism) system in detail and the disclosure of project documents in websites, and their unrestricted and uninitiated access to those system and resources. As such, public consultation is a living process as the types of problems/ difficulties, involved parties or stakeholders and mode of settlement or resolution processes are more likely to differ with time. Thus, consultation with different parties or stakeholders will be continued throughout the sub-project implementation period and records of resolutions, whatsoever and wherever possible, will be kept in writing at the site and made available on any enquiries or requests by all parties concerned. [SOURCE: Page_415]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_416]

SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACTS Overall Construction Related Impacts: The proposed construction works are expected to generate localized and temporary environmental and social impacts typical of small- to medium- scale civil works. Key environmental impacts include dust and air emissions, noise and vibration from machinery, construction waste generation, temporary soil disturbance, and minor vegetation loss during site preparation. There may also be risks of water and soil contamination from improper material handling or drainage obstruction. Social impacts are anticipated to be limited, involving temporary disruption of school activities, restricted access to playgrounds, increased traffic movement, and potential occupational health and safety risks for workers. However, no land acquisition, displacement, or impacts on ethnic or vulnerable communities are expected. Overall, the impacts are short-term, reversible, and confined within existing school premises, manageable through standard environmental and social mitigation practices. Tree cutting: Approximate 3 trees are likely to be cut down and no water bodies are likely to be filled up due to the construction of the flood shelter. The ecological impact of the subproject is low. There will be temporary negative impacts on physic-chemical environment. Nevertheless, these impacts are manageable if mitigation measures are taken according to ESMP. Grass turfing: Grass turfs on embankment, slope, building compound & any critical place to enhance the ecological condition and protect the top soil. Tentative area of turf has been estimated as 240 square meters (half of total area), after discussion with architects and engineers. It is likely to be changed depending on the requirement during construction as per site design and as per direction of E.I.C. Land Ownership: Availability of adequate public land area is as important as community consent to construct the flood shelter and access roads. The D&S Survey team did not find any conflicts over the school land. The land issue has been discussed in the meeting. Participants unanimously confirmed that the school has its own 62 decimals of land and there is no dispute about this land. Land Acquisition: The proposed Sub-project, Kajla New Government Primary School, does not have any involuntary resettlement impacts due to the construction of flood shelter and approach roads as the Sub-projects will be constructed in existing Government Primary Schools’ premises. The Government Primary School has 62 decimals of land. No land acquisition will be required for the activities to be implemented under the project. Access road needs to construct or rehabilitate within its existing alignment. Considering the impacts identified at this particular school site, the site-specific Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) may be outlined as follows: [SOURCE: Page_416]

LOCATION OF THE SUB-PROJECT The subproject is located in the Northern part of Shariakandi Upazila in Bogura District, which is within the Rajshahi Division. The location details of the subproject have been summarized in Table 2. Table 2: Location Details of the Sub-project Site District                                          :    Bogura Upazila                                           :    Shariakandi Union                                             :    Kutubpur Mouza                                             :    Kutubpur Village                                           :    Solartair GPS Location                                      :    24.812314 N; 89.575549 E Distance of the site from Upazila HQ              :    13 km Nearby Major Road:                                :    Chandonbaisha- Bogura Road Nearby River/ Canal:                              :    Bangari (1km- west side), Jamuna River (1.5km – East side) [SOURCE: Page_431]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, July 2025) The catchment area of the subproject mostly comprises of Solartair, Kutubpur, Kajla, Banshata, Kashahar, Char para villages which have been significantly affected by floods. The floods in Shariakandi Upazila are mainly caused by the natural behavior of the Jamuna. Presence of Cholon Beel and smaller wetland are seen also seen within these upazilas contributing to regions flood susceptibility. During monsoon season, heavy rainfall and overflow of rivers inundates the surrounding low-lying areas creating flood hazard and have had profound impacts on the village's infrastructure and livelihoods. The flood shelter will be constructed at Solartair Government Primary School (GPS), which is located at the Solartair village under Kutubpur Union of Shariakandi Upazila in Bogura District. There are 07 teachers, and 202 students (Boys: 103; Girls: 99) in the school, operated by the guidance of School Management Committee (SMC) and government officials of Tarash Upazila Education Office. The students, teachers and residents of the catchment area come to the proposed site by using the connecting/access road named Chandonbaisha- Bogura Road. The road is a BC road with 4.57 meters width and just passing beside the Solartair Government Primary School at west side. The population of the catchment area is about 30,000 – 35,000. The Kutubpur Union map indicating sub-project location has been shown respectively in Figure 1. The topographical Map with indicative and tentative location of labor camp, construction materials storage area, and waste disposal area have been shown in Figure 2 which shall be placed as per direction and satisfaction of LGED and E.I.C. Figure 5: Proposed Waste Disposal Area for the Subproject Site The existing Solartair Government Primary School has 81 decimals of land comprises a one- storied school building that currently accommodates all classrooms and administrative offices. The proposed flood shelter is planned to be constructed on the west side of the school premises, with no demolition of the existing building required. Accordingly, all academic and administrative activities will continue to be conducted within the current school building throughout the construction period. Community members residing adjacent to the school have emphasized the importance of ensuring uninterrupted class operations to maintain continuity in students’ education. (Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, July 2025) The proposed sub-project (construction of new School cum Flood shelter building) is not located within any environmentally sensitive area and will not cause any severe negative effects to the environmental settings of the area, neither to important environmental features. The disaster shelter will be constructed within an existing school boundary, so no agricultural land/ activities or fish farming will be disturbed due to the construction of the sub project. There are found some socio-environmental features such as Soalraid Akondopara Mosque (500m), Solaraid Community Clinic (500m), Solaraid Kashipur School Dakhil Madrasa (1km), Solaraid Khal (450m) on the North side of the proposed sub-project location. To the south, Solaraid Eidgah Field (1km), Solaraid Kawmi Hafezia Madrasa (800m), Soalraid Shahi Mosque (500m), Chandan Baisha Degree College (1km) are found on from the sub-project component. Solaraid Purbopara Mosque (500m), Manas Bil (1km), Chandan Baisha Police Tadando Kendro (950m) found on the East side from the sub-project component. Some important socio-environmental features such as Bashhata GPS (1km), Bangali River (1km) located on West side from the sub-project location. No significant disturbance to all these establishments/features is anticipated due to construction activities for having sufficient distance from the construction site, and strict construction site management system- including restrictive work schedule during the daytime only, water- sprinkling twice a day in and around the site, proper fencing around the working area, safe storage of materials, etc. Construction related activities and setting up of labor camps along with associated facilities and their management issues will be accounted for impacts more likely to be generated during the pre, post and construction period. Noise pollution from pilling or drilling, air pollution caused by dust or gaseous emissions from vehicle movement, running of motorized equipment and land clearing, odors and soil pollution from leaking of latrines and fecal sludge, will more likely to take place. Soil can further be eroded and polluted from chemical spills or improper disposal of waste materials. Noise and vibration effects generated from pilling and drilling may also trigger landslides and harmful disturbances to local fauna. Impact on surface and ground water bodies might get acute due mainly to the high abstraction rate and disposal/leakage of pollutants to the surface/ground water bodies. Clearing of trees, bushes or any type of vegetation may put impact on floral species and unscrupulous clearance also trigger habitat loss. All these impacts can only be prevented or minimized by adopting measures delineated into the ESMP and good practice engineering and site management. ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SCREENING This section identifies the potential impacts that the various elements of the proposed sub- project may have on the physical, biological and socio-economic environment within half a kilometer of the radial distance around the site. Environmental and Social Assessment (ESA) based on this screening study for the Sub-project as Solartair Government Primary School of Shariakandi Upazila under Bogura District has been conducted to identify and determine which potential project impacts may be significant and therefore require the application of reasonable and effective management and/or mitigation measures. In order to realize the exact physical, [SOURCE: Page_435]

Page | 393 [SOURCE: Page_435]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_436]

biological and socio-economic environment of the proposed sub-project site and the influence area in regards to the implementation measures, an extensive field visit was carried out on 02 July 2025 in the Sub-project area. Environmental and Social Screening form, as adopted in Annexure-2 of the Environmental and Social Management Framework of RIVER, was administered for identifying the impacts and their extents. [SOURCE: Page_436]

PUBLIC CONSULTATION AND PARTICIPATION Public participation and community consultation has been taken up as an integral part of environmental assessment process of the project. Field visit has been carried out on 02 July 2025 in and around the Sub-project component site. As part of the impact assessment, participatory public consultation was conducted in that area by the field level staffs, and consultants from D&SC. Checklist of the consultation is attached in Annexure-3. The consultation meeting was attended by 26 persons (Male -8 and Female -18) and local individuals, teachers, chairman and/or member of Union Parishad and school management committee were among the attendees in that meeting. The participants were selected from different cohorts of stakeholders, and some of whom will have major active roles before, during and even after the construction works. Therefore, the meeting was organized in an informed, expressive and unbiased manner, wherefrom different views and concerns came across which will be properly taken care of during the design and construction phases. Refer to Figure 8 and Annexure-4 for selected photographs of the participatory public consultation held at site of the Solartair Government Primary School and list of attendees in that public consultation meeting, respectively. A questionnaire was kept ready and responses were elicited. During these consultations, the communities were explained about the project, its benefits, associated social and environmental aspects and possible mitigation measures. The participants were also informed about the project GRM (Grievance Redress Mechanism) system in detail and the disclosure of project documents in websites, and their unrestricted and uninitiated access to those system and resources. As such, public consultation is a living process as the types of problems/ difficulties, involved parties or stakeholders and mode of settlement or resolution processes are more likely to differ with time. Thus, consultation with different parties or stakeholders will be continued throughout the sub-project implementation period and records of resolutions, whatsoever and wherever possible, will be kept in writing at the site and made available on any enquiries or requests by all parties concerned. [SOURCE: Page_436]

Page | 394 [SOURCE: Page_436]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_437]

Figure 8: Public Consultation Meeting in the Proposed Sub-project Site [SOURCE: Page_437]

SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACTS Overall Construction Related Impacts: The proposed construction works are expected to generate localized and temporary environmental and social impacts typical of small- to medium- scale civil works. Key environmental impacts include dust and air emissions, noise and vibration from machinery, construction waste generation, temporary soil disturbance, and minor vegetation loss during site preparation. There may also be risks of water and soil contamination from improper material handling or drainage obstruction. Social impacts are anticipated to be limited, involving temporary disruption of school activities, restricted access to playgrounds, increased traffic movement, and potential occupational health and safety risks for workers. However, no land acquisition, displacement, or impacts on ethnic or vulnerable communities are expected. Overall, the impacts are short-term, reversible, and confined within existing school premises, manageable through standard environmental and social mitigation practices. Environmental Impacts: No trees are likely to be cut down and no water bodies are likely to be filled up due to the construction of the flood shelter. The ecological impact of the subproject is low. There will be temporary negative impacts on physic-chemical environment. Nevertheless, these impacts are manageable if mitigation measures are taken according to ESMP. Grass turfing: Grass turfs on embankment, slope, building compound & any critical place to enhance the ecological condition and protect the top soil. Tentative area of turf has been estimated as 240 square meters (half of total area), after discussion with architects and engineers. It is likely to be changed depending on the requirement during construction as per site design and as per direction of E.I.C. Land Ownership: Availability of adequate public land area is as important as community consent to construct the flood shelter and access roads. The D&S Survey team did not find any conflicts over the school land. The land issue has been discussed in the meeting. Participants unanimously confirmed that the school has its own 81 decimals of land and there is no dispute about this land. Land Acquisition: The proposed Sub-project, Solartair Government Primary School, does not have any involuntary resettlement impacts due to the construction of flood shelter and approach roads as the Sub-projects will be constructed in existing Government Primary Schools’ Page | 395 [SOURCE: Page_437]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_438]

premises. The Government Primary School has 81 decimals of land. No land acquisition will be required for the activities to be implemented under the project. Access road needs to construct or rehabilitate within its existing alignment. Considering the impacts identified at this particular school site, the site-specific Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) may be outlined as follows: [SOURCE: Page_438]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_450]

LOCATION OF THE SUB-PROJECT The subproject is located in the Northern part of Shariakandi Upazila in Bogura District, which is within the Rajshahi Division. The location details of the subproject have been summarized in Table 2. Table 2: Location Details of the Subproject Site District                                          :    Bogura Upazila                                           :    Shariakandi Union                                             :    Narchi Mouza                                             :    Banchgari Village                                           :    Banchgari GPS Location                                      :    24.812314 N; 89.575549 E Distance of the site from Upazila HQ              :    5 km Nearby Major Road:                                :    Shariakandi-Bogura Road Nearby River/ Canal:                              :    Echamati River (West side-1 km), Bangali River (East side -1km) [SOURCE: Page_450]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, July 2025) The catchment area of the subproject mostly comprises of Banchgari, Putiar Ghon, Jat Holida, Shekhahati, Chittor para, Ganok para, Neurghacha, Narchi, Godagari villages which have been significantly affected by floods. The floods in Shariakandi Upazila are mainly caused by the natural behavior of the Jamuna. Presence of Cholon Beel and smaller wetland are seen also seen within these upazilas contributing to regions flood susceptibility. During monsoon season, heavy rainfall and overflow of rivers inundates the surrounding low-lying areas creating flood hazard and have had profound impacts on the village's infrastructure and livelihoods. The flood shelter will be constructed at Banchgari Government Primary School (GPS), which is located at the Banchgari village under Narchi Union of Shariakandi Upazila in Bogura District. There are 07 teachers, and 150 students (Boys: 73; Girls: 80) in the school, operated by the guidance of School Management Committee (SMC) and government officials of Tarash Upazila Education Office. The students, teachers and residents of the catchment area come to the proposed site by using the connecting/access road named Shariakandi-Bogura Road. The road is a BC road with 4.57 meters width and just passing beside the Banchgari Government Primary School at south side. The population of the catchment area is about 20,000 – 22,000. The Narchi Union map indicating sub-project location has been shown respectively in Figure 1. The topographical Map with indicative and tentative location of labor camp, construction materials storage area, and waste disposal area have been shown in Figure 2 which shall be placed as per direction and satisfaction of LGED and E.I.C. Direction                      Important Establishments with Approximate Distance North side     Putiar Jame Mosque (300m), Tiorpara Mosque (500m), Tiorpara Community Clinic (500m), Gonakpara Mosque (1km), South side     Bashgari Dakkhin Para Mosque (500m), Ruier Beel (500m), Bashgari Mosque (800m) East side      Neorgacha Mosque (500m), Sardarpara Mosque (700m), Narchibazar Central Mosque (1km), Bangali River (1km), Garibunnecha Kawmi Madrasa (1km), Narchibazar (1km) West side      Putiarghon Dakkhin Para Mosque (200m), Jathalda Mosque (700m), Ichamati (1km) (Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, July 2025) The proposed sub-project (construction of new School cum Flood shelter building) is not located within any environmentally sensitive area and will not cause any severe negative effects to the environmental settings of the area, neither to important environmental features. The disaster shelter will be constructed within an existing school boundary, so no agricultural land/ activities or fish farming will be disturbed due to the construction of the sub project. There are found some socio-environmental features such as Putiar Jame Mosque (300m), Tiorpara Mosque (500m), Gonakpara Mosque (1km), Tiorpara Community Clinic (500m) on the North side of the proposed sub-project location. To the south, Bashgari Mosque (800m), Bashgari Dakkhin Para Mosque (500m), Ruier Bil (500m) are found on from the sub-project component. Neorgacha Mosque (500m), Sardarpara Mosque (700m), Narchibazar Central Mosque (1km), Bangali River (1km), Garibunnecha Kawmi Madrasa (1km), Narchibazar (1km) found on the East side from the sub-project component. Some important socio-environmental features such as Putiarghon Dakkhin Para Mosque (200m), Jathalda Mosque (700m), Ichamati (1km) located on West side from the sub-project location. No significant disturbance to all these establishments/features is anticipated due to construction activities for having sufficient distance from the construction site, and strict construction site management system- including restrictive work schedule during the daytime only, water- sprinkling twice a day in and around the site, proper fencing around the working area, safe storage of materials, etc. Construction related activities and setting up of labor camps along with associated facilities and their management issues will be accounted for impacts more likely to be generated during the pre, post and construction period. Noise pollution from pilling or drilling, air pollution caused by dust or gaseous emissions from vehicle movement, running of motorized equipment and land clearing, odors and soil pollution from leaking of latrines and fecal sludge, will more likely to take [SOURCE: Page_454]

place. Soil can further be eroded and polluted from chemical spills or improper disposal of waste materials. Noise and vibration effects generated from pilling and drilling may also trigger landslides and harmful disturbances to local fauna. Impact on surface and ground water bodies might get acute due mainly to the high abstraction rate and disposal/leakage of pollutants to the surface/ground water bodies. Clearing of trees, bushes or any type of vegetation may put impact on floral species and unscrupulous clearance also trigger habitat loss. All these impacts can only be prevented or minimized by adopting measures delineated into the ESMP and good practice engineering and site management. [SOURCE: Page_455]

ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SCREENING This section identifies the potential impacts that the various elements of the proposed sub- project may have on the physical, biological and socio-economic environment within half a kilometer of the radial distance around the site. Environmental and Social Assessment (ESA) based on this screening study for the Sub-project as Banchgari Government Primary School of Shariakandi Upazila under Bogura District has been conducted to identify and determine which potential project impacts may be significant and therefore require the application of reasonable and effective management and/or mitigation measures. In order to realize the exact physical, biological and socio-economic environment of the proposed sub-project site and the influence area in regards to the implementation measures, an extensive field visit was carried out on 03 July 2025 in the Sub-project area. Environmental and Social Screening form, as adopted in Annexure-2 of the Environmental and Social Management Framework of RIVER, was administered for identifying the impacts and their extents. [SOURCE: Page_455]

PUBLIC CONSULTATION AND PARTICIPATION Public participation and community consultation has been taken up as an integral part of environmental assessment process of the project. Field visit has been carried out on 03 July 2025 in and around the Sub-project component site. As part of the impact assessment, participatory public consultation was conducted in that area by the field level staffs, and consultants from D&SC. Checklist of the consultation is attached in Annexure-3. The consultation meeting was attended by 40 persons (Male -10 and Female -30) and local individuals, teachers, chairman and/or member of Union Parishad and school management committee were among the attendees in that meeting. The participants were selected from different cohorts of stakeholders, and some of whom will have major active roles before, during and even after the construction works. Therefore, the meeting was organized in an informed, expressive and unbiased manner, wherefrom different views and concerns came across which will be properly taken care of during the design and construction phases. Refer to Figure 8 and Annexure-4 for selected photographs of the participatory public consultation held at site of the Banchgari Government Primary School and list of attendees in that public consultation meeting, respectively. A questionnaire was kept ready and responses were elicited. During these consultations, the communities were explained about the project, its benefits, associated social and environmental aspects and possible mitigation measures. [SOURCE: Page_455]

Page | 413 [SOURCE: Page_455]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_456]

The participants were also informed about the project GRM (Grievance Redress Mechanism) system in detail and the disclosure of project documents in websites, and their unrestricted and uninitiated access to those system and resources. As such, public consultation is a living process as the types of problems/ difficulties, involved parties or stakeholders and mode of settlement or resolution processes are more likely to differ with time. Thus, consultation with different parties or stakeholders will be continued throughout the sub-project implementation period and records of resolutions, whatsoever and wherever possible, will be kept in writing at the site and made available on any enquiries or requests by all parties concerned. [SOURCE: Page_456]

SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACTS Overall Construction Related Impacts: The proposed construction works are expected to generate localized and temporary environmental and social impacts typical of small- to medium- scale civil works. Key environmental impacts include dust and air emissions, noise and vibration from machinery, construction waste generation, temporary soil disturbance, and minor vegetation loss during site preparation. There may also be risks of water and soil contamination from improper material handling or drainage obstruction. Social impacts are anticipated to be limited, involving temporary disruption of school activities, restricted access to playgrounds, increased traffic movement, and potential occupational health and safety risks for workers. However, no land acquisition, displacement, or impacts on ethnic or vulnerable communities are expected. Overall, the impacts are short-term, reversible, and confined within existing school premises, manageable through standard environmental and social mitigation practices. Tree cutting: Approximately 5 trees are likely to be cut down and no water bodies are likely to be filled up due to the construction of the flood shelter. The ecological impact of the subproject is low. There will be temporary negative impacts on physic-chemical environment. Nevertheless, these impacts are manageable if mitigation measures are taken according to ESMP. Grass turfing: Grass turfs on embankment, slope, building compound & any critical place to enhance the ecological condition and protect the top soil. Tentative area of turf has been estimated as 240 square meters (half of total area), after discussion with architects and engineers. It is likely to be changed depending on the requirement during construction as per site design and as per direction of E.I.C. Land Ownership: Availability of adequate public land area is as important as community consent Page | 414 [SOURCE: Page_456]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_457]

to construct the flood shelter and access roads. The D&S Survey team did not find any conflicts over the school land. The land issue has been discussed in the meeting. Participants unanimously confirmed that the school has its own 54 decimals of land and there is no dispute about this land. Land Acquisition: The proposed Sub-project, Banchgari Government Primary School, does not have any involuntary resettlement impacts due to the construction of flood shelter and approach roads as the Sub-projects will be constructed in existing Government Primary Schools’ premises. The Government Primary School has 54 decimals of land. No land acquisition will be required for the activities to be implemented under the project. Access road needs to construct or rehabilitate within its existing alignment. LOCATION OF THE SUB-PROJECT The subproject is located in the Northern part of Shariakandi Upazila in Bogura District, which is within the Rajshahi Division. The location details of the subproject have been summarized in Table 2. Table 2: Location Details of the Subproject Site District                                          :    Bogura Upazila                                           :    Shariakandi Union                                             :    Shariakandi Mouza                                             :    Dakshin Dighalkandi Village                                           :    Dighalkandi GPS Location                                      :    24.875228 N; 89.572255 E Distance of the site from Upazila HQ              :    3 km Nearby Major Road:                                :    Dighalkandi-Shariakandi Road Nearby River/ Canal:                              :    Jamuna River (East side -500 m) [SOURCE: Page_470]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, July 2025) The catchment area of the subproject mostly comprises of Dighalkandi villages which have been significantly affected by floods. The floods in Shariakandi Upazila are mainly caused by the natural behavior of the Jamuna. Presence of Cholon Beel and smaller wetland are seen also seen within these upazilas contributing to regions flood susceptibility. During monsoon season, heavy rainfall and overflow of rivers inundates the surrounding low-lying areas creating flood hazard and have had profound impacts on the village's infrastructure and livelihoods. The flood shelter will be constructed at Dighalkandi Government Primary School (GPS), which is located at the Dighalkandi village under Shariakandi Union of Shariakandi Upazila in Bogura District. There are 09 teachers, and 214 students (Boys: 106; Girls: 108) in the school, operated by the guidance of School Management Committee (SMC) and government officials of Tarash Upazila Education Office. The students, teachers and residents of the catchment area come to the proposed site by using the connecting/access road named Dighalkandi-Shariakandi Road. The road is a BC road with 4.57 meters width and just passing beside the Dighalkandi Government Primary School at South side. The population of the catchment area is about 18,000 – 20,000. The Shariakandi Union map indicating sub-project location has been shown respectively in Figure 1. The topographical Map with indicative and tentative location of labor camp, construction materials storage area, and waste disposal area have been shown in Figure 2 which shall be placed as per direction and satisfaction of LGED and E.I.C. [SOURCE: Page_470]

Figure 5: Proposed Waste Disposal Area for the Subproject Site The existing Dighalkandi Government Primary School has 74 decimals of land comprises a one- storied school building that currently accommodates all classrooms and administrative offices and an old tin shed building. The proposed flood shelter is planned to be constructed in the school premises by demolishing the old tin shed building. All academic and administrative activities will continue to be conducted within the current school building throughout the construction period. Community members residing adjacent to the school have emphasized the importance of ensuring uninterrupted class operations to maintain continuity in students’ education. Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_474]

(Source: Field survey and Public Consultation Meeting, July 2025) The proposed sub-project (construction of new School cum Flood shelter building) is not located within any environmentally sensitive area and will not cause any severe negative effects to the environmental settings of the area, neither to important environmental features. The disaster shelter will be constructed within an existing school boundary, so no agricultural land/ activities or fish farming will be disturbed due to the construction of the sub project. There are found some socio-environmental features such as Deluabari GPS (500m), Daruna GPS (1km), Digholkandi uttar Para Mosque (600m), Beribadh (700m), Eidgah Math (1km) on the North side of the proposed sub-project location. To the south, Digholkandi Moddhopara Mosque (200m), Digholkandi Dakkhin Para Mosque (600m), Digholkandi Community Clinic (150m), Pond (650m), Molar Bil (1km) are found on from the sub-project component. Digholkandi Purbopara Mosque (800m), Digholkandi Jomunar Ghat (1km) found on the East side from the sub-project component. Some important socio-environmental features such as Tarafdarpara Mosque (500m), Eitvabi (500m), Pond (800m) located on West side from the sub-project location. No significant disturbance to all these establishments/features is anticipated due to construction activities for having sufficient distance from the construction site, and strict construction site management system- including restrictive work schedule during the daytime only, water- sprinkling twice a day in and around the site, proper fencing around the working area, safe storage of materials, etc. Construction related activities and setting up of labor camps along with associated facilities and their management issues will be accounted for impacts more likely to be generated during the pre, post and construction period. Noise pollution from pilling or drilling, air pollution caused by dust or gaseous emissions from vehicle movement, running of motorized equipment and land clearing, odors and soil pollution from leaking of latrines and fecal sludge, will more likely to take place. Soil can further be eroded and polluted from chemical spills or improper disposal of waste materials. Noise and vibration effects generated from pilling and drilling may also trigger landslides and harmful disturbances to local fauna. Impact on surface and ground water bodies might get acute due mainly to the high abstraction rate and disposal/leakage of pollutants to the surface/ground water bodies. Clearing of trees, bushes or any type of vegetation may put impact on floral species and unscrupulous clearance also trigger habitat loss. All these impacts can only be prevented or minimized by adopting measures delineated into the ESMP and good practice engineering and site management. [SOURCE: Page_474]

ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SCREENING This section identifies the potential impacts that the various elements of the proposed sub- project may have on the physical, biological and socio-economic environment within half a kilometer of the radial distance around the site. Environmental and Social Assessment (ESA) based on this screening study for the Sub-project as Dighalkandi Government Primary School of Shariakandi Upazila under Bogura District has been conducted to identify and determine which potential project impacts may be significant and therefore require the application of reasonable [SOURCE: Page_474]

Page | 432 [SOURCE: Page_474]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_475]

and effective management and/or mitigation measures. In order to realize the exact physical, biological and socio-economic environment of the proposed sub-project site and the influence area in regards to the implementation measures, an extensive field visit was carried out on 01 July 2025 in the Sub-project area. Environmental and Social Screening form, as adopted in Annexure-2 of the Environmental and Social Management Framework of RIVER, was administered for identifying the impacts and their extents. [SOURCE: Page_475]

PUBLIC CONSULTATION AND PARTICIPATION Public participation and community consultation has been taken up as an integral part of environmental assessment process of the project. Field visit has been carried out on 01 July 2025 in and around the Sub-project component site. As part of the impact assessment, participatory public consultation was conducted in that area by the field level staffs, and consultants from D&SC. Checklist of the consultation is attached in Annexure-3. The consultation meeting was attended by 34 persons (Male -17 and Female -17) and local individuals, teachers, chairman and/or member of Union Parishad and school management committee were among the attendees in that meeting. The participants were selected from different cohorts of stakeholders, and some of whom will have major active roles before, during and even after the construction works. Therefore, the meeting was organized in an informed, expressive and unbiased manner, wherefrom different views and concerns came across which will be properly taken care of during the design and construction phases. Refer to Figure 8 and Annexure-4 for selected photographs of the participatory public consultation held at site of the Dighalkandi Government Primary School and list of attendees in that public consultation meeting, respectively. A questionnaire was kept ready and responses were elicited. During these consultations, the communities were explained about the project, its benefits, associated social and environmental aspects and possible mitigation measures. The participants were also informed about the project GRM (Grievance Redress Mechanism) system in detail and the disclosure of project documents in websites, and their unrestricted and uninitiated access to those system and resources. As such, public consultation is a living process as the types of problems/ difficulties, involved parties or stakeholders and mode of settlement or resolution processes are more likely to differ with time. Thus, consultation with different parties or stakeholders will be continued throughout the sub-project implementation period and records of resolutions, whatsoever and wherever possible, will be kept in writing at the site and made available on any enquiries or requests by all parties concerned. [SOURCE: Page_475]

SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACTS Overall Construction Related Impacts: The proposed construction works are expected to generate localized and temporary environmental and social impacts typical of small- to medium- scale civil works. Key environmental impacts include dust and air emissions, noise and vibration from machinery, construction waste generation, temporary soil disturbance, and minor vegetation loss during site preparation. There may also be risks of water and soil contamination from improper material handling or drainage obstruction. Social impacts are anticipated to be limited, involving temporary disruption of school activities, restricted access to playgrounds, increased traffic movement, and potential occupational health and safety risks for workers. However, no land acquisition, displacement, or impacts on ethnic or vulnerable communities are expected. Overall, the impacts are short-term, reversible, and confined within existing school premises, manageable through standard environmental and social mitigation practices. Tree Cutting: Approximately 12 trees (medium to large size) are likely to be cut down and no water bodies are likely to be filled up due to the construction of the flood shelter. The ecological impact of the subproject is low. There will be temporary negative impacts on physic-chemical environment. Nevertheless, these impacts are manageable if mitigation measures are taken according to ESMP. Grass turfing: Grass turfs on embankment, slope, building compound & any critical place to enhance the ecological condition and protect the top soil. Tentative area of turf has been estimated as 240 square meters (half of total area), after discussion with architects and engineers. It is likely to be changed depending on the requirement during construction as per site design and as per direction of E.I.C. Land Ownership: Availability of adequate public land area is as important as community consent to construct the flood shelter and access roads. The D&S Survey team did not find any conflicts over the school land. The land issue has been discussed in the meeting. Participants unanimously confirmed that the school has its own 74 decimals of land and there is no dispute about this land. Land Acquisition: The proposed Sub-project, Dighalkandi Government Primary School, does not have any involuntary resettlement impacts due to the construction of flood shelter and approach roads as the Sub-projects will be constructed in existing Government Primary Schools’ Page | 434 [SOURCE: Page_476]

Resilient Infrastructure for Adaptation and Vulnerability Reduction (RIVER) Project Environmental & Social Screening Report for Bogura District [SOURCE: Page_477]

premises. The Government Primary School has 74 decimals of land. No land acquisition will be required for the activities to be implemented under the project. Access road needs to construct or rehabilitate within its existing alignment. ### 1. Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for Demolition works at Site 1.0 PURPOSE

The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to establish safe, efficient, standardized and environmentally responsible methods for carrying out building demolition works at construction sites. The SOP aims to minimize risks to workers, the public, adjacent structures, and the environment while ensuring compliance with applicable laws, standards, and contract requirements. [SOURCE: Page_570]

---

[CHUNK_METADATA]

- Parent_Topic: D40075603

- Summary: Section focusing on 2.0 scope

- Key_Entities: Agriculture, Irrigation Research

- Confidence_Score: High

---

## 2.0 SCOPE

Since the demolition works fall under the responsibility of the Directorate of Primary Education (DPE), the Upazila Education Officer, on behalf of the DPE, is tasked with inviting tenders for the demolition works through a third-party contractor. However, the RIVER Project authority, under the supervision of the local LGED and project staff, will maintain additional oversight to ensure that no injuries, fatalities, or other accidents occur at the demolition sites. Accordingly, the project authority will provide guidance and recommendations to the demolition contractor on the following matters: [SOURCE: Page_570]

   Site preparation and safety measures    Demolition execution    Waste management and disposal    Post-demolition site clearance and inspection [SOURCE: Page_570]

## 3.0 PROCEDURE

3.1 Pre-Demolition Planning & Engineering Survey [SOURCE: Page_570]

1. Appoint a Competent Person: A designated, experienced person (e.g., Project Manager or Demolition Specialist) must be appointed to plan, supervise, and direct the demolition. 2. Engineering Survey: A detailed survey must be conducted by a Structural Engineer. The report shall include:  The structure's design and construction method.  The condition of the structure, identifying any signs of weakness or damage.  The presence of pre-stressed or post-tensioned concrete members. 3. Hazardous Materials Survey: A pre-demolition audit must be conducted to identify and manage hazardous materials such as:  Asbestos Containing Materials (ACM)  Lead-based paints  PCBs (in electrical equipment)  Chemical or biological waste  Underground/overhead services (gas, water, electricity, telecom) Page | 528 [SOURCE: Page_570]
